journeys.name: Explicit commercial decline → reason → terminal, cooldown or recycle
journeys.purpose: Route a negative commercial outcome by its cause rather than filing every one of them under lost.

entity.scope: lead, opportunity or account
entity.note: The decline belongs to the opportunity it was given about. A different opportunity with the same account is not declined by it.

distinctFrom.because: Someone decided something here. Where the recorded reason turns out to be silence rather than a decision, this journey hands it to decay instead of treating it as one.

journeys.objective: Route a negative commercial outcome by its cause rather than filing every one of them under lost.
eligibility: a decline stated by the person or account, or a lost outcome recorded in the system of record
no instance of this journey is already open for the lead
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: The lost reason history is preserved. Routing depends on it, so overwriting it destroys the ability to route at all.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Not now is not never. Only a terminal reason ends acquisition permanently.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A declined opportunity is not swept into generic marketing as a consolation.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Where no re-entry condition was recorded, none is invented. The absence of a date is not an invitation to pick one.

guardrails: state_written_on_stale_entity

useCases: a declined opportunity whose reason says when to try again
a loss for silence routed to intent decay rather than filed as lost

insufficientAlone: silence
a missed meeting
an unanswered email

nodes.does: Capture the reason against the opportunity and append it to the decline history, leaving earlier reasons readable - a second loss for a different reason is two facts, not a correction of the first

nodes.asks: Which reason family applies?

branches.label: NOT_FIT

branches.label: TIMING
branches.when: right fit, wrong moment

branches.label: NO_PRIORITY
branches.when: real fit, no current mandate to act

branches.label: PROCUREMENT_BLOCK
branches.when: a process or policy obstacle rather than a judgement about us

branches.label: PRICE
branches.when: the value case did not clear the price at this moment

branches.label: COMPETITOR
branches.when: another supplier was chosen, which has a term and therefore an end

branches.label: NO_RESPONSE
branches.when: the opportunity was closed for silence, which nobody actually decided

branches.label: OTHER
branches.when: the reason is unclassified and cannot be routed as recorded

nodes.state: declined, terminal mismatch
nodes.reEntry: none from this reason - what would have to change is what we sell, not what this account decided

nodes.on: an opportunity closed for silence rather than for a decision
carries: the fact that no decision was made, so nothing downstream reads this as a refusal
the intent history, which is now the stale evidence decay is about

nodes.on: a decline recorded as OTHER

suppresses: automatic re-entry until the reason is classified

branches.label: Not known
branches.when: the reason is temporary but nothing was recorded that would say when to return

after.rule: The re-entry wait ends at the event, date or condition recorded alongside the reason; nothing is scheduled where none is known.

nodes.recheck: the lead re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

nodes.on: the recorded re-entry condition being met
carries: the decline history, so the new attempt starts knowing what was said before
the condition that was met

nodes.state: declined, recycle-eligible, nothing scheduled
nodes.reEntry: a new inbound signal, or a re-entry condition recorded later; no cadence is invented to fill the silence

guardrails: The lost reason history is preserved. Routing depends on it, so overwriting it destroys the ability to route at all.

A declined opportunity is not swept into generic marketing as a consolation.

journeys.name: Captured interest → readiness check → destination-appropriate first touch
journeys.purpose: Answer a declared interest with the thing that interest actually asked for, and carry it onward only as far as what the person said about themselves justifies.

entity.scope: the individual capture and what it asked for, resolved onto a person
entity.note: One capture, one destination. A second, different request from the same person is its own instance and is not considered answered by what the first one produced.

distinctFrom.because: ACQ-02 decides which destination a capture justifies and records that decision with its own state. This journey is what the person receives once that decision exists, and it invents no destination of its own.

journeys.objective: Answer a declared interest with the thing that interest actually asked for, and carry it onward only as far as what the person said about themselves justifies.
eligibility: a first-party capture recorded with the context the person declared
a contact point the person gave in that capture
the permission position recorded as its own fact, separate from the submission
no instance of this journey is already open for the the individual capture and what it asked for
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE

the permission position recorded as its own fact, separate from the submission

journeys.name: Process started → abandonment confirmed → recovered, superseded or lapsed
journeys.purpose: Return a person to a resumable process they started and did not complete - a checkout, an application, a quote, a registration - while it is still resumable, without ever asserting a state the system does not hold.
journeys.objective: Bring the person back to the specific unfinished process and let them complete it; never claim reserved stock, a held price or a discount the system does not assert.

entity.scope: the logical process - the basket-and-checkout, application, quote or registration the person is trying to complete - not the platform's identifier for it
entity.note: One instance per logical process. A platform that rotates its process id when the same basket resumes still has one process, and the company's mapping resolves the new id to the open instance rather than opening a second. Two different baskets are two processes; whether they may both be pursued is the supersession statement below.

supersession.label: RECOMMENDED_DEFAULT
supersession.text: A new logical process for the same person supersedes an open instance - two recovery sequences to one person about two baskets is the duplicate-communication failure. A company whose processes are genuinely independent (a marketplace, a B2B account with separate buyers) sets concurrency to many and lets the person-level pressure cap protect the person.

eligibility: the identity behind the process resolves to a person we may contact
the process is still resumable in the system of record, with at least one item and a resume destination
no recovery instance is already open for this logical process
no payment failure is recorded on the process - a failed payment is FIN-134's, not abandonment
purpose-level permission for commercial recovery communication is recorded, and hard gates (GLB-31) allow it

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Exit the moment the process completes by any channel - in the product, in a store, by phone. A recovery message about a completed process is the failure this journey exists to prevent, and every touch re-reads the process first.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Exit when the process is cancelled by the person, expired by the platform, or emptied. Nothing is sent about a process the person cannot return to.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A payment failure on the process hands the instance to payment failure recovery (FIN-134). The two never message the same person about the same process.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: No touch without purpose-level permission for commercial recovery communication; absent permission is a recorded no-action, never a fallback to another channel.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: An open retention-outreach journey, an open complaint or an open payment recovery on the same account outranks this journey; its touch is deferred and re-evaluated against current state, not queued blindly (GLB-06).

suppressions.label: RECOMMENDED_DEFAULT
suppressions.text: A newer logical process for the same person supersedes this instance (see the entity's supersession statement).

suppressions.label: RECOMMENDED_DEFAULT
suppressions.text: A new process opened inside the cooldown after a lapsed or suppressed instance enters, is tracked, and sends nothing.

suppressions.label: OPTIONAL_STRATEGY
suppressions.text: If the company enables an incentive (recovery.incentive_policy), it appears only on the last enabled touch, once, and its issuance is recorded per person so it cannot be re-issued on the next process. The library recommends none by default: an incentive on the first touch teaches abandonment.

value.rule: Every touch runs against a budget fixed when the instance opened; the budget is the plan's own length, and no touch is repeated because nothing could tell whether it arrived.

default.applicableWhen: GLB-24; two touches when the final notice is disabled

cooldown.rule: After a lapsed or suppressed instance, a new process by the same person is tracked but not messaged until the cooldown has passed. A completed process carries no cooldown.

default.applicableWhen: repeat abandoners on considered purchases
default.avoidWhen: high-frequency replenishment purchases, where a short cooldown is honest

competition.precedence: highest in the group - a process in motion outranks a held selection, an inferred interest or a predicted need for the same person

roles.when: an app session or a valid push token exists for this person - the intent is minutes old and a nudge back beats content
no low-friction route exists, or the touch has to carry the items and survive until the person can act
explicit commercial SMS permission exists and the process carries an asserted time-bound element - an expiry, a hold, a delivery cut-off

touches.purpose: The process is still open; here are the items; here is the link that reopens this exact process with its state restored. Nothing the system does not assert.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: Address the likely blocker - shipping, returns, trust, a route to ask a question - with the same link. Still nothing the system does not assert.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: The last honest statement: the process closes at its real expiry, and here is the link. No urgency the system does not assert.

mustNotClaim: an expiry the platform does not enforce

touches.label: OPTIONAL_STRATEGY

requires: an authoritative record that a resumable process opened for this person
at least one item in the process
a resumable state and a resume destination
the time of the last activity on the process
insufficientAlone: a cart page view
an item added without entering the process - that is a recorded selection, Abandoned Selection Recovery's subject
a process with no items
a process already completed, cancelled or expired

nodes.asks: Can this process be recovered for this person at all?

branches.label: Eligible
branches.when: the identity resolves to a contactable person, the process is resumable with items and a destination, no instance is open for it, no payment failure is recorded on it, and commercial recovery permission is recorded
branches.observes: process state, identity resolution, permission record

branches.label: Not eligible
branches.when: any of those fails - the reason is recorded as the no-action reason
branches.observes: process state, identity resolution, permission record

nodes.does: Open the recovery instance against the logical process and start the abandonment clock from the last activity on it, not from when it opened. Activity before the first touch moves the clock; nothing after the first touch extends any window

after.rule: The first check waits long enough after the last activity that the person has actually left the process rather than paused inside it, and no longer than the intent stays fresh.

default.applicableWhen: considered purchases and multi-step applications
default.avoidWhen: impulse baskets and single-step processes, where a shorter first check is honest

timeout.reason: a person still inside the process is not abandoning it; the clock runs from their last activity so that pausing is not punished

nodes.recheck: the process re-read from the system of record: still resumable, items still present, no order placed, no payment failure

nodes.asks: What is the process now?

branches.label: Still resumable
branches.when: the process is open with items and a resume destination and no order has been placed against it

branches.label: Completed
branches.when: an order or completion is recorded against the process by any channel

branches.label: Cancelled, expired or emptied
branches.when: the person cancelled it, the platform expired it, or every item was removed

branches.label: Superseded
branches.when: a newer logical process exists for the same person and the supersession rule applies

branches.label: Payment failed
branches.when: a payment failure is recorded against this process

nodes.asks: May the first touch go out?

branches.label: Sendable
branches.when: the send path passes: permission for commercial recovery, a deliverable destination, the promotional pressure cap, no higher-precedence contest on the account, and no cooldown in force

branches.label: Suppressed
branches.when: a gate stops it; the gate is recorded as the reason

nodes.does: Record which gate stopped the touch and against which process, so no-action is a measured outcome rather than a silent absence

Say the process is still open, show the items as they are now, and give the link that reopens this exact process with its state restored. Claim nothing the system does not assert - no reserved stock, no held price, no discount

after.rule: The second check comes after the person has had a chance to act on the first touch in their own time, and before the process stops being resumable.

default.avoidWhen: perishable or time-boxed processes - the second check is the resumable window minus a margin

timeout.reason: a second touch inside the same hour is pressure, not help; a second touch after the process has expired is noise

nodes.recheck: the process re-read from the system of record, plus whether the person resumed it since the first touch

nodes.asks: What is the process now, and did they come back?

branches.label: Completed
branches.when: an order or completion is recorded against the process

branches.label: Cancelled, expired or emptied
branches.when: the process can no longer be returned to

branches.label: Superseded
branches.when: a newer logical process exists for the same person and the supersession rule applies

branches.label: Payment failed
branches.when: a payment failure is recorded against this process

branches.label: Resumed, still open
branches.when: an authenticated session touched the process since the first touch and it is still open - the person is deciding, not forgetting

branches.label: Still open, not resumed
branches.when: the process is open and untouched since the first touch

nodes.does: Record the return and re-arm one further wait from the new last activity. A person who came back and left again is deciding; the second touch is held once, not skipped and not hurried

attemptBudget.rule: A return re-arms the wait a bounded number of times; the budget is fixed when the instance opens and does not renew on activity.

default.applicableWhen: GLB-24: every retry, reminder and re-request runs against a budget fixed when it started

after.rule: After a return, the same first-check interval runs again from the new last activity.

default.applicableWhen: the same value as the first check

timeout.reason: the person is inside the process again; the same patience applies as before the first touch

nodes.recheck: the process re-read from the system of record

nodes.asks: May the second touch go out?

branches.label: Sendable
branches.when: the send path passes and the touch budget is not spent

branches.label: Suppressed
branches.when: a gate stops it; the gate is recorded

nodes.does: Address the likely blocker - shipping, returns, trust, a route to ask a question - with the same link back into the process. Still nothing the system does not assert

after.rule: The recovery lifetime ends before the platform's own resumable lifetime, so the last touch never points at a process that has already closed.

default.avoidWhen: the platform's resumable lifetime is shorter - the lifetime is that, minus a margin

timeout.reason: an unfinished process stops being an intent and becomes a record; pursuing it past that point is pressure

nodes.recheck: the process re-read from the system of record, and whether the platform asserts an expiry

nodes.asks: At the end of the recovery lifetime, what is the process?

branches.label: Completed
branches.when: an order or completion is recorded against the process

branches.label: Cancelled, expired or emptied
branches.when: the process can no longer be returned to

branches.label: Superseded
branches.when: a newer logical process exists for the same person and the supersession rule applies

branches.label: Payment failed
branches.when: a payment failure is recorded against this process

branches.label: Still open
branches.when: the process is open and resumable

nodes.asks: Is a final notice enabled, and is there a real expiry to name?

branches.label: Enabled, expiry asserted
branches.when: the company has enabled the final notice (recovery.final_notice_enabled), the platform asserts an expiry for this process, and the send path passes

the product's own record of setup milestones is readable
no nurture instance is already open for this onboarding instance
no ACT-14 assisted-help session is open (booked and not yet resolved) for this account
hard gates (GLB-31) permit lifecycle communication

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: No touch without permission for lifecycle communication; absent permission is a recorded no-action.

nodes.does: Read which setup milestones are complete and which remain, from the product's own record of what was done rather than from what was sent or opened

nodes.asks: Is there a critical next step still outstanding?

branches.label: A step remains
branches.when: at least one incomplete milestone stands between this account and value

branches.label: Nothing critical left
branches.when: the setup work is done and what remains is whether value has actually been produced

nodes.does: Surface the single most useful next action. A completed step is never suggested again, and an order is imposed only where one step genuinely depends on another - elsewhere the person picks

attemptBudget.rule: The same budget as the local cap: every prompt spends it, and a spent budget waits out the window silently.

nodes.asks: Has activation actually been achieved?

branches.label: Activated
branches.when: the authoritative activation event has been recorded

branches.label: Setup complete, value not yet produced
branches.when: every milestone is done and no activation event exists - the checklist finished and the product has still not done anything for them

after.rule: The interval between step prompts is the one appropriate to the remaining work - a step that takes minutes and a step that needs an administrator cannot share it.

timeout.reason: the wait is for the person to act; when nothing happens the state is re-read rather than the same message being repeated

nodes.recheck: the milestone record re-read from the product: which steps are complete, whether activation is recorded, whether the window is still open

nodes.asks: Which event arrived?

branches.label: Activation
branches.when: the authoritative activation event was recorded

branches.label: A setup milestone
branches.when: progress was made but value has not been produced yet

nodes.asks: Is the same prerequisite actually blocking activation?

branches.label: A named blocker is holding it
branches.when: authoritative state shows one mandatory prerequisite unchanged and preventing activation, not merely a quiet interval

branches.label: No blocker; simply incomplete
branches.when: setup has not advanced but nothing identifiable is preventing it

nodes.on: one named mandatory prerequisite established as the thing preventing activation, rather than a general lack of progress
carries: the exact outstanding prerequisite and how long it has stayed unchanged
the onboarding route and the milestones already completed
suppresses: the generic next-step prompt for this prerequisite while the blocker journey owns it

nodes.asks: Is the onboarding window still open?

branches.label: Still open
branches.when: the window fixed at entry has not expired

branches.label: Closed
branches.when: the window has expired without activation

nodes.on: the authoritative activation event
carries: which event satisfied activation
what onboarding still had outstanding, so the right things get invalidated rather than all of them

nodes.state: onboarding window closed without activation
nodes.reEntry: a later setup or activation event re-opens this normally; the completed milestones are kept, so a return does not start from the beginning

preemptedBy.event: the authoritative activation event, from anywhere
preemptedBy.then: ACT-16 takes ownership and invalidates whatever this journey still had pending
ACT-13 owns the blocker; generic next-step messaging stops until it is resolved

preemptedBy.event: an assisted setup session scheduled through ACT-14
preemptedBy.then: ACT-14 owns setup communication until the session outcome is recorded; generic next-step prompts pause rather than compete with a booked call

guardrails: A completed step is never suggested again. Reading the setup record rather than the send history is what makes that true.
Step order is enforced only where a real dependency exists. Imposed sequence turns optional work into a blocker.
A finished checklist is not activation. Setup being complete and the product having produced value are two different facts, and this journey can reach the first without the second.
journeys.reusableRule: Onboarding communication should respond to actual progress rather than elapsed time alone.

journeys.name: Missing activation requirement → resolve blocker → resume

entity.scope: the blocking requirement, held against the account or onboarding instance
entity.note: One instance per requirement. Two blockers are two instances, because they may be resolved by different people at different times.

distinctFrom.because: Here the obstacle has a name and resolving it is the whole job. ACT-14 is for the case where nothing specific is missing and the person is still not getting anywhere.

journeys.objective: Aim the whole journey at one named missing thing, and resume onboarding once it exists.
eligibility: a specific unmet requirement: an integration not connected, a required configuration absent, a verification incomplete, a required person not yet present, a mandatory setup step unfinished
no instance of this journey is already open for the the blocking requirement
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE

roles.when: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it
the person is active in the product and the action is taken there
the step is carried out by a person - a call, a task, a visit - and recorded as done by them

touches.purpose: Give the one specific action that clears this requirement, named as the thing it is - never a general prompt to finish setup, which tells someone who is already blocked nothing they did not know

mustNotClaim: that setup in general is unfinished

touches.purpose: Raise the requirement with whoever can actually resolve it, carrying what is blocked and why.

useCases: an integration that must be connected before the product can produce value
a required approval or permission held by someone other than the account

requires: a specific unmet requirement: an integration not connected, a required configuration absent, a verification incomplete, a required person not yet present, a mandatory setup step unfinished

a profile that is not filled in

nodes.does: Identify the exact requirement and what it is blocking, so everything downstream can name it rather than describe setup in general

nodes.asks: Does this requirement actually block activation?

branches.label: Genuinely blocking
branches.when: activation cannot occur while it is unmet

branches.label: Incomplete but not blocking
branches.when: the field or step is missing and value can still be produced without it

nodes.state: not a blocker; ordinary onboarding continues
nodes.reEntry: if the same requirement later becomes mandatory, it enters as a real blocker; presenting it as one now would teach people to ignore the ones that matter

nodes.asks: Can this account resolve the requirement directly?

branches.label: Yes, directly
branches.when: the account holds the access, the information and the permission needed

branches.label: No, it depends on someone else
branches.when: it needs another team, an internal process, a third party, or a person who has not joined yet

nodes.does: Give the one specific action that clears this requirement, named as the thing it is - never a general prompt to finish setup, which tells someone who is already blocked nothing they did not know
Raise the requirement with whoever can actually resolve it, carrying what is blocked and why. Ownership of the resume stays here, so the account is not handed away and forgotten

after.rule: The resolution horizon appropriate to this requirement.

timeout.reason: requirements resolved by third parties and requirements resolved in a settings screen do not deserve the same patience

nodes.recheck: the the blocking requirement re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

nodes.does: Stop every reminder about this requirement immediately, including any already queued - a nudge about something the person has just finished is the clearest possible signal that nothing was watching

nodes.asks: With this requirement met, is activation now reachable?

branches.label: Reachable
branches.when: no other mandatory requirement is outstanding

branches.label: Another requirement is blocking
branches.when: clearing this one revealed a second mandatory requirement

nodes.on: the blocker cleared and activation reachable again
carries: which requirement was resolved and how long it took
the setup state as it now stands, so onboarding resumes rather than restarts

nodes.state: resolved; a further requirement now blocks
nodes.reEntry: the next requirement opens its own instance, named on its own terms - stacking them into one message is how a specific blocker turns back into generic setup pressure

nodes.asks: What does this unresolved requirement warrant?

branches.label: Escalate to a person
branches.when: the requirement matters enough to the outcome that a human should now own it

branches.label: An alternate route exists
branches.when: value can be reached by a different path that does not need this requirement

branches.label: No route
branches.when: the requirement is mandatory and neither resolvable nor avoidable

nodes.on: a blocker outliving its resolution horizon
carries: the requirement, who was asked, and what has already been tried
what activation is waiting on, so the person picking it up starts informed
suppresses: automated reminders about this requirement while a person holds it

nodes.on: an alternate path to value that does not require the blocked thing
carries: the requirement that could not be met
the setup state already reached

nodes.state: activation blocked, no route available
nodes.reEntry: the requirement becoming satisfiable later re-opens this; nothing is repeatedly asked for in the meantime

guardrails: No generic finish-your-setup messaging. The requirement is named, or this journey has nothing to say.
A missing field that does not block activation is not presented as a blocker. Doing so trains people to discount the real ones.
The moment the requirement is met, its reminders stop, including any already scheduled.
journeys.reusableRule: When activation is blocked, orchestration should target the actual dependency rather than increase generic onboarding pressure.

journeys.name: Struggling user detection → proactive assistance → recovery or exit
journeys.purpose: Offer help to someone who is visibly trying and not getting anywhere, and stop asking once they have answered.

entity.scope: person or account plus the open onboarding or trial instance
entity.note: The struggle is against this attempt at value. A previous trial that went badly does not qualify anyone here.

distinctFrom.because: ACT-13 has a named requirement to clear. Here the evidence is effort without progress and no single thing to point at, which is why the offer is help rather than an instruction.

journeys.objective: Offer help to someone who is visibly trying and not getting anywhere, and stop asking once they have answered.
eligibility: help-seeking behaviour: repeated help-centre visits, repeated returns to the same setup page, repeated failed integration or setup attempts, or repeated errors
and no activation progress behind it
no instance of this journey is already open for the person or account plus the open onboarding or trial instance
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: High activity is not struggling. Someone doing a lot and getting somewhere is the last person to interrupt.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: An open support case for the same issue suppresses this entirely. The automated offer is always the one that does not know the current state.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A decline is respected and cooled down. Asking again after being told no is the behaviour this journey is supposed to replace.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: The offer is made at most twice: the offer itself, and one final self-service alternative.

value.rule: Every touch runs against a budget fixed when the instance opened; the budget is the plan's own length, and no touch is repeated because nothing could tell whether it arrived.

default.applicableWhen: GLB-24; the graph's own touch count

cooldown.rule: The cooldown between instances of this journey for the same person or account plus the open onboarding or trial instance, so that a re-qualifying person or account plus the open onboarding or trial instance is tracked but not messaged again inside it.

roles.when: the person is active in the product and the action is taken there
no active session, a valid token exists, and the message is a single step from the notification
no active session and no valid push token - the message has to be kept and survive until the person returns to act on it

touches.purpose: Offer help named against the step they keep returning to.

touches.purpose: Confirm the time, how to join, and the specific problem the session will open with, taken from the step they were stuck on
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: Send one final self-service option and stop.

useCases: someone returning to the same setup step repeatedly without progress
a help-centre loop with no activation behind it

requires: help-seeking behaviour: repeated help-centre visits, repeated returns to the same setup page, repeated failed integration or setup attempts, or repeated errors
and no activation progress behind it
insufficientAlone: a high session count on its own
a single help-centre visit
heavy usage that is making real progress

nodes.asks: Are the hard entry conditions met?

branches.label: Eligible
branches.when: the onboarding or trial is still open and core activation has not been recorded

branches.label: Not eligible
branches.when: the instance has closed, or activation already happened - in which case the help-seeking is about something else

nodes.state: not in scope for rescue
nodes.reEntry: a later struggle inside an open, unactivated instance qualifies normally

nodes.asks: Is a person already working this same blocker?

branches.label: Already handled
branches.when: an open support case or an assigned human owner covers the same issue, or ACT-13 already owns a named requirement on this instance - the struggle is almost always that requirement, and a help offer beside a blocker reminder is two voices on one problem

branches.label: Nobody on it
branches.when: no open case or owner covers it

nodes.state: deferred to the person already handling it
nodes.reEntry: if that case closes with the struggle unresolved, this qualifies again - two channels chasing one problem is worse than one slow channel

nodes.does: Offer help named against the step they keep returning to. The primary route books assisted setup; the secondary opens the specific guide for that step, for people who would rather not talk to anyone

after.rule: A bounded response window.

timeout.reason: no answer is an answer, and it does not license asking again in the same terms

nodes.recheck: the person or account plus the open onboarding or trial instance re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

nodes.asks: What did they do?

branches.label: Booked
branches.when: an assisted session was scheduled

branches.label: Solved it themselves
branches.when: the activation event was recorded without any session

branches.label: Declined
branches.when: the offer was explicitly turned down

nodes.state: assistance declined, cooldown in force
nodes.reEntry: a new struggle after the cooldown may qualify again; the same offer is not re-sent to someone who has already said no to it

nodes.does: Confirm the time, how to join, and the specific problem the session will open with, taken from the step they were stuck on

after.rule: The scheduled session time plus a short grace period.

timeout.reason: a booking with no recorded outcome is not evidence of anything, and waiting longer will not produce one

nodes.recheck: the person or account plus the open onboarding or trial instance re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

nodes.state: no session outcome recorded
nodes.reEntry: the assistance offer is not repeated on this instance; a fresh struggle after the cooldown is a new question

nodes.asks: Did activation follow the assistance?

branches.label: Activated
branches.when: the authoritative activation event was recorded after the session

branches.label: Still not activated
branches.when: the session happened and value still has not been produced

nodes.asks: Is there one genuinely useful follow-up left?

branches.label: Yes
branches.when: the session surfaced a specific remaining action worth naming

branches.label: No
branches.when: nothing specific came out of it, and a follow-up would only restate the offer

nodes.does: Send one follow-up tied to what the session actually covered. There is no second one, and no further request for a call

nodes.asks: With no response, is one final self-service option worth sending?

branches.label: Worth one
branches.when: a specific guide exists for the step they were stuck on

branches.label: Not worth it
branches.when: nothing specific exists to point at, and a general nudge would just repeat the offer

nodes.does: Send one final self-service option and stop. The call is not asked for a third time

nodes.on: activation reached, with or without the session
carries: whether assistance was involved, which is worth knowing about this account later
the struggle that preceded it

nodes.state: rescue attempt closed, ordinary lifecycle resumes
nodes.reEntry: a new struggle in an open, unactivated instance after the cooldown

guardrails: High activity is not struggling. Someone doing a lot and getting somewhere is the last person to interrupt.
An open support case for the same issue suppresses this entirely. The automated offer is always the one that does not know the current state.
A decline is respected and cooled down. Asking again after being told no is the behaviour this journey is supposed to replace.
The offer is made at most twice: the offer itself, and one final self-service alternative.

journeys.purpose: Make onboarding let go the moment activation is recorded, including the messages it has already queued.

entity.scope: person or account plus the onboarding instance being closed
entity.note: Only this instance closes. Another product's onboarding for the same account is untouched by this activation.

journeys.objective: Make onboarding let go the moment activation is recorded, including the messages it has already queued.
eligibility: the product's own record that core value was produced
no instance of this journey is already open for the person or account plus the onboarding instance being closed
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Activation is never determined by a click on an onboarding email. The message is not the milestone.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Onboarding completion is not product mastery. Closing onboarding says value was produced once, nothing more.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Invalidation reaches queued sends, not only future scheduling. The reminder that arrives after success is the one people remember.

a mandatory operational requirement spun off into its own lifecycle at close

a completed setup checklist
a login
a feature opened but not used to any end

nodes.asks: Did this come from the product's record of value produced?

branches.label: Authoritative
branches.when: the product recorded the value-producing event

branches.label: Proxy
branches.when: the signal describes engagement with a message or navigation inside the product

nodes.state: no activation recorded; onboarding continues untouched
nodes.reEntry: the real event, when it happens, arrives from the product and opens a proper instance

nodes.does: Mark the onboarding objective complete, recording which event satisfied it - so a later question about when this account activated has one answer rather than an inference

Invalidate what onboarding still has outstanding: remaining setup reminders, onboarding calls to action, incomplete-step messages that are no longer true, and assistance prompts whose purpose has just disappeared - including everything already queued

nodes.asks: Does a mandatory operational requirement remain outstanding?

branches.label: Something still required
branches.when: an operational obligation is unmet - a verification, a billing detail, a compliance step - none of which blocked value but all of which still have to happen

branches.label: Nothing outstanding
branches.when: no obligation remains beyond ordinary use

nodes.does: Hand the outstanding operational requirement to its own lifecycle. It does not keep onboarding open, and onboarding does not keep messaging on its behalf

nodes.on: activation recorded and onboarding closed
carries: which event activated the account
what was left unfinished, since activation is not mastery and adoption may still need it
any operational requirement spun off separately
the use_case_id the activating event implies, minted at this handoff since no use-case concept exists prior to activation
suppresses: every remaining onboarding action for this instance, queued or scheduled

guardrails: Activation is never determined by a click on an onboarding email. The message is not the milestone.
Onboarding completion is not product mastery. Closing onboarding says value was produced once, nothing more.
Invalidation reaches queued sends, not only future scheduling. The reminder that arrives after success is the one people remember.
journeys.reusableRule: Once activation occurs, onboarding should relinquish ownership instead of continuing its original sequence.

journeys.name: Early adoption → usage depth → habit or stable use
journeys.purpose: Carry an account from having produced value once to producing it repeatedly, measured against its own use-case.

entity.scope: person or account plus the product or use-case value comes from
entity.note: Adoption is measured against the use-case that produced first value, not against the product's full surface.

distinctFrom.because: Onboarding gets someone to value once. This is about the second, fifth and twentieth time, where the obstacle is habit rather than setup.

journeys.objective: Turn a first activation into repeated value in the same use-case: recognise what was actually produced, point at the one behaviour that would produce more, and stop the moment adoption is stable or stalls.
eligibility: an activation or first value-producing event is recorded for this account in a named use-case
no adoption instance is already open for this account and use-case
the account is not in a terminated or restricted state
hard gates (GLB-31) permit lifecycle communication to the people on the account

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: The moment value is produced repeatedly at the rhythm the use-case implies, adoption is stable and nothing further is sent; the lifecycle owner takes the account.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: When the observation window closes without repeated value the instance hands to adoption recovery; a nurture nudge is never sent into a stall.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Recognition names the real thing produced or is not sent; a next action is surfaced only when one genuinely follows from what they did.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: An open complaint under human ownership, a live risk case or a declared cancellation intent on the same account outranks lifecycle nurture; the touch is deferred and re-evaluated against current state (GLB-06).

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: No touch without permission for lifecycle communication; absent permission is a recorded no-action, never a fallback to another channel.

value.rule: Recognition and the nudges that follow run against one budget fixed when the instance opened; a nudge is never repeated because nothing could tell whether it was seen.

default.applicableWhen: one recognition and a small number of behaviour nudges across the early-adoption window

cooldown.rule: A second activation in the same use-case is the same relationship; a new instance opens only after the previous one has closed and the cooldown has passed.

roles.when: the person is active in the product - the next behaviour is one step away and is best pointed at from inside
no active session, or the recognition and the suggested behaviour have to survive until the person returns

touches.purpose: Acknowledge the specific thing that was produced, in its own terms. Recognition that names nothing real is worse than silence.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: Surface the one action that genuinely follows from what they produced - sharing it, repeating it, extending it - and nothing from the feature list.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: Encourage only the next behaviour that would produce more value in this use-case; breadth is never pushed where the value is narrow.
touches.label: RECOMMENDED_DEFAULT

complaint
message_after_success

useCases: an account that produced its first real result and should now repeat it
a workspace activated on one use-case whose next valuable behaviour is known

requires: a recorded activation, with the use-case that produced it - or, where the product defines activation as first value, the first value-producing event itself: a completed workflow, a completed transaction, a published project, a generated report
the artifact or result that was produced, so recognition can name it
insufficientAlone: a login, a page view or a completed onboarding checklist - nothing was produced
onboarding steps completed without the activation event itself
an opened or clicked message

nodes.does: Read adoption from value-producing usage - how often, how deep, whether success repeats, whether others are involved where the use-case needs them. Activity that produces nothing does not count toward it, however much of it there is
Acknowledge what was actually produced, in the terms of the thing itself. Recognition that names nothing real reads as manufactured and devalues the milestones that follow

nodes.asks: Does a natural next action follow from what they just did?

branches.label: Yes
branches.when: something specific follows from the thing they produced - sharing it, repeating it, extending it
branches.observes: produced_artifact and the use-case's own next step

branches.label: No
branches.when: nothing genuinely follows, and inventing a next step would turn recognition into a pitch

nodes.does: Surface one relevant next action, drawn from what they produced rather than from the product's feature list

nodes.asks: Has adoption become stable?

branches.label: Stable
branches.when: value is being produced repeatedly at the rhythm this use-case implies, without prompting

branches.label: Not yet
branches.when: value has been produced but not reliably repeated

nodes.on: adoption stabilising
carries: the use-case that adoption settled around, which is what any later health or expansion judgement should read
the rhythm it settled at, so a change in it later means something

nodes.does: Identify the next behaviour that would actually produce more value for this use-case, and encourage only that. Breadth is not pursued where the value is narrow - a person who gets everything they need from one workflow is adopted, not under-adopted
nodes.idempotencyKey: account_id + use_case_id + touch id + observation cycle

attemptBudget.rule: Behaviour nudges run against a budget fixed when the instance opened; when it is spent the instance waits out the observation window silently.

after.rule: The early-adoption window is the product's own intended usage rhythm for this use-case; a weekly product and a twice-a-year product cannot share one, and a shared window reports every seasonal account as failing.

timeout.reason: a weekly product and a twice-a-year product cannot share a window, and a shared one would report every seasonal account as failing

nodes.recheck: value-producing usage re-read from the product's own record - not activity, not logins

nodes.on: the early-adoption window passing without repeated value
carries: what was produced and when it stopped
the expected pattern it was measured against, so the stall is diagnosed rather than assumed

guardrails: More feature usage is not better adoption. The measure is repeated value, not surface covered.
Breadth is not forced where value is narrow. Pushing a satisfied single-workflow user toward features they do not need makes the product feel heavier, not stickier.
Vanity activity does not inflate the adoption state. Logins, opened dashboards and idle sessions are excluded by construction, not filtered out afterwards.
journeys.reusableRule: Adoption should measure repeated value-producing behavior, not raw product activity.

journeys.name: Adoption stall → diagnose missing value → recover or re-route
journeys.purpose: Work out why value stopped recurring before doing anything about it, including the case where nothing is wrong.

entity.scope: person or account plus the product or use-case that stalled
entity.note: A stall in one use-case is not a stall in the account. Others it holds may be perfectly healthy.

journeys.name: Churn risk escalation → evidence → intervention priority
journeys.purpose: Decide how hard to push back on a relationship at risk, in proportion to how much independent evidence there actually is.

entity.scope: customer, account or subscription relationship
entity.note: Risk is held where the evidence was observed. A risky subscription inside a healthy account is a risky subscription.

journeys.objective: Decide how hard to push back on a relationship at risk, in proportion to how much independent evidence there actually is.
eligibility: several independent churn-relevant signals crossing a defined threshold together: sustained meaningful usage decline, a failed renewal or payment, a negative support experience, repeated unresolved blockers, explicit dissatisfaction, exploration of cancellation, a key stakeholder leaving, falling account-wide adoption
no instance of this journey is already open for the customer

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A single weak signal never constitutes churn risk. Corroboration between independent signals is what the threshold is measuring.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A high-value customer is not automatically at high risk. Value is what is at stake, not the probability of losing it.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A risk score is not the outcome. It orders attention; it does not decide anything.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: The size of the intervention tracks the strength of the evidence. An expensive save offer on thin evidence teaches customers what to do when they want one.

value.rule: Every touch runs against a budget fixed when the instance opened; the budget is the plan's own length, and no touch is repeated because nothing could tell whether it arrived.

default.applicableWhen: GLB-24; the graph's own touch count

cooldown.rule: Escalation is per risk episode; the same episode re-crossing the threshold is the same instance and a later episode is its own.

competition.precedence: below an open issue under human ownership and below a declared cancellation intent on the same account, above generic retention intervention

roles.when: the step is carried out by a person - a call, a task, a visit - and recorded as done by them

touches.purpose: Raise a task for the account owner or customer success, carrying the evidence rather than the score, and suppress automated retention on this relationship so the person is not contradicted by a sequence while they work

useCases: several independent risk signals crossing a threshold on one account
deciding between a person, an automated intervention, or watching

requires: several independent churn-relevant signals crossing a defined threshold together: sustained meaningful usage decline, a failed renewal or payment, a negative support experience, repeated unresolved blockers, explicit dissatisfaction, exploration of cancellation, a key stakeholder leaving, falling account-wide adoption
insufficientAlone: a single weak signal
high account value, which describes what is at stake rather than the likelihood of losing it
a risk score with no decomposable evidence behind it

nodes.asks: Has explicit cancellation intent already been expressed?

branches.label: Already cancelling
branches.when: a cancellation has been requested or a cancel flow entered

branches.label: No stated intent
branches.when: the risk is inferred from behaviour and events, and nobody has said anything

nodes.on: cancellation intent already on record when risk escalates
carries: the risk evidence, which is context for the conversation rather than a second conversation
suppresses: any separate retention track for this relationship while the cancellation decision is live

nodes.does: Assemble the signals with their sources and strengths. What matters is whether they corroborate each other, not how many there are - three readings of the same underlying event are one piece of evidence

nodes.asks: Is the risk driven by a known operational problem, other than a payment failure already open in payment recovery?

branches.label: Known problem
branches.when: the evidence points at something specific that is broken or unresolved, and it is not a payment failure with an open payment recovery instance on this relationship - that cause already has an owner

branches.label: No known problem
branches.when: the relationship is deteriorating and nothing identifiable is causing it, or the identifiable cause is a payment failure that payment recovery already owns

nodes.on: risk with an identifiable operational cause
carries: the risk evidence and which part of it names the problem
the fact that this is already at risk level, so the cause-specific recovery knows what is at stake
suppresses: promotional retention offers on this relationship until the problem is resolved

nodes.asks: Does the evidence justify a person?

branches.label: Justified
branches.when: the evidence is strong and corroborated, and the relationship warrants the cost of someone's attention

branches.label: Not justified
branches.when: the evidence is real but thin, and putting a person on it would be a larger intervention than the signal supports

nodes.does: Raise a task for the account owner or customer success, carrying the evidence rather than the score, and suppress automated retention on this relationship so the person is not contradicted by a sequence while they work

nodes.on: risk strong enough to justify a person
carries: the assembled evidence, so the first conversation is informed
what has already been sent, so it is not repeated in person

nodes.asks: Is a proportionate automated recovery available?

branches.label: Available
branches.when: something exists that matches the evidence at this strength

branches.label: Nothing proportionate
branches.when: the only available responses are larger than the evidence justifies

nodes.on: a proportionate automated retention intervention being delivered
carries: the evidence it was chosen against
the risk state at the time it was sent

nodes.state: risk recorded, nothing proportionate to do
nodes.reEntry: stronger or fresher evidence re-opens this at a higher level - doing nothing is a legitimate response to weak evidence, and doing something disproportionate is not

guardrails: A single weak signal never constitutes churn risk. Corroboration between independent signals is what the threshold is measuring.
A high-value customer is not automatically at high risk. Value is what is at stake, not the probability of losing it.
A risk score is not the outcome. It orders attention; it does not decide anything.
The size of the intervention tracks the strength of the evidence. An expensive save offer on thin evidence teaches customers what to do when they want one.
journeys.reusableRule: Churn intervention should increase only as independent evidence of relationship risk becomes stronger.

journeys.name: Negative experience → recovery eligibility → appropriate response
journeys.purpose: Match the response to what actually failed, whether it is fixed, and whether a remedy is genuinely owed.

entity.scope: person or account plus the experience or service entity that failed
entity.note: The recovery belongs to the failure. A second unrelated failure is a second instance, and one apology does not cover both.

journeys.objective: After an authoritative service failure, say what failed, what was done and what prevents it recurring - once, only when it is useful, only after the failure is resolved, and only where no other process already owns it; route anything owed to remedy.
eligibility: an authoritative record of a negative experience or service failure attributable to this person and an experience entity
no other recovery process is already handling the same failure
the underlying issue is resolved - nothing is said about a failure that is still ongoing
hard gates (GLB-31) permit service communication

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Another recovery process already handling this failure owns it; this instance defers and nothing is sent.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: While the underlying issue is still broken the operational owner has it; a recovery message before the fix is a promise the journey cannot keep.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A recovery communication is sent only where it is useful to the person - a failure they noticed or were affected by; a silent fix of something they never saw stays silent.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Where policy and impact support compensation the remedy journey (REM-159) owns it; no discount is offered here standing in for an explanation.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Hard gates apply; pressure caps do not, because this is service communication about something that happened to the person.

value.rule: One acknowledgement per failure; a second message about the same failure is a second failure.

default.applicableWhen: the graph reaches at most one acknowledgement per instance

cooldown.rule: Recovery is per failure; a later failure is its own instance and no cooldown applies between failures, though repeated failures are themselves evidence for the relationship's health.

roles.when: the acknowledgement should be something the person can keep - what failed, what was done, what prevents it - which is the default
the failure happened inside the app, the person is active there, and the acknowledgement is short

touches.purpose: Say what failed, what was done about it, and what stops it happening again. No discount standing in for an explanation.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

support_contact_within_24h

useCases: a delivery that failed and was later completed
an outage or error that affected this person and has been fixed
a service appointment that went wrong and was put right

requires: a recorded failure: a service failure, a failed fulfilment, a confirmed disruption, a failed critical action, or severe support dissatisfaction
insufficientAlone: negative feedback on its own, which reports an experience rather than confirming a failure
a low survey score with no incident behind it

nodes.does: Establish what failed, what it cost the customer, whether it has been resolved, whether they are still affected, and whether some other process is already handling it

nodes.asks: Is another recovery process already handling this failure?

branches.label: Already handled
branches.when: an open case, an assigned owner or another recovery journey covers the same incident

branches.label: Nobody on it
branches.when: no existing process covers it

nodes.state: deferred to the process already handling it
nodes.reEntry: if that process closes with the customer still affected, this re-opens - two apologies from two systems is worse than one, because it proves neither knew about the other

nodes.asks: Is the underlying issue still unresolved?

branches.label: Still broken
branches.when: the customer remains affected

branches.label: Resolved
branches.when: the failure is over and the customer is no longer affected

nodes.on: a failure that is still ongoing
carries: what failed and who is affected
the fact that no recovery message has been sent yet
suppresses: apology and compensation messaging until the thing being apologised for has stopped happening

nodes.asks: Is a recovery communication actually useful here?

branches.label: Useful
branches.when: the customer noticed, or would want to know it was handled

branches.label: Not useful
branches.when: the failure was resolved before it reached them - raising it now creates the concern it would be apologising for

nodes.state: resolved without contact
nodes.reEntry: a recurrence, or any sign they did notice, re-opens this

nodes.asks: Does policy and the actual impact support compensation?

branches.label: Owed
branches.when: the impact and the policy both support a remedy

branches.label: Not owed
branches.when: the failure was real but no remedy is justified - which is most failures

nodes.on: a remedy that policy and impact both support
carries: the failure and its assessed impact
what has already been said to the customer

nodes.does: Say what failed, what was done about it, and what stops it happening again. No discount standing in for an explanation - a remedy offered instead of an account of what went wrong reads as buying silence

nodes.state: failure acknowledged, no remedy owed
nodes.reEntry: a recurrence changes the assessment, and repetition is itself part of the impact

guardrails: Negative feedback is not a confirmed service failure. One is a report of an experience, the other is a record of something going wrong.
A discount is not a default apology. Compensation follows impact and policy, not the awkwardness of the conversation.
An existing support case suppresses this entirely. A parallel recovery journey contradicts the person already handling it.
journeys.reusableRule: Service recovery should reflect the actual failure, current resolution state and justified remedy rather than use compensation as a default response.

journeys.name: Recovery signal → observation buffer → stable or relapse
journeys.purpose: Keep the distance between a good sign and an actual recovery, so a relapse is still being watched for when it happens.

entity.scope: person or account plus the health or risk context that deteriorated
entity.note: Recovery is judged in the context that fell. Improvement somewhere else is not recovery here.

distinctFrom.because: An improving engagement state is one input to this. RET-21 updates a state; this decides whether an improvement should be believed yet, which is a different question with a waiting period in it.

journeys.objective: Keep the distance between a good sign and an actual recovery, so a relapse is still being watched for when it happens.
eligibility: a positive behaviour in a context that had deteriorated or received a recovery intervention
no instance of this journey is already open for the person or account plus the health or risk context that deteriorated
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: One login is not recovery. It is the event that starts watching for one.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: One payment attempt may not be payment recovery. An attempt and a restored payment relationship are different facts.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: The observation window is set from the use-case. A window that fits a daily product declares a quarterly one recovered before anything has been proven.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Recovery observation delays declaring the relationship stably recovered. It does not by itself require communication to be suppressed: an authoritative event - a purchase, a completed renewal, an explicit request to stay - can immediately end an inactivity or reactivation restriction and return the person to normal current-state orchestration while this journey is still observing. Operational eligibility restored and health confidently stable are different conclusions with different evidence.

useCases: a good sign after deterioration that is watched before it counts as recovery
a relapse inside the stability window sent back to diagnosis

requires: a positive behaviour in a context that had deteriorated or received a recovery intervention
insufficientAlone: a single login
a single payment attempt, which is an attempt rather than a restored payment relationship
an opened or clicked message

nodes.does: Record RECOVERY_OBSERVED, explicitly not RECOVERED. The whole journey is the distance between those two states, and writing the second one here would remove the reason it exists

after.rule: The stability window appropriate to this use-case and this kind of deterioration.

timeout.reason: surviving the window without relapse is the evidence, so the timeout is the success path rather than the failure one - a payment relationship and a usage pattern need different windows to prove the same thing

nodes.recheck: the person or account plus the health or risk context that deteriorated re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

nodes.does: Record the relapse, keeping the observed improvement in the history rather than erasing it - that something briefly worked is part of the diagnosis, not noise

nodes.on: deterioration returning inside the stability window
carries: what improved, for how long, and what brought it back
the fact that this is a relapse rather than a first occurrence, which usually changes the answer

nodes.does: Record RECOVERED and suppress the recovery interventions still pending, including any queued - a save message arriving after a relationship has genuinely stabilised reopens a question the customer had stopped asking

nodes.on: recovery sustained through the stability window
carries: what had deteriorated and what restored it
the fact that this relationship has recovered once, which is context for the next time it does not

guardrails: One login is not recovery. It is the event that starts watching for one.
One payment attempt may not be payment recovery. An attempt and a restored payment relationship are different facts.
The observation window is set from the use-case. A window that fits a daily product declares a quarterly one recovered before anything has been proven.

Recovery observation delays declaring the relationship stably recovered. It does not by itself require communication to be suppressed: an authoritative event - a purchase, a completed renewal, an explicit request to stay - can immediately end an inactivity or reactivation restriction and return the person to normal current-state orchestration while this journey is still observing. Operational eligibility restored and health confidently stable are different conclusions with different evidence.
journeys.reusableRule: A positive signal begins recovery observation; stable recovery requires evidence that the improvement persists.

journeys.name: Cancellation intent → understand state → save or proceed
journeys.purpose: Treat stated intent to leave as a decision point where a genuinely relevant alternative may be offered, and never as an obstacle course.

entity.scope: the subscription, membership or service relationship being cancelled
entity.note: Intent is against one relationship. Cancelling one subscription says nothing about the others an account holds.

distinctFrom.because: This runs while the decision is still reversible and the person is still deciding. RET-29 runs after it is made, and the two must never share an event.

journeys.objective: At the moment a person declares they want to cancel, learn why if that is useful, offer one genuine alternative if one matches the reason, and let them decide - with the cancellation path fully open at every step.
eligibility: an explicit cancellation intent is declared by the person - in the product, by message or by phone
the relationship is active and cancellable by this person
no save instance is already open for this intent
hard gates (GLB-31) permit service communication

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: The cancellation path is never obstructed: the question and the offer sit beside it, never in front of it, and no contest with another journey delays the cancellation itself.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: The reason is asked once and the alternative is offered once; a second ask or a second offer is pressure on a decision already being made.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: No offer is made where nothing genuinely matches the reason; the person proceeds to decide without one.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A confirmed cancellation goes to execution and nothing further is sent by this journey; an abandoned flow leaves the relationship unchanged and silent.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A declared intent outranks inferred risk on the same account; only the offer step yields to an open issue under human ownership (GLB-06).

value.rule: One question and one offer at most, both at the decision point; the plan has nothing after the decision.

default.applicableWhen: the graph reaches at most one ask and one offer per intent

cooldown.rule: The same intent re-expressed inside the intent window is the same instance; a new intent after a lapsed one is a new instance and the question is not repeated inside the cooldown.

competition.precedence: above risk-driven escalation and offer follow-up on the same account - a declared intent to leave outranks an inferred risk. Only the offer step ever yields; the cancellation path itself is never obstructed by any contest

roles.when: the intent was declared inside the product - the question and the offer are put beside the cancellation step the person is on
the intent was declared outside the product, by message or by phone, and the question or offer has to reach the person where they are

touches.purpose: Ask once why, with the cancellation path fully open beside the question. The question is never a step that has to be passed.

mustNotClaim: that answering is required to cancel

touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: Offer the one alternative that matches the reason, once, alongside an unobstructed route to continue cancelling.

mustNotClaim: that cancelling is harder than it is
an alternative that does not match the reason

touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

cancel_path_obstructed
second_offer_sent

useCases: a subscriber who clicks cancel and is asked once why
a member who tells support they are leaving and is offered the one alternative that fits

requires: an explicit act: a cancel flow entered, a cancellation requested while still reversible, or a cancellation asked for through a person
insufficientAlone: viewing the billing page
a pricing question to support
declining usage, which is a signal about risk and not a statement of intent

nodes.does: Read what they currently hold, what cancelling would end, and when it would take effect - so anything said next is about their actual relationship rather than a generic one

nodes.asks: Is a declared reason available?

branches.label: Declared
branches.when: the person has stated a reason

branches.label: Not declared
branches.when: no reason has been given

nodes.asks: Is asking for a reason useful and appropriate here?

branches.label: Worth asking
branches.when: the answer would change what is offered, and asking does not delay the cancellation

branches.label: Not worth asking
branches.when: the answer would change nothing, or asking would function as friction

nodes.does: Ask once, with the cancellation path fully open beside the question. The question is never a step that has to be passed to leave - a reason obtained that way is not information, it is a toll

after.rule: The question is open only while the person is at the point where it was put; when they leave that point, unanswered is the answer.

default.value: the end of the session or conversation in which the question was put

timeout.reason: a reason is useful only while the choice it informs is still open - an unanswered question is itself an answer, and chasing it is what turns a question into a toll

nodes.recheck: the intent re-read: still open, not confirmed, not abandoned

nodes.asks: What came back?

branches.label: A reason
branches.when: the person stated a reason

branches.label: They decided meanwhile
branches.when: the cancellation was confirmed or abandoned while the question was still open

nodes.does: Record the reason with its source among PRICE, LOW_USAGE, MISSING_VALUE, TECHNICAL_PROBLEM, SERVICE_ISSUE, TEMPORARY_NEED, SWITCHING or OTHER. A reason inferred later never overwrites one that was declared
Proceed without a reason and record that none was given. An inferred reason may be stored, but never in the field that holds declared ones

nodes.asks: Does a legitimate resolution exist for this reason?

branches.label: A real alternative
branches.when: something genuinely addresses the stated reason - technical help for a technical problem, a plan change or pause for cost or temporary need, education for unrealised value, service recovery for a service failure

branches.label: Nothing genuine
branches.when: no alternative actually answers the reason, or no reason was given to answer

nodes.does: Offer the alternative that matches the reason, once, alongside an unobstructed path to continue cancelling. A discount appears only where the reason is price and policy supports it - offering one for a technical fault answers the wrong question and reveals that nobody read the reason

nodes.on: a retention alternative offered at the decision point
carries: the declared reason and the alternative chosen against it
the cancellation episode this belongs to, so a decline is remembered inside it

after.rule: An intent stays meaningful for a bounded period; past it, an unconfirmed cancellation is a lapsed intent and the relationship stands unchanged.

timeout.reason: an intent neither confirmed nor withdrawn is not a standing invitation to keep raising it

nodes.recheck: the relationship re-read: still active, no cancellation executed elsewhere

nodes.asks: What did they decide?

branches.label: Confirmed
branches.when: the cancellation was carried through

branches.label: Abandoned
branches.when: they left the flow with the relationship intact

nodes.on: cancellation confirmed by the customer
carries: the declared reason, which belongs to the record of why this relationship ended
what was offered, if anything, and what was declined

nodes.state: intent expressed, not carried through; relationship unchanged
nodes.reEntry: a fresh expression of intent opens a new episode, and the earlier one is context - repeatedly approaching cancellation is itself evidence RET-24 should be reading

guardrails: Cancellation intent is not cancellation. Nothing downstream may treat this journey's trigger as an ending.
No dark patterns. Every alternative is offered beside an unobstructed path to leave, never in front of one.

A save attempt is bounded by the authoritative renewal or cancellation timing it is competing with, and never contradicts it. An offer that runs past the date it was trying to protect arrives after the decision it was for.
The cancellation path is never made longer to create room for a save attempt.
A discount only where the declared reason and policy both support it. Elsewhere it is an answer to a question nobody asked.
A reason is asked for at most once, and never as a condition of leaving.
journeys.reusableRule: Cancellation intent is a decision point where relevant alternatives may be offered without obstructing the user's ability to leave.

entity.scope: the subscription, membership or service relationship that ended

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: An end-of-period cancellation does not revoke paid entitlement early unless policy says so. They have paid for the remainder.

nodes.asks: Does service or access remain temporarily active?

branches.label: Still active
branches.when: the cancellation takes effect at period end or on a future date

branches.label: Ended now
branches.when: the cancellation took effect immediately

nodes.does: Hold the relationship in a defined wind-down state with its end date. Paid entitlement is not revoked before that date unless policy explicitly says otherwise - someone who cancelled has still paid for the rest of the term, and taking it early converts a neutral ending into a grievance

nodes.asks: Do open obligations remain on either side?

branches.label: Something outstanding
branches.when: a final invoice, a refund, a return, a data export, equipment to come back, or an open support issue

branches.label: Nothing outstanding
branches.when: neither side owes the other anything further

nodes.on: obligations outstanding after cancellation
carries: each outstanding obligation and which side owes it
the termination state, since some obligations only fall due at the end date

nodes.asks: Has the relationship fully ended?

branches.label: Fully ended
branches.when: the end date has passed and nothing is outstanding

branches.label: Still winding down
branches.when: the end date is in the future

nodes.state: former customer; relationship ended, account and data untouched
nodes.reEntry: returning is a new relationship handled by win-back, not by reviving this one. Closing the account and deleting the data are two further states with their own triggers, and neither of them happened here

nodes.state: cancelled, in wind-down until the end date
nodes.reEntry: reversal before the end date is possible and is its own event; the wind-down state exists precisely so that window is representable rather than collapsed into an ending

guardrails: Cancellation is not data deletion. Nothing here removes anything.
Cancellation is not account closure. The account survives the subscription that ended.
An end-of-period cancellation does not revoke paid entitlement early unless policy says so. They have paid for the remainder.
Invalidation runs before anything else, because everything else can wait and a save offer cannot be un-sent.

journeys.name: Retention intervention → outcome → suppress, escalate or exit
journeys.purpose: Close a retention attempt on what actually happened to the relationship, and stop the same offer being made twice.

entity.scope: the customer, account or subscription plus the retention episode the intervention belongs to

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE

nodes.asks: What happened to the intervention?

branches.label: Accepted
branches.when: the customer took what was offered

branches.label: Declined
branches.when: the customer explicitly turned it down

branches.label: Recovered without answering

nodes.asks: Did the state actually change?

branches.label: Applied
branches.when: the authoritative record shows the change

branches.label: Accepted but not applied
branches.when: the customer agreed and the change did not take effect

nodes.asks: Is a cancellation still in progress?

branches.label: No cancellation underway

branches.label: Not justified
branches.when: silence is a clear enough answer and repeating it adds only pressure

nodes.reEntry: a new episode may open on new evidence, and this intervention is not repeated within the cooldown
