journeys.reusableRule: Synchronization conflicts should be resolved through explicit authority rules rather than generic last-write-wins behavior.

journeys.name: External dependency unavailable → degrade capability → alternate or recover
journeys.purpose: Lose only the capability that actually depends on an unavailable provider, and keep every uncertain outcome uncertain.

entity.scope: the external dependency and each capability that depends on it
entity.note: Scope is the whole decision. Failing the product because one provider is down is a self-inflicted outage larger than the one being responded to.

distinctFrom.because: INT-116 is about our integration to a provider failing. This is about the provider itself being unavailable, where an alternate path may exist and the question is what our product can still do.

requires: a critical external dependency confirmed unavailable
insufficientAlone: a single failed call, which is an error rather than an outage

nodes.does: Determine which capabilities actually depend on this provider. Failing the whole product because one dependency is down is a self-inflicted outage larger than the one we are responding to

nodes.asks: What can continue?

branches.label: Degraded mode possible
branches.when: the capability has a reduced form that does not need this dependency

branches.label: A safe alternate exists
branches.when: another provider or path can perform the operation under a defined policy

branches.label: Cannot continue safely
branches.when: neither degradation nor an alternate is available

nodes.does: Disable only the unavailable function and leave everything else working, so the outage the user sees is the size of the outage that happened

nodes.asks: Has the operation already been submitted to the primary provider?

branches.label: Not submitted
branches.when: nothing has reached the primary provider for this operation

branches.label: Already submitted, outcome unknown
branches.when: the operation reached the primary provider and no authoritative outcome exists

nodes.state: alternate not used; the primary operation's outcome is still unknown
nodes.reEntry: the operation's true state is established through reconciliation first. Submitting it again elsewhere while the first outcome is unknown is how one payment becomes two

nodes.does: Use the alternate path according to the defined policy, with its own correlation and idempotency identifiers

Block the affected operation and preserve the user's and the business's state, so nothing is lost and nothing is claimed. Where an outcome is unknown it stays unknown - a provider outage is not evidence that the user's action failed, and recording it as failed converts our blindness into their result

timeout.reason: a degraded capability that has not recovered within its window is an operational decision about whether to keep waiting, and that decision belongs to a person

nodes.does: Revalidate the affected pending actions before resuming any of them. Several may have completed at the provider while we could not see them, and resuming without checking is how a retry becomes a duplicate

nodes.state: capability restored after pending actions were revalidated
nodes.reEntry: a further outage is scoped on its own terms

nodes.on: a dependency outage outliving its operational window
carries: which capabilities are degraded or blocked and for how long
the operations held with unknown outcomes, which nobody has resolved either way

guardrails: A provider outage does not mark a user action as failed while its outcome is unknown.
An alternate provider never repeats an operation already submitted to the primary one.
Success is not claimed until an authoritative outcome exists.
Only the capability that depends on the dependency is degraded.
journeys.reusableRule: External dependency failure should degrade only the capability that actually depends on it while preserving safe recovery and outcome reconciliation.

journeys.name: Integration connection broken → reconnect → restored or degraded
journeys.purpose: Tell the person who owns a broken connection which of their capabilities stopped, whether the fix is theirs to perform, and what one step restores it - so a silent dependency failure becomes a decision instead of a slow discovery.

entity.scope: one connection to one external provider, plus the failure recorded against it
entity.note: The connection is the subject. A second provider failing at the same time is its own instance, and a capability that never depended on this connection is untouched.

distinctFrom.because: INT-112 revalidates capabilities against a changed authorization and sets the connection's state. This journey starts once that state says something is broken, and it never decides what is broken - only what the holder is told.
INT-116 stops unsafe operations and preserves in-flight work. Here nothing operational happens; the subject is the holder's window to re-authorise before the break becomes permanent.

journeys.objective: Tell the person who owns a broken connection which of their capabilities stopped, whether the fix is theirs to perform, and what one step restores it - so a silent dependency failure becomes a decision instead of a slow discovery.
eligibility: an authoritative failed or disconnected state recorded against a named connection
a diagnosed failure cause
the list of capabilities that depended on it
no instance of this journey is already open for the one connection to one external provider
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Nothing is sent before the failure has a diagnosed cause. A notice that cannot say what to do is a notice that generates the question it should have answered.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A reduced authorization disables what depended on it, never the whole connection.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Where the holder cannot perform the fix, no reconnection step is attached.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Restoration is confirmed capability by capability, because a partial recovery and a full one are told apart nowhere else.

value.rule: Every touch runs against a budget fixed when the instance opened; the budget is the plan's own length, and no touch is repeated because nothing could tell whether it arrived.

default.applicableWhen: GLB-24; one notice and one confirmation

cooldown.rule: This journey is per one connection to one external provider; a later instance concerns a different one connection to one external provider and no cooldown applies between them.

default.applicableWhen: the entity note: one instance per entity

roles.when: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it
the person is active in the product and the action is taken there

touches.purpose: Say which capabilities have stopped and that nothing is required from them, with no reconnection step attached - because there is no step that would work.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: Name exactly which capabilities stopped, which are still running, and the single re-authorisation step.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

mustNotClaim: a reduced authorisation as a full one

touches.purpose: Say the connection is carrying nothing at present, name what has stopped depending on it, and give the single re-authorisation step.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: Confirm which capabilities are working again and name any that came back reduced.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

guardrails: complaint
message_after_success
unsubscribe

useCases: a de-authorised connection whose owner is told which capabilities stopped and the one step that restores them
a break the holder cannot fix, stated without a reconnection step

requires: an authoritative failed or disconnected state recorded against a named connection
a diagnosed failure cause
the list of capabilities that depended on it
insufficientAlone: a single failed call that has not been classified
a provider rate limit that clears itself
a scheduled provider maintenance window

nodes.asks: Is the fix the holder's to perform?

branches.label: Holder can re-authorise
branches.when: the cause is a withdrawn, expired or insufficient authorization on the holder's side of the connection

branches.label: Not theirs
branches.when: the cause is a provider outage, a defect on our side, or an entitlement the holder does not control

nodes.does: Say which capabilities have stopped and that nothing is required from them, with no reconnection step attached - because there is no step that would work. Prompting a re-auth against a provider outage produces a person who tries three times and then opens a ticket

nodes.state: informed, recovery not the holder's to perform
nodes.reEntry: if the cause is later reclassified as holder-fixable, this qualifies again on the re-authorisation path

nodes.asks: How much of the connection is affected?

branches.label: Some capabilities
branches.when: the authorization still covers part of what was granted and the rest of the connection keeps running

branches.label: Nothing works
branches.when: no capability on this connection can run until it is re-authorised

nodes.does: Name exactly which capabilities stopped, which are still running, and the single re-authorisation step. Telling somebody their whole connection is broken when most of it works buys an afternoon of unnecessary work and a lasting distrust of the next notice

Say the connection is carrying nothing at present, name what has stopped depending on it, and give the single re-authorisation step. What stopped is the part the holder needs in order to judge how urgent this is

after.rule: The re-authorisation step is left open for a bounded response window from the notice; a connection still broken past it is judged against independent relationship evidence, never labelled from this break alone.

timeout.reason: a broken connection nobody has reconnected is a churn signal long before it is reported as one, and it must be handed over while that is still true

nodes.recheck: the one connection to one external provider re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

nodes.asks: What ended the wait?

branches.label: Reconnected
branches.when: revalidation confirms the capabilities are working against the new authorization

branches.label: Removed
branches.when: the holder deliberately disconnected rather than re-authorising

branches.label: Not theirs after all
branches.when: the cause was reclassified and no holder action would have helped

nodes.does: Confirm which capabilities are working again and name any that came back reduced. A reconnection that silently restores less than before is discovered later, at whatever moment the missing capability was needed

nodes.state: reconnected and confirmed
nodes.reEntry: a later break on the same connection is a new instance

nodes.state: connection deliberately removed by the holder
nodes.reEntry: connecting the same provider again is a new connection and enters through activation, not through this journey

nodes.does: Record that the recovery window closed with the connection still broken, as a dated fact about this integration rather than a conclusion about the relationship. A connection somebody chose not to restore is one signal, and it may be the deliberate end of a use case rather than a customer leaving

nodes.asks: Is there independent evidence that the relationship itself is at risk?

branches.label: Corroborated
branches.when: risk evidence from another source already exists against this relationship, so the unreconnected integration adds to a picture rather than being the whole of it

branches.label: This break is the only signal
branches.when: nothing else indicates the relationship is at risk

nodes.state: recovery window closed, connection still broken, relationship not labelled at risk
nodes.reEntry: a further disconnection event, or a re-authorisation attempt, opens recovery again

nodes.on: a connection the holder could re-authorise and has not, past the point where the break is still being treated as an interruption
carries: which capabilities have been unavailable and for how long
what was already said about the break and on which routes
that this is one contributing signal alongside evidence that already existed, not a churn conclusion drawn from a broken connection

guardrails: Nothing is sent before the failure has a diagnosed cause. A notice that cannot say what to do is a notice that generates the question it should have answered.
A reduced authorization disables what depended on it, never the whole connection.
Where the holder cannot perform the fix, no reconnection step is attached.
Restoration is confirmed capability by capability, because a partial recovery and a full one are told apart nowhere else.
journeys.reusableRule: A broken dependency is worth telling somebody about only when the message can name both what stopped and the one act that would restart it.

journeys.name: Integration connection started → validation outcome → active or targeted fix
journeys.purpose: Tell the person who started a connection which stage it actually failed at and what would fix that stage - because a generic failure sends a capable person to support and an incapable one away for good.

entity.scope: the single connection attempt and the integration it configures
entity.note: One instance per connection. A second connection to the same provider has its own credentials, scopes and outcome, and inherits nothing from this one.

distinctFrom.because: INT-111 authenticates, checks scope, probes capability and decides whether the connection is active. This journey is what the person configuring it is told about that outcome, and it invents no diagnosis of its own.
INT-269 addresses an established connection that has broken. Here nothing has ever worked, so there is no prior capability to restore and nothing to describe as degraded.

journeys.objective: Tell the person who started a connection which stage it actually failed at and what would fix that stage - because a generic failure sends a capable person to support and an incapable one away for good.
eligibility: a connection attempt recorded against a named integration by a named configurer
a recorded outcome from the authentication, scope and capability checks
no instance of this journey is already open for the the single connection attempt and the integration it configures
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: The stage that failed is named, or the failure is admitted as unidentified. A generic error is a support ticket with extra steps.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A saved credential is never described as a connection.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: The message states the capabilities that were validated, never the ones that were configured.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: No fix is suggested that the configurer cannot perform. Where the cause sits with the provider, the message says so.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: One message per named failure. A fix already given is not repeated on the next attempt.

value.rule: Stage messages are repeated only as retries recur, against a total budget fixed at the first attempt; the budget is the company's, and the plan never repeats a stage message without a new attempt behind it.

cooldown.rule: This journey is per the single connection attempt and the integration it configures; a later instance concerns a different the single connection attempt and the integration it configures and no cooldown applies between them.

default.applicableWhen: the entity note: one instance per entity

roles.when: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it
the person is active in the product and the action is taken there

touches.purpose: Confirm the connection is active and name the capabilities that were actually validated rather than the ones that were configured.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: Say the credential itself was refused and give the one step that re-establishes it.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: Name the specific permission that is missing and where it is granted.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: Say that access was granted but the minimum operation could not be performed, and name which operation.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

mustNotClaim: that a saved credential is a connection

touches.purpose: Say the attempt failed, that the stage has not been identified, and that nothing further is needed from the configurer while it is looked at.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

message_after_success

useCases: a connection attempt that names the stage it failed at and the fix for that stage
a successful connection confirmed with the capabilities actually validated

requires: a connection attempt recorded against a named integration by a named configurer
a recorded outcome from the authentication, scope and capability checks
insufficientAlone: an integration browsed or selected
a credential entered but never submitted

nodes.asks: How far did the attempt get?

branches.label: Active
branches.when: authentication, required scope and the capability probe all passed and the connection is recorded active

branches.label: Failed at a named stage
branches.when: the attempt failed and which stage failed is authoritatively recorded

branches.label: Failed, stage unidentified
branches.when: the attempt failed and no stage is authoritatively identified

nodes.does: Confirm the connection is active and name the capabilities that were actually validated rather than the ones that were configured. The difference is what stops somebody building on a permission they do not have

nodes.state: active, with validated capabilities stated
nodes.reEntry: a further connection to the same provider is a new instance

nodes.asks: Which stage failed?

branches.label: Credential
branches.when: the provider refused the credential or the authorisation was never completed

branches.label: Permission
branches.when: the credential was accepted but a required permission was not granted

branches.label: Capability
branches.when: credential and permission both passed but the safe probe could not perform the minimum operation

nodes.does: Say the credential itself was refused and give the one step that re-establishes it. This is the only stage the configurer can usually fix unaided, and it is the one most often buried under a generic error

attemptBudget.rule: This loop runs against a budget fixed when the instance opened; when it is spent the instance takes its timeout path (GLB-24).

nodes.does: Name the specific permission that is missing and where it is granted. A missing permission reported as a failed setup makes somebody redo an entire connection to change one switch

attemptBudget.rule: This loop runs against a budget fixed when the instance opened; when it is spent the instance takes its timeout path (GLB-24).

nodes.does: Say that access was granted but the minimum operation could not be performed, and name which operation. This usually sits with a limit on the provider side, so the message points there rather than at the configurer

attemptBudget.rule: This loop runs against a budget fixed when the instance opened; when it is spent the instance takes its timeout path (GLB-24).

nodes.does: Say the attempt failed, that the stage has not been identified, and that nothing further is needed from the configurer while it is looked at. Admitting there is no cause yet beats inventing one - a guessed cause sends somebody to fix what is not broken

nodes.on: a failed connection attempt with no stage authoritatively identified
carries: the attempt, its provider and what the configurer has already been told
which stages did pass before the failure

after.rule: The period beyond which an unfinished connection is treated as abandoned.

timeout.reason: a half-configured integration nobody returns to is not work in progress and must stop being counted as such

nodes.recheck: the the single connection attempt and the integration it configures re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

nodes.asks: What did the next attempt do?

branches.label: Now active
branches.when: a later attempt passed every stage and the connection is recorded active

branches.label: Failed again
branches.when: a later attempt failed at a stage that has already been named to the configurer

branches.label: Failed at a different stage
branches.when: a later attempt cleared the stage that was named and failed at one that has not been named yet

branches.label: Removed
branches.when: the configuration was removed before any attempt succeeded

nodes.state: still not connected after the named fix
nodes.reEntry: a later attempt re-enters at the outcome check; a fix already given is not sent twice

nodes.state: abandoned before the connection was ever made
nodes.reEntry: a new attempt on the same integration starts a fresh instance

guardrails: The stage that failed is named, or the failure is admitted as unidentified. A generic error is a support ticket with extra steps.
A saved credential is never described as a connection.
The message states the capabilities that were validated, never the ones that were configured.
No fix is suggested that the configurer cannot perform. Where the cause sits with the provider, the message says so.
One message per named failure. A fix already given is not repeated on the next attempt.
