useCases: a payment applied to its obligation exactly once
a restriction released only where it rested on that obligation

requires: an authoritative payment, credit or settlement that discharges some or all of an obligation
insufficientAlone: a payment authorised but not settled
a financial event that names no obligation
a reminder or dunning event, which is communication about an obligation

nodes.does: Apply the amount idempotently against the obligation, keyed so the same financial event arriving twice moves the balance once. Currency compatibility is checked before anything is netted - amounts in different currencies are not offset against each other
Recalculate the remaining balance, the obligation's status, any overpayment, and which dependent restrictions or holds rested on this obligation specifically

nodes.asks: What does the recalculated balance show?

branches.label: Fully satisfied
branches.when: the balance reaches zero

branches.label: Partially satisfied
branches.when: an amount remains outstanding

branches.label: Overpaid
branches.when: the amount applied exceeds what was owed

nodes.does: Record PARTIALLY_SATISFIED with the remaining balance stated explicitly. Partial is not paid, and a remainder that is implied rather than carried is one nobody can collect and nobody can dispute

nodes.state: PARTIALLY_SATISFIED; the remaining balance is explicit and still outstanding
nodes.reEntry: further financial events apply against the remaining balance. Restrictions that depended on this obligation stay in force, because it is not discharged

nodes.on: an amount applied exceeding what was owed
carries: the obligation, the amount applied and the excess, with its currency
the fact that the obligation is satisfied and the excess is a separate financial position

nodes.does: Record SATISFIED against the obligation

nodes.asks: Does an existing restriction depend solely on this obligation?

branches.label: Restriction rested on this
branches.when: a capability was restricted specifically because this obligation was unpaid

branches.label: No restriction depended on it
branches.when: nothing was withheld on account of this obligation

nodes.on: an obligation whose payment removes the reason a capability was restricted
carries: the obligation and the restriction it caused
the instruction to revalidate rather than replay - paying this does not restore capabilities that were suspended for their own separate reasons

the obligation's own account_id (resolved from the obligation record's payer/account, per its own entity scope), and a restoration_case_id minted at this handoff from obligation_id and the restriction it caused, so ACC-79 can construct its own instance without inventing either

nodes.state: SATISFIED; nothing else depended on it
nodes.reEntry: a later adjustment or reversal against this obligation is its own financial event, applied to a discharged balance rather than an outstanding one

guardrails: A payment success is never applied twice.
Financial satisfaction does not automatically restore unrelated suspended capabilities.
Partial payment is not full payment, and the remainder is carried explicitly.
Amounts are not netted across incompatible currencies.
journeys.reusableRule: Successful financial events should update the obligation balance exactly once and release only the states that actually depended on that obligation.

journeys.purpose: Turn a refund request into an authorised decision, without money moving on the request itself.

entity.scope: the refund request and the original transaction it is made against
entity.note: The request does not modify the original payment history. It creates a decision process alongside it.

distinctFrom.because: Approving a refund authorises the movement. FIN-138 performs it and confirms the money arrived, which fails independently and more often than the decision does.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE

default.applicableWhen: GLB-24; the graph's own touch count

cooldown.rule: This journey is per the refund request and the original transaction it is made against; a later instance concerns a different the refund request and the original transaction it is made against and no cooldown applies between them.

default.applicableWhen: the entity note: one instance per entity

roles.when: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it
the step is carried out by a person - a call, a task, a visit - and recorded as done by them

touches.purpose: Reject with the actual reason and whatever process does apply.

touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

message_after_success
unsubscribe

useCases: a refund request turned into an authorised decision without money moving on the request
a request needing judgement, acknowledged as under review without implying an outcome

requires: a refund requested against an identified original transaction
insufficientAlone: dissatisfaction expressed about a purchase, which is feedback until it is made as a request

nodes.does: Record the request id, the original transaction, the requested amount, the reason, the requester and the submission time. The original payment history is not modified by a request made against it

nodes.asks: Is the request valid and within the process scope?

branches.label: Valid
branches.when: it identifies a real transaction, from someone entitled to ask, within any applicable window

branches.label: Out of scope
branches.when: it names no valid transaction, comes from someone with no standing, or falls outside the process entirely

nodes.does: Reject with the actual reason and whatever process does apply. A rejection that does not say why produces the next request rather than closing this one

nodes.asks: Is a refund eligibility policy defined for this transaction type?

branches.label: Defined
branches.when: policy states what qualifies for a refund and on what terms

branches.label: Not defined
branches.when: no policy covers this kind of refund

nodes.on: a refund request with no governing eligibility policy
carries: the request and the original transaction
the explicit fact that no eligibility rule was invented in order to decide it

nodes.asks: What does the policy determine?

branches.label: Eligible
branches.when: the policy's conditions are met deterministically

branches.label: Ineligible
branches.when: the policy rules it out deterministically

branches.label: Requires judgement
branches.when: the policy leaves this case to a decision rather than a rule

nodes.does: Record REJECTED with the reason drawn from the policy that ruled it out

Tell the requester the refund was refused and the governing reason, whether that came from policy directly or from a reviewer. A refusal recorded and never sent leaves someone waiting on a decision that has already been made

nodes.state: REJECTED; no money moves and the original transaction stands
nodes.reEntry: a differently grounded request, or new evidence, is assessed on its own. A refund requested is not a refund owed

nodes.does: Record UNDER_REVIEW and gather whatever the decision requires. Nothing moves while it is under review

Tell the requester the refund is under review and what that state means, without implying an outcome. The wait for a human decision is the longest silence in this journey and the one most easily read as no answer coming

after.rule: The decision SLA.

timeout.reason: a refund request left undecided is a customer waiting on money with no answer, which produces a dispute that costs more than the refund

nodes.recheck: the the refund request and the original transaction it is made against re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

nodes.asks: What was decided?

branches.label: Approved
branches.when: the reviewer authorised the refund

branches.label: Rejected
branches.when: the reviewer declined it

nodes.on: a refund decision outliving its SLA
carries: the request, its age and what is holding the decision

nodes.does: Record APPROVED with the authorised amount and the authority that approved it. Approved authorises the movement and performs none of it

nodes.on: a refund authorised for execution
carries: the approved amount, its currency and the original transaction
the explicit fact that nothing has moved yet

guardrails: A refund requested is not a refund owed.
A refund request does not modify the original payment history.
Eligibility policy is never invented. Where none exists the decision goes to a person.
journeys.reusableRule: A refund request creates a financial decision process; money should move only after the request reaches an authorized outcome.

journeys.name: Refund approved → execute → confirm or reconcile
journeys.purpose: Move the money and confirm it arrived, keeping that separate from having decided it should.

entity.scope: the approved refund and the original transaction it is issued against
entity.note: A refund is a new financial event rather than an edit to the original transaction, which stays historical throughout.

requires: a refund approved for a stated amount against a stated transaction

nodes.does: Submit the refund under a stable operation identity and record REFUND_PENDING. The stable identity is what stops a retry or a redelivered response producing a second refund - and a duplicate refund is money that has to be asked for back

timeout.reason: a provider accepting the request is not the customer's funds having returned, and the gap between those two is where a replayed refund is created

nodes.asks: What did the refund do?

branches.label: Completed in full
branches.when: the full approved amount returned to the customer

branches.label: Completed partially
branches.when: part of the approved amount returned

branches.label: Failed
branches.when: the provider reports the refund did not go through

nodes.does: Record REFUNDED and reconcile against the original transaction and the obligation balance. The original transaction stays historical - a refund is a new financial event and not an edit to the old one, and rewriting the original would remove the evidence that either happened

nodes.state: REFUNDED; funds confirmed returned and balances reconciled
nodes.reEntry: a further refund against the same transaction is a new request with its own approval

nodes.does: Record the partial refund and update the remaining refundable amount explicitly, so what is still owed back is carried rather than implied

nodes.state: partially refunded; the remaining refundable amount is explicit
nodes.reEntry: the remainder is executed as its own operation against the recorded balance

nodes.does: Record the refund outcome as unknown and suppress any replay. Submitting again while this one may have completed produces a duplicate refund, which is the same failure as a duplicate charge pointing the other way

nodes.asks: Is a retry safe within the bounded policy?

branches.label: Safe and available
branches.when: the failure is transient and the operation identity guarantees no duplicate

branches.label: Not safe or exhausted
branches.when: the failure is not transient, or the retry budget is spent

nodes.on: a refund that failed, could not be retried, or whose outcome is unknown
carries: the approved refund, the original transaction and every attempt made
the customer's position, which is that a refund was approved and they have not received it

guardrails: Approved is not refunded.
A provider accepting the refund request is not the customer's funds having returned.
A retry never creates a duplicate refund.
The original transaction remains historical.
journeys.reusableRule: Refund execution requires independent confirmation because approval authorizes the refund but does not prove funds were returned.

journeys.name: Financial dispute or chargeback → evidence → decision → reconcile
journeys.purpose: Run a transaction-level dispute through the authority that decides it, without treating the claim as a finding.

entity.scope: the dispute and the specific transaction it contests
entity.note: The dispute is adjudicated by an external authority with its own deadline and its own evidence rules. Our part is representation, not decision.

distinctFrom.because: FBK-47 reviews a decision we made, under our own process. A chargeback is adjudicated by a card scheme or a regulator with power to move funds regardless of what we conclude, and missing its deadline decides it against us whatever the evidence says.

requires: a dispute or chargeback formally opened with the authority or provider that adjudicates it
insufficientAlone: a customer complaining about a charge, which is feedback until it is raised with the body that can reverse it

nodes.does: Record the dispute id, the transaction, the amount, the reason category, when it opened, the response deadline and the external authority handling it. A dispute being opened is not fraud confirmed and not a loss - it is a claim with a deadline, and most of them are confusion, a forgotten subscription or an unrecognised descriptor
Collect the evidence this dispute category actually requires, which the authority defines rather than we do

nodes.asks: Is a response or representation allowed?

branches.label: Allowed
branches.when: the process permits us to submit evidence before the deadline

branches.label: Not allowed
branches.when: the category or stage admits no representation

nodes.does: Submit before the deadline. A deadline missed is usually decided against us regardless of what the evidence would have shown, which makes the date more important than the argument

timeout.reason: the decision is not ours to make or to hurry, and an undecided dispute stays an unresolved financial state rather than defaulting either way

nodes.state: UNKNOWN / PENDING; the authority has not decided
nodes.reEntry: the decision arriving later reconciles normally. Nothing is written off in either direction while the claim is live

nodes.asks: What did the authority decide?

branches.label: WON
branches.when: the original transaction stands

branches.label: LOST
branches.when: the funds are reversed against us

branches.label: PARTIAL
branches.when: part of the amount is reversed

branches.label: WITHDRAWN
branches.when: the claimant withdrew it

nodes.does: Reconcile the financial balance and the related obligation according to the outcome - won leaves the original transaction standing, lost reverses the funds and reopens what they had discharged, partial does both in proportion, withdrawn leaves everything as it was. In every case the dispute's own history is preserved: the final outcome does not overwrite the record of what was claimed, what was submitted and when

nodes.asks: Does the outcome warrant action on the business relationship?

branches.label: Warrants assessment
branches.when: a pattern or the outcome itself raises a question about the relationship

branches.label: Financial only
branches.when: the dispute is settled and says nothing about the relationship

nodes.on: a dispute outcome raising a risk question that has not been answered
carries: the dispute and its outcome
the explicit fact that a dispute is not a finding of wrongdoing - it is a signal to be evaluated, and most of them are not what they look like

nodes.state: dispute decided and reconciled; history preserved
nodes.reEntry: a further dispute on the same transaction is its own instance with its own deadline

guardrails: A dispute opened is not fraud confirmed.
A dispute opened is not a dispute lost.
The dispute history is not overwritten by the final outcome.
A generic decision appeal is not a substitute for transaction-level dispute mechanics.
journeys.reusableRule: Financial disputes remain unresolved financial states until the governing authority returns an outcome that can be reconciled against the original transaction.

journeys.name: Financial reconciliation → detect mismatch → correct or escalate
journeys.purpose: Restore financial consistency by explaining the difference and adjusting it, never by editing the record that is inconvenient.

entity.scope: the set of financial records that disagree - transactions, obligations, refunds and settlement state together
entity.note: Several records, several systems. What makes this different from an unknown outcome is that everyone has an answer and the answers do not match.

distinctFrom.because: FIN-135 has one attempt and no answer, and the provider can supply one. Here every system has an answer and they disagree, which needs comparison, an authority rule and an explicit adjustment.

requires: a material inconsistency across financial records: a payment succeeded with the obligation still open, a refund completed with the balance unchanged, a provider settlement differing from local state, a duplicate charge, a missing transaction, or an incorrect partial balance

nodes.does: Collect the authoritative records from every relevant system rather than reasoning from the one that raised the alarm

Compare transaction identifiers, amounts, currency, statuses, timestamps, obligation allocations, refunds and credits, and settlement state. Amounts in different currencies are not compared or netted - a mismatch across currencies is a context error rather than a discrepancy, and resolving it as one produces a balance that is confidently wrong

nodes.asks: What can be established from the records?

branches.label: A deterministic correction
branches.when: the authoritative records identify what the true state is and what the difference was

branches.label: External confirmation needed
branches.when: the provider holds the answer and has not supplied it

branches.label: Cannot be safely resolved
branches.when: the records disagree in a way the evidence does not settle - and a newer record is not automatically the correct one

until: the provider confirms the authoritative state

timeout.reason: an unreconciled financial position is a balance nobody can rely on, and waiting past the window turns it into a permanent one

nodes.asks: Does an accounting policy cover this correction?

branches.label: Covered
branches.when: policy states how this kind of difference is adjusted and against what

branches.label: Not covered
branches.when: no accounting policy addresses it

nodes.does: Apply the correction idempotently as an explicit adjustment, preserving the adjustment history. A mismatch is never fixed by deleting the inconvenient transaction - the correction is a new record that explains the difference, and the original stays so the explanation has something to refer to
Verify the final financial state balances according to the defined accounting and business invariants

nodes.asks: Does the corrected state balance?

branches.label: Balanced
branches.when: every invariant holds after the adjustment

branches.label: Still not balanced
branches.when: the correction did not close the difference, or opened another

nodes.state: reconciled through an explicit, auditable adjustment
nodes.reEntry: a further mismatch on the same records is its own reconciliation, with this adjustment in the history

nodes.does: Record FINANCIAL_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED, naming exactly which records disagree and by how much. Accounting policy is not invented to close it - an unexplained difference stated plainly is worth more than a resolved one nobody can justify

nodes.on: a financial difference that cannot be safely resolved
carries: every record collected, with its source, amount, currency and timestamp
the difference itself, and the invariant it breaks

guardrails: A financial mismatch is never fixed by deleting inconvenient transaction history.
The newest record is not automatically the correct one.
Corrections are explicit adjustments rather than silent rewrites.
Accounting policy is never invented.
journeys.reusableRule: Financial reconciliation restores consistency by explaining and correcting mismatches through authoritative transaction history rather than rewriting financial history.

journeys.objective: Decide whether we are taking responsibility for delivering something, as a state distinct from having been asked.

no instance of this journey is already open for the the fulfillment request and
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

a request held on an unresolved dependency until it lapses or clears

insufficientAlone: a payment succeeding, which discharges a financial obligation and does not by itself create a fulfillment one
an item placed in a basket or a slot browsed

Validate the minimum fulfillment requirements - that what is asked for exists as something we deliver, that the destination is serviceable, that the requester may ask for it, and that the scope is coherent

nodes.asks: Is the request valid?

branches.label: Valid
branches.when: it passes the minimum requirements for us to consider taking it on

branches.label: Invalid
branches.when: it fails a requirement in a way no dependency will resolve

nodes.does: Record REJECTED with the specific reason. No obligation is created - a hidden obligation behind a rejected request is one nobody is working and nobody knows exists, and it surfaces when the customer asks where their order is

nodes.state: REJECTED; no fulfillment obligation created
nodes.reEntry: a corrected request is validated on its own terms

nodes.asks: Is an additional dependency unresolved?

branches.label: Something outstanding
branches.when: a prerequisite, an approval, a document or a confirmation is required before we can take responsibility

branches.label: Nothing outstanding
branches.when: everything required to accept is present

nodes.does: Record HOLD / PENDING_REQUIREMENT, naming the specific dependency. A held request is not an accepted one and creates no obligation while it waits

after.rule: The request's validity window.

timeout.reason: a request held indefinitely against an unresolved dependency is neither accepted nor refused, and the requester cannot tell which they have

nodes.recheck: the the fulfillment request and re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

nodes.state: request lapsed with its dependency unresolved; no obligation created
nodes.reEntry: a fresh request is validated against whatever the dependency now looks like

nodes.does: Record ACCEPTED and create the fulfillment obligation. This is where responsibility for delivery begins, and everything downstream is owed rather than merely requested

nodes.on: an accepted obligation requiring resources to satisfy it
carries: the obligation, its scope and its requested timing
the explicit fact that nothing has been reserved - acceptance is a promise, not a claim on capacity

guardrails: A request received is not a request accepted.

journeys.objective: Establish whether the resources to satisfy an accepted obligation actually exist, in the scope and window that would serve it.

no instance of this journey is already open for the the obligation and the resources it requires
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.text: Catalog availability is not allocatable availability.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: An accepted order is not allocated inventory.

requires: an accepted obligation whose satisfaction requires committing a resource or capacity
insufficientAlone: a catalog availability figure
an order accepted with no resource requirement
a payment succeeding

Catalog availability is a statement about what we sell; allocatable availability is a statement about what can be committed to this obligation now

nodes.asks: What is actually available for this obligation?

branches.label: Fully available
branches.when: everything the obligation needs can be committed in the right scope and window

branches.label: Partially available
branches.when: some of the scope can be committed and some cannot

branches.label: Temporarily unavailable
branches.when: the resource is expected to return within a window the obligation can tolerate

branches.label: Cannot be fulfilled
branches.when: the resource will not be available within any window this obligation tolerates

nodes.asks: Does policy permit partial fulfillment of this obligation?

branches.label: Partial permitted
branches.when: the scope divides and delivering part of it is useful to the recipient

branches.label: All or nothing
branches.when: the scope does not divide, or a partial delivery would not serve the recipient

nodes.does: Record BACKORDER / WAITING_CAPACITY, naming exactly what is missing and what would resolve it. The obligation stands - it is waiting on capacity rather than failing

after.rule: The obligation's tolerance window.

nodes.recheck: the the obligation and the resources it requires re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

nodes.asks: With capacity returned, can the obligation now be served?

branches.label: Now available
branches.when: the returned capacity covers what this obligation needs in its scope and window

branches.label: Still short
branches.when: what returned does not cover this obligation, or was taken by another

nodes.does: Record FULFILLMENT_UNAVAILABLE with what could not be sourced and why

nodes.on: an obligation that cannot be resourced
carries: the obligation and what could not be sourced
the explicit fact that nothing has been allocated, so there is nothing to release - and that any financial consequence is a separate lifecycle

nodes.on: resources existing that can serve this obligation
carries: the obligation, the scope to be committed and the resources identified
the explicit fact that availability was read and not yet claimed

guardrails: Catalog availability is not allocatable availability.
An accepted order is not allocated inventory.

journeys.name: Resource allocation → reserve → confirm, release or reallocate

entity.scope: the allocation itself - a link between a specific resource quantity and one fulfillment obligation
entity.note: The allocation belongs to one obligation. Releasing it touches only that link, never a shared resource's other claims.

eligibility: a specific resource identified as the one that will serve a specific obligation
no instance of this journey is already open for the the allocation itself
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Allocation is idempotent.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A cancelled fulfillment does not retain scarce resource.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A release affects only this obligation's allocation, never another's or a shared claim.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A temporary reservation carries an explicit expiry or release condition.

guardrails: state_written_on_stale_entity

useCases: specific capacity bound to one obligation until consumed or released
a temporary reservation expiring unconsumed

requires: a specific resource identified as the one that will serve a specific obligation
insufficientAlone: a catalog quantity being positive
an order accepted before a specific resource is identified
a reservation request that lost its race for the resource

nodes.does: Create the allocation idempotently, storing the resource id, the quantity or capacity, the fulfillment it belongs to, the reservation time, its validity and its status. Idempotency is what stops a retried allocation consuming the resource twice - which is how a system oversells without anyone overselling anything

nodes.asks: Was the reservation confirmed?

branches.label: Confirmed
branches.when: the resource system accepted the claim

branches.label: Lost to another claim
branches.when: the resource went between the availability reading and this reservation

nodes.on: a reservation losing a race for a resource that had appeared available
carries: the obligation and what it still needs
the fact that this is the concurrency the availability check cannot prevent, which is why the claim rather than the reading is what commits

nodes.asks: Is this reservation temporary?

branches.label: Temporary
branches.when: the claim expires unless consumed within a window

branches.label: Held until consumed or released
branches.when: the claim stands until the obligation uses it or gives it up

nodes.does: Record ALLOCATED with an explicit expiry or release condition. A reservation with no stated end holds scarce capacity against an obligation that may never consume it, and nobody discovers it until the capacity is needed
Record ALLOCATED, held until the obligation consumes it or explicitly releases it

after.rule: The reservation's validity, where it has one.

timeout.reason: a temporary claim that expires returns the capacity to whoever needs it next, which is the whole reason for making it temporary

nodes.recheck: the the allocation itself re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

nodes.asks: What happened to the allocation?

branches.label: Consumed
