journeys.name: Availability query → evaluate capacity → offer valid options
journeys.purpose: Produce the options that are genuinely bookable right now, and say plainly that nothing is being held.

entity.scope: the availability request and the schedulable resource or service it asks about
entity.note: The request is a question, not a claim on anything. Nothing it returns is protected between being shown and being requested.

distinctFrom.because: FUL-142 asks whether an accepted obligation can be resourced at all. This asks which specific times a resource can be committed to, for a requester who has not committed to anything yet.

requires: a request for bookable times against an identified resource, service or context

nodes.asks: Does an authoritative capacity model exist for this resource and service?

branches.label: It exists
branches.when: capacity, duration, operating window and any lead-time or buffer rules are defined

branches.label: It does not
branches.when: no authoritative capacity model covers this resource

nodes.does: Record that this resource has no authoritative capacity model, and return no options rather than every option. An absent constraint is not an absence of constraint - a resource with nothing configured will otherwise appear infinitely bookable, and the overbooking is discovered by whoever turns up

Evaluate the authoritative constraints together - the resource's capacity, the service's duration, the location and context, eligibility constraints, existing reservations and holds, the operating window, lead-time rules and any defined buffers. Operating hours are not availability: a clinic open until six with every slot taken has nothing at five

Return only the options currently valid for the requested resource and context, labelled as what they are - what appeared bookable at this instant. Nothing here is held, and under contention any of it can be gone before the requester acts

nodes.asks: Did any valid option survive the evaluation?

branches.label: Options exist
branches.when: at least one slot satisfies every constraint

branches.label: None
branches.when: no slot in the requested window satisfies the constraints

nodes.does: Record NO_AVAILABILITY for the requested window, with the constraint that closed it where that can be said without exposing anything it should not

nodes.asks: What does policy offer when the requested window is empty?

branches.label: A different window
branches.when: policy allows offering the nearest valid alternative

branches.label: A waitlist
branches.when: the resource operates a waitlist for released capacity

branches.label: Nothing further
branches.when: policy offers neither

nodes.does: Offer the nearest valid window, labelled as a different window rather than presented as the one that was asked for. Someone who wanted Tuesday and is shown Friday should be able to see that at a glance
Record the requester as waitlisted, which reserves nothing. Waitlisted is not reserved, and someone who believes they hold a place they do not hold will plan their day around it

nodes.state: valid options offered; no capacity is held by this query
nodes.reEntry: any option shown can be taken by someone else before it is requested. The reservation revalidates against current capacity rather than against what was displayed

nodes.state: waitlisted; nothing is reserved and no time is committed
nodes.reEntry: capacity being released offers the waitlisted requester a chance to book, which is a new request that has to be confirmed like any other

nodes.state: NO_AVAILABILITY for the requested resource and window
nodes.reEntry: availability changes constantly as holds expire and reservations cancel. A later query is answered on its own terms rather than from this result

guardrails: A displayed schedule is not guaranteed availability until a reservation or hold succeeds.
Availability is never inferred from generic operating hours.
Availability is evaluated for the requested resource and context rather than for the service in general.
journeys.reusableRule: Availability represents capacity that appears bookable at query time; commitment begins only after that capacity is successfully reserved.

journeys.name: Slot hold → reserve temporarily → confirm, expire or release
journeys.purpose: Protect specific capacity for a bounded moment while a booking is being completed, without pretending it is a booking.

entity.scope: the hold, the capacity it protects and the requester who owns it
entity.note: One hold per requester per slot. A second hold by the same requester consumes the capacity twice and releases at two different times.

distinctFrom.because: FUL-143 allocates a resource to an obligation that already exists. This protects capacity for a commitment that does not exist yet and may never - most holds end in expiry rather than in a booking.

journeys.objective: Protect specific capacity for a bounded moment while a booking is being completed, without pretending it is a booking.
eligibility: a hold granted against real, currently free capacity on an identified slot
no instance of this journey is already open for the the hold
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A hold is not a confirmed reservation.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: An expired hold consumes no capacity.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Hold creation and release are both idempotent.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Concurrent holds respect real capacity rather than the capacity each of them assumed.

guardrails: state_written_on_stale_entity

useCases: capacity protected for a bounded moment while a booking is completed
an expired hold consuming nothing

requires: a hold granted against real, currently free capacity on an identified slot
insufficientAlone: a hold requested, which is not a hold granted - under contention two requests can both be made and only one can succeed, and treating the request as the grant overbooks by exactly the number of losers

nodes.asks: Does a live hold by this requester already cover this slot?

branches.label: One already exists
branches.when: an unexpired hold with the same owner and slot is live

branches.label: None
branches.when: no live hold covers it

nodes.does: Return the existing hold rather than creating a second. A retried booking step produces one hold, not two - two holds against one slot consume twice the capacity and expire at two different moments, so the slot is unbookable long after either of them mattered

Create the scoped hold with its id, the resource and slot, the capacity held, the owner, the creation time, the expiry and the booking intent it belongs to. Record HELD. The hold consumes capacity for its duration and creates no commitment - nobody has an appointment, and nothing here should be described to the requester as if they do

after.rule: The hold's expiry.

timeout.reason: the expiry is the entire point of a hold. Capacity still counted against a lapsed one is capacity nobody can book and nobody owns, and the resource reads as full while standing empty

nodes.recheck: the the hold re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

nodes.asks: What resolved the hold?

branches.label: Confirmed
branches.when: a reservation was confirmed against this hold

branches.label: Explicitly released
branches.when: the owner or the booking flow released it

branches.label: The intent was abandoned
branches.when: the booking attempt that created it stopped

nodes.asks: Is the held capacity still required by anything live?

branches.label: No longer needed
branches.when: nothing else depends on this capacity being held

branches.label: Still needed
branches.when: another live booking step for the same requester still depends on it

nodes.does: Release the capacity and record the hold EXPIRED. An expired hold consumes nothing, and the release happens because the clock said so rather than because anyone remembered

Release the capacity and record the hold RELEASED. The release is idempotent - releasing an already-released hold changes nothing rather than returning capacity a second time, and the difference between those two behaviours is how many people can be booked into one slot

Consume the hold into the confirmed reservation, moving the capacity from held to reserved in one step. Releasing first and re-taking opens a window - short, and entirely long enough - in which someone else takes the slot the requester has just paid for

nodes.state: consumed into a confirmed reservation; capacity never passed back through free
nodes.reEntry: the reservation now owns the capacity. A cancellation releases it through the cancellation lifecycle rather than through this hold

nodes.state: EXPIRED; capacity released and available again
nodes.reEntry: the same requester can take a new hold on the same slot if it is still free, which is a new hold rather than an extension of this one

nodes.state: RELEASED; capacity available again
nodes.reEntry: a repeated release against this hold is a no-op rather than a second return of capacity

guardrails: A hold is not a confirmed reservation.
An expired hold consumes no capacity.
Hold creation and release are both idempotent.
Concurrent holds respect real capacity rather than the capacity each of them assumed.
journeys.reusableRule: A temporary hold protects capacity for a bounded period without creating the full commitment of a confirmed reservation.

journeys.name: Reservation request → validate → confirm, reject or pending
journeys.purpose: Turn a request for a specific time into a commitment both sides can rely on, or say clearly that it did not.

entity.scope: the reservation request, the requester and the resource or service it names
entity.note: One reservation per requester, resource and slot. A retried submission produces the same reservation rather than a second one against the same capacity.

distinctFrom.because: FUL-141 creates a generic fulfillment obligation. This creates a commitment to a specific time on both sides - which is why it revalidates capacity at the moment of confirming and why its failure mode is contention rather than eligibility.

journeys.objective: Turn a request for a specific time into a commitment both sides can rely on, or say clearly that it did not.
eligibility: a request to reserve an identified slot on an identified resource or service
no instance of this journey is already open for the the reservation request
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A request submitted is not a reservation confirmed.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Previously displayed availability may have changed and is revalidated rather than trusted.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A payment attempt alone does not confirm a reservation unless the authoritative booking semantics say so.

guardrails: state_written_on_stale_entity

useCases: a request for a specific time turned into a commitment or clearly not
a pending requirement resolved or lapsed before anything is committed

requires: a request to reserve an identified slot on an identified resource or service
insufficientAlone: a payment attempt for the booking, which funds it without confirming it unless the booking semantics explicitly make payment the confirming act
a slot being held, which protects capacity without committing anyone to anything

nodes.does: Capture the requested slot, the resource or service, the requester, the details the booking requires and the intent behind it

nodes.asks: Does a confirmed reservation already exist for this requester, resource and slot?

branches.label: It exists
branches.when: the same booking is already confirmed

branches.label: None
branches.when: no confirmed reservation covers it

nodes.state: already confirmed; the existing reservation stands and no second one was created
nodes.reEntry: a genuinely different booking is a different request. A resubmitted one resolves here rather than consuming a second slot

nodes.does: Re-read the slot's current state rather than trusting what the requester was shown. The availability they saw was true when it was rendered and may not be true now - under contention this is the single most common way two people end up holding one appointment, and only one of them finds out at the door

nodes.asks: Is the capacity still available to this requester?

branches.label: Available
branches.when: the slot is free, or is held by this requester

branches.label: Gone
branches.when: the capacity was taken between the query and the request

nodes.does: Record the request REJECTED with the reason. What is offered next is current availability rather than the set the requester was originally shown, which by definition contains at least one slot that no longer exists

nodes.on: a reservation that could not be made against the requested slot
carries: the resource, the service and the window the requester actually wanted
the explicit fact that nothing is held and nothing was committed

nodes.does: Validate the requester's eligibility, the details the booking requires and the dependencies its semantics define. Eligibility for a service and availability of a slot are different questions, and passing one says nothing about the other

nodes.asks: What do the booking requirements say?

branches.label: All satisfied
branches.when: eligibility, details and dependencies are all in place

branches.label: A further confirmation or dependency is required
branches.when: the booking semantics require an approval, a prepayment or a verification before it can commit

branches.label: Not met
branches.when: a requirement fails and cannot be satisfied for this request

nodes.does: Record PENDING_CONFIRMATION with exactly what is outstanding, and keep the capacity protected for as long as the booking semantics allow. Pending is not confirmed and the requester is told which - an appointment someone believes they have and does not have is worse than being asked to wait

after.rule: The pending window the booking semantics allow.

timeout.reason: capacity protected indefinitely for a booking that never completes is capacity taken from everyone who would have completed one

nodes.recheck: the the reservation request re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

nodes.asks: How did the pending requirement resolve?

branches.label: Resolved
branches.when: the outstanding confirmation or dependency completed

branches.label: Withdrawn
branches.when: the requester withdrew before it resolved

nodes.does: Record the request as lapsed and release any capacity protected for it. The slot returns to availability rather than staying reserved against a booking that never completed

nodes.state: request lapsed; capacity released and nothing committed
nodes.reEntry: a new request is evaluated against current availability, which may no longer include the slot that was being held

nodes.does: Create the commitment explicitly. Record CONFIRMED_RESERVATION with the slot, the resource, the parties and the terms. This is the point at which two parties owe each other a specific time - the customer arranges their day around it and the provider stops selling the slot - and nothing before it was that

nodes.on: a confirmed reservation with time still to run before it
carries: the commitment, its time and the parties
the explicit fact that the time is now fixed and preparation runs alongside it rather than deciding it
a fresh booking_id minted at a.confirm, deterministically derived from reservation_request_id, so SCH-174 can construct its own instance

guardrails: A request submitted is not a reservation confirmed.
Previously displayed availability may have changed and is revalidated rather than trusted.
A payment attempt alone does not confirm a reservation unless the authoritative booking semantics say so.
journeys.reusableRule: A reservation becomes confirmed only when the requested capacity and all required booking conditions have been authoritatively committed.

journeys.name: Reservation confirmed → prepare → upcoming or ready
journeys.purpose: Get the conditions for a successful service in place, without letting them move the time that was promised.

entity.scope: the confirmed reservation and the preparation running against it
entity.note: The preparation is subordinate to the booking. It can fail, and the booking stays confirmed while somebody decides what to do about it.

journeys.objective: Establish, by the pre-service checkpoint, that every prerequisite of a confirmed reservation is met - escalating what is not to ownership - so that the start-time journey begins from a booking that is actually ready.
eligibility: a reservation is confirmed with its prerequisites defined
the pre-service checkpoint for its service class is defined
no readiness instance is already open for this booking

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A booking that materially changes - moved, reassigned, cancelled - supersedes the open readiness instance; readiness is re-established against the new booking, never carried over.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: This journey sends nothing to the customer; prerequisites the customer must meet are prompted by the reminder journey (SCH-266), and what remains unmet at the checkpoint goes to ownership.

guardrails: start_on_unready_booking
readiness_carried_over_change

useCases: an appointment whose intake forms and access details must be in place before the checkpoint
a reservation whose provider-side prerequisites are tracked to a checkpoint

requires: a reservation confirmed with a scheduled time still in the future
insufficientAlone: a booking requested but not confirmed
a confirmation with no prerequisites defined, which has nothing to make ready
a reminder having been sent, which says nothing about readiness

nodes.does: Determine the pre-event requirements this booking actually has - forms, documents, instructions, resource preparation, verification, prepayment, a check-in requirement, provider preparation. Which apply is a property of this service rather than a standard list, and running the standard list asks people for things their appointment does not need

nodes.asks: Is each prerequisite already satisfied or already running?

branches.label: Already handled
branches.when: the requirement is satisfied, or a journey against it is already live

branches.label: Outstanding
branches.when: the requirement is neither satisfied nor in progress

nodes.does: Do not repeat it. A verification completed last month is completed, and re-running it opens a second journey against one requirement and asks the customer for something they have already given
Initiate each outstanding prerequisite on its own lifecycle. The reservation's time does not move while they run, and none of them owns the booking

after.rule: The checkpoint is the lead the pre-service policy defines ahead of the scheduled time for this service class; what is unmet at the checkpoint is escalated, not waited on further.

timeout.reason: the checkpoint is the last point at which an unresolved prerequisite can still be acted on. After it, the choice is to proceed unprepared or to disrupt someone's day at short notice

nodes.recheck: the booking and each prerequisite re-read at the checkpoint

nodes.asks: What resolved the wait?

branches.label: Preparation complete
branches.when: every prerequisite finished before the checkpoint

branches.label: The booking changed
branches.when: the reservation was rescheduled, cancelled or materially altered

nodes.state: preparation superseded by a change to the booking
nodes.reEntry: the reschedule or cancellation owns what happens next. Preparation is re-derived against the new booking rather than carried across, because a different time can need different things

nodes.asks: Is an unresolved prerequisite critical to delivering the service?

branches.label: Critical
branches.when: the service cannot be delivered properly without it

branches.label: Not critical
branches.when: the service can proceed and the requirement can follow

nodes.does: Record AT_RISK or HOLD according to policy, naming the prerequisite. The confirmed time is not moved here - a preparation failing is a reason to escalate or to contact someone, and moving an appointment is a booking decision that belongs to the reschedule lifecycle

nodes.on: a critical prerequisite unresolved at the pre-service checkpoint
carries: the booking, its time and exactly which prerequisite is missing
the explicit fact that the reservation remains confirmed and no time has been changed

nodes.does: Record READY or UPCOMING with which prerequisites are complete and which are outstanding but not critical. A reminder having been sent is recorded separately from preparation being complete, because the first is something we did and the second is something that happened

nodes.state: READY or UPCOMING; the commitment stands and its conditions are in the state recorded
nodes.reEntry: the revalidation at service time reads the booking's current state rather than this readiness record, which was true when it was written

guardrails: A reminder sent is not preparation complete.
Duplicate prerequisite journeys are not created for a requirement already satisfied or running.
Preparation never alters the confirmed time unless the booking rules themselves require it.
journeys.reusableRule: A confirmed reservation should preserve the time commitment while independently preparing the conditions required for successful service delivery.

journeys.name: Reschedule request → recheck availability → move, reject or preserve original
journeys.purpose: Move a commitment to a new time without ever leaving the customer holding neither.

entity.scope: the existing reservation and the reschedule request raised against it
entity.note: One reservation throughout, carrying every time it has held. A reschedule is a move recorded on it rather than a cancellation followed by a new booking.

distinctFrom.because: SUB-166 changes the terms of a continuing relationship. This moves one specific occurrence to a different time or resource, and its whole difficulty is contention for the replacement - which terms changes never have.

journeys.objective: Move a commitment to a new time without ever leaving the customer holding neither.
eligibility: an authorized request to move an existing confirmed reservation
no instance of this journey is already open for the the existing reservation and the reschedule request raised against it
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A reschedule requested is not a reschedule completed.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: The original slot is never released before the replacement is secured unless policy explicitly requires it.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: The historical original time remains auditable.

guardrails: state_written_on_stale_entity

useCases: a commitment moved without the customer ever holding neither
a replacement lost to contention, leaving the original intact

requires: an authorized request to move an existing confirmed reservation
insufficientAlone: someone viewing other times, which is looking rather than asking to move

nodes.does: Keep the original reservation confirmed and intact while the replacement is evaluated. Releasing it first is the mistake this journey exists to prevent - the customer ends up with no appointment at all, and the slot they had is gone by the time anyone realises the replacement was not available
Search and validate the target availability against current authoritative capacity, for the resource and service the original booking actually requires

nodes.asks: Is a valid replacement available?

branches.label: One exists
branches.when: a slot satisfying the booking's requirements is currently free

branches.label: None
branches.when: nothing valid is available in the requested window

nodes.does: Record the reschedule as not possible and leave the original reservation exactly as it was. The customer still has their appointment, which is the position they were in before they asked - and is a far better outcome than the alternative

nodes.state: original reservation preserved unchanged; no move took place
nodes.reEntry: the reschedule can be attempted again against different availability. Cancelling the original is a separate decision the customer makes explicitly

nodes.does: Secure the new slot under the same scheduling semantics as an original booking - a hold and then a confirmation, or a direct commitment where the resource permits. The replacement has to be genuinely committed before anything is given up

nodes.asks: Was the replacement actually secured?

branches.label: Secured
branches.when: the new slot is committed to this reservation

branches.label: Lost to contention
branches.when: the slot was taken between finding it and securing it

nodes.does: Transfer the commitment to the new slot, recording the original time, the new one and the fact that this reservation moved. The original time stays readable - a reservation that only ever shows its current time cannot answer how many times it was moved, which is the first thing anyone investigating a service problem wants to know
Release the original slot, and only now. Capacity returns to availability at the point the replacement is real, which is the ordering the whole journey exists to enforce

Reconcile everything that pointed at the old time - the resource, the provider, the instructions, the prepayment, the preparation tasks and every queued notification. A reminder still aimed at the original time will fire, and the customer will arrive on the wrong day because of it

nodes.asks: Does the new time or resource change what preparation is required?

branches.label: It changes
branches.when: a different provider, location or lead time alters the prerequisites

branches.label: Unchanged
branches.when: the same preparation applies and is already in the state it was

nodes.on: a rescheduled booking whose preparation requirements have changed
carries: the new time and resource, and which prerequisites are already satisfied
the explicit instruction not to re-request what the customer has already provided

nodes.state: moved; the new time is committed and the original is preserved in the record
nodes.reEntry: a further move is a new reschedule against this reservation, and it joins the same history rather than replacing it

guardrails: A reschedule requested is not a reschedule completed.
The original slot is never released before the replacement is secured unless policy explicitly requires it.
The historical original time remains auditable.
journeys.reusableRule: Rescheduling should preserve the existing commitment until a valid replacement commitment has been successfully established.

journeys.name: Reservation cancellation → stop commitment → release capacity → reconcile
journeys.purpose: End a future time commitment cleanly, returning the capacity and leaving the money to be decided elsewhere.

entity.scope: the reservation and the cancellation acting on it
entity.note: The reservation survives its own cancellation as a record. A released slot says something about capacity and nothing about whether the appointment existed.

distinctFrom.because: FUL-150 cancels what remains of a generic fulfillment obligation. This ends a specific future time commitment, which releases capacity someone else can use and turns on timing relative to the appointment rather than on remaining scope.

journeys.objective: End a future time commitment cleanly, returning the capacity and leaving the money to be decided elsewhere.
eligibility: an authorized cancellation of a confirmed reservation, taking effect
no instance of this journey is already open for the the reservation and the cancellation acting on it
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A cancellation requested is not a cancellation effective.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A cancellation is not a no-show.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Cancellation never deletes reservation history.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: The refund or fee decision belongs to the financial lifecycle rather than to this one.

guardrails: state_written_on_stale_entity

useCases: a future commitment ended cleanly with capacity returned
the refund or fee decided elsewhere

requires: an authorized cancellation of a confirmed reservation, taking effect
insufficientAlone: a cancellation requested, which is a request and may be blocked or may be for a later effective time
someone not responding to a reminder, which is silence rather than a cancellation

nodes.does: Record the actor and source, the reason, the effective time, the reservation's state at cancellation, and the timing relative to the scheduled service. The timing is what most cancellation policies turn on, and it has to be recorded at the moment rather than reconstructed afterwards from timestamps that mean something else

nodes.asks: Which side cancelled?

branches.label: The customer or requester
branches.when: the cancellation originates from the party who booked

branches.label: The provider or resource side
branches.when: the cancellation originates because we cannot deliver

nodes.on: a cancellation originating on the provider side
carries: the reservation, the failure and its scope
the explicit instruction that the customer is not recorded as having cancelled and is never classified as a no-show

nodes.does: Mark the reservation CANCELLED, preserving everything about it - the original booking, the times it held, the preparation that ran. The history is not deleted, because a released slot is capacity returning to the pool and says nothing about whether the appointment ever existed

Release the reserved capacity where the booking semantics permit it. The release is idempotent - an already-released reservation returns capacity once rather than once per attempt, and the difference shows up as two people booked into one room

Stop the obsolete preparation, reminders and check-in actions. A reminder for a cancelled appointment brings someone to a place where nobody is expecting them, which is the most avoidable failure in this whole category

nodes.asks: Is an external provider or booking system holding this reservation?

branches.label: It is
branches.when: the slot exists in a system outside our own

branches.label: It is not
branches.when: the reservation is entirely internal

nodes.does: Verify the cancellation actually took effect on the external side. A cancellation we recorded and they did not leaves them holding a slot we have released, and both sides discover it when someone arrives

nodes.asks: Did the external side confirm the cancellation?

branches.label: Confirmed
branches.when: the external system authoritatively reports it cancelled

branches.label: Not confirmed
branches.when: the external side is unreachable, silent or still shows it booked

nodes.on: a cancellation the external booking system has not confirmed
carries: the reservation, its external reference and what the external side last reported
the explicit fact that capacity was released locally and may still be held externally

nodes.asks: Does the cancellation carry a financial consequence?

branches.label: A refund or credit may be due
branches.when: the booking was paid for and the terms may return some or all of it

branches.label: A cancellation fee applies
branches.when: the terms create a charge given the timing of the cancellation

branches.label: Neither
branches.when: nothing was paid and the terms create no charge

nodes.on: a cancelled reservation that was paid for
carries: what was paid, the cancellation timing and the terms that govern it
the explicit fact that this journey ended the booking and decided nothing about whether money is owed

nodes.on: a cancellation the terms attach a fee to
carries: the fee basis, the cancellation timing and the term that creates it
the explicit fact that no fee amount was invented here - the terms define it or there is no fee

nodes.state: CANCELLED; capacity released, history preserved, nothing owed
nodes.reEntry: a new booking is a new reservation rather than this one resuming, and this cancellation stays part of the record either way

guardrails: A cancellation requested is not a cancellation effective.
A cancellation is not a no-show.
Cancellation never deletes reservation history.
The refund or fee decision belongs to the financial lifecycle rather than to this one.
journeys.reusableRule: Reservation cancellation ends the future time-bound commitment while independently reconciling released capacity and any resulting financial obligations.

journeys.name: Scheduled time approaches → revalidate → check in, start or exception
journeys.purpose: Start a service from what the booking is now, not from a confirmation issued weeks ago.

entity.scope: the confirmed reservation and the occurrence about to begin
entity.note: The scheduled job carries the booking version it was created against. Everything it does begins with comparing that against the booking as it now stands.

journeys.objective: Start a service from what the booking is at its start time, and establish attendance from evidence rather than from the fact that a reminder went out.
eligibility: the booking's pre-start window has been reached in the booking's own local time
the booking was confirmed and has not been superseded by a later confirmation

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A start that no longer matches authoritative state - cancelled, moved, reassigned - is suppressed: no service is begun and no attendance is recorded against a booking that is not the one the person holds.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A cancellation arriving inside the start window is a cancellation, not a no-show; it hands to cancellation reconciliation and nothing here treats it as a miss.

guardrails: service_started_on_stale_booking
attendance_recorded_without_evidence

useCases: an appointment reaching its start time
a reservation whose arrival must be established before service begins

requires: the defined pre-start or start window for a scheduled occurrence being reached
insufficientAlone: a reminder having been sent, which says nothing about the start
the scheduled time itself passing - that is the arrival window, not its opening
a provider-side readiness check, which SCH-174 owns

nodes.does: Re-read the booking from authoritative current state - is the reservation still confirmed, is the resource or provider available, are the required prerequisites met, does eligibility still hold where it is required, is there a material operational restriction. The confirmation from three weeks ago is not evidence about now, and this job is running because of a clock rather than because anything was checked

nodes.asks: Is the reservation still valid?

branches.label: Still confirmed
branches.when: the booking stands as scheduled

branches.label: Cancelled or rescheduled since
branches.when: the booking has moved or ended since the job was scheduled

nodes.does: Record the scheduled job as suppressed, naming what superseded it. A stale start job revives a cancelled booking, allocates a provider to it, and then produces a no-show for someone who cancelled correctly - three wrong outcomes from one unchecked assumption

nodes.state: stale start suppressed; no service was begun and no attendance state was written
nodes.reEntry: the booking's current version has its own scheduled occurrence, which revalidates on its own terms when it arrives

nodes.asks: Can the provider or resource actually deliver?

branches.label: They can
branches.when: the assigned provider and resource are available and able

branches.label: They cannot
branches.when: the provider is unavailable, the resource failed, or the location cannot host it

nodes.on: a booking that cannot be delivered by its assigned provider or resource
carries: the reservation, its time and what has failed
the explicit instruction that the customer's obligation stands and they are not the cause

nodes.asks: Are the critical prerequisites met?

branches.label: Met
branches.when: everything the service requires to start properly is in place

branches.label: Missing
branches.when: a prerequisite the service cannot proceed without is unresolved

nodes.does: Record the occurrence as blocked at service time with the missing prerequisite, and do not start. Starting a service whose prerequisite is missing produces a partial or invalid delivery, which then needs a remedy - and the customer has spent the appointment either way

nodes.on: a service blocked at its own start time
carries: the booking, the missing prerequisite and the fact that the customer is present or expected
the explicit fact that nothing was started and no attendance outcome was recorded

nodes.does: Record READY_TO_START. The scheduled time arriving is not the service starting - the two are kept apart because everything between them can still fail, and most of what fails in this category fails exactly here

after.rule: The arrival window is the tolerance after the scheduled start that the service's own attendance semantics allow. Its end is what turns a late arrival into a miss.

default.value: scheduled_at plus the arrival tolerance policy records

timeout.reason: the arrival window is what makes a missed appointment a fact rather than an assumption. Concluding before it closes records a no-show against someone who is running late and about to walk in

nodes.recheck: the booking re-read at the end of the window: still the same commitment, and attendance evidence from the source that records it

nodes.asks: What happened inside the arrival window?

branches.label: Attended
branches.when: attendance or check-in was authoritatively established

branches.label: Cancelled inside the window
branches.when: the booking was cancelled after the start window opened

nodes.on: attendance established for a revalidated booking
carries: the booking, its scope and the prerequisites that were confirmed at start
the explicit fact that attendance says the interaction began and nothing about its outcome

nodes.on: a cancellation arriving inside the start window
carries: the cancellation timing relative to the scheduled service, which is what its terms turn on

nodes.on: an arrival window closing with no attendance established
carries: the booking, the window that closed and the fact that it was revalidated and the provider was able
the explicit instruction that this is not yet a no-show - the contradicting explanations have not been excluded

guardrails: The scheduled time being reached is not the service having started.
Interaction with a reminder is not attendance.
A stale scheduled job never revives a cancelled or rescheduled reservation.
journeys.reusableRule: A scheduled commitment should begin only after the reservation and its critical dependencies are revalidated at the time of service.

journeys.name: Attendance or service start → complete, partial or interrupted
journeys.purpose: Separate the fact that someone turned up from the question of whether they got what they came for.

entity.scope: the reservation occurrence and the service delivered inside it
entity.note: Attendance is about the occurrence. Completion is about the obligation. One appointment can end with the first true and the second false.

journeys.objective: Separate the fact that someone turned up from the question of whether they got what they came for.
eligibility: attendance or service commencement established authoritatively
no instance of this journey is already open for the the reservation occurrence and the service delivered inside it
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Check-in is not service completed.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Attendance is not a successful outcome.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Partial service is never represented as full completion.

guardrails: state_written_on_stale_entity

useCases: turning up separated from getting what they came for
a partial or interrupted service routed to its remedy or reschedule

requires: attendance or service commencement established authoritatively
insufficientAlone: a reminder being opened or clicked, which is interest rather than attendance
arriving at a location, where the booking semantics require a check-in to establish attendance

nodes.does: Record IN_SERVICE or ATTENDED. The interaction is happening and nothing about its outcome is known yet
Track the scope actually delivered, where the service has a scope worth tracking. What is recorded is what was delivered rather than the fact that the appointment took place

after.rule: The scheduled duration plus its tolerance.

timeout.reason: an occurrence that started and was never concluded is unknown rather than complete, and closing it as complete makes an unfulfilled service invisible to everyone downstream

nodes.recheck: the the reservation occurrence and the service delivered inside it re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

nodes.does: Record the occurrence's outcome as unknown - someone attended and what happened afterwards was never recorded. This is not completion, and treating it as completion closes an obligation nobody confirmed was met

nodes.on: an occurrence that began and whose outcome was never established
carries: the booking, the attendance record and the point at which the trail stops
the explicit fact that no completion was recorded and none should be inferred

nodes.asks: How did the service end?

branches.label: Fully delivered
branches.when: the whole scheduled service was delivered

branches.label: Partly delivered
branches.when: some of the scheduled scope was delivered and some was not

branches.label: Interrupted
branches.when: delivery started and stopped before finishing

branches.label: Could not proceed after arrival
branches.when: the customer was present and the service never began

nodes.does: Record COMPLETED. The scheduled obligation was met, which is a different claim from the appointment having happened

nodes.state: COMPLETED; attendance and delivery both established
nodes.reEntry: a problem raised afterwards about what was delivered is a post-completion issue and is assessed on its own terms

nodes.does: Record PARTIALLY_COMPLETED with exactly what was delivered and what remains. Attendance is not a successful outcome, and a half-delivered service recorded as complete closes something the customer is still owed - they will find out, and they will find out later than we could have told them

nodes.on: a scheduled service delivered only in part
carries: the delivered scope and the remaining obligation, separately
the explicit fact that the appointment occurred, so this is a shortfall rather than a missed service

nodes.does: Record the interruption with its cause and the point at which delivery stopped

attemptBudget.rule: This loop runs against a budget fixed when the instance opened; when it is spent the instance takes its timeout path (GLB-24).

nodes.asks: What does the interruption allow?

branches.label: Resuming now
branches.when: the cause cleared and the remaining scope fits inside the occurrence

branches.label: Another appointment
branches.when: the remaining scope needs a separate scheduled occurrence

branches.label: A remedy
branches.when: the shortfall needs resolving rather than repeating

nodes.does: Resume the same occurrence and continue tracking delivered scope. The wait's timeout is the scheduled duration and does not extend, so an occurrence that keeps stopping reaches its limit rather than running indefinitely

nodes.on: remaining scope needing a further scheduled occurrence
carries: what was delivered in this occurrence and what the next one has to cover
the explicit fact that this occurrence is not a no-show and not a cancellation

nodes.does: Record that attendance happened and the service did not. This is a different fact from a no-show and from a cancellation - the customer did everything asked of them and left with nothing, which is the outcome most likely to be recorded wrongly and least likely to be forgotten by them

nodes.asks: Why could it not proceed?

branches.label: The provider or resource side
branches.when: the provider, equipment, location or capacity failed at the point of delivery

branches.label: Something the customer had to bring
branches.when: a required document, condition or preparation the customer owns was absent

nodes.on: a service that could not proceed for provider-side reasons after the customer arrived
carries: the attendance record, which stands, and what failed on our side
the explicit instruction that the customer is never classified as a no-show for this

nodes.on: a service that could not proceed because a customer-side requirement was absent
carries: the attendance record and the requirement that was missing
the explicit fact that they attended, which is what separates this from a no-show

guardrails: Check-in is not service completed.
Attendance is not a successful outcome.
Partial service is never represented as full completion.
journeys.reusableRule: Attendance establishes that the scheduled interaction occurred; completion depends on the actual service obligation being delivered.

journeys.name: No-show or missed appointment → validate → rebook, close or consequence
journeys.purpose: Establish that one confirmed booking did not happen because the customer did not attend, having ruled out every other explanation.

entity.scope: the single reservation occurrence that did not take place
entity.note: One occurrence. Nothing here says anything about the customer's engagement, their history or their relationship - it is a fact about one appointment.

distinctFrom.because: RET-22 reads a pattern of expected usage not happening across a relationship. This is the non-occurrence of one specific confirmed booking at one specific time, and it is established by exclusion rather than by observing a trend.

journeys.objective: Establish that one confirmed booking did not happen because the customer did not attend, having ruled out every other explanation.
eligibility: a confirmed occurrence whose service and arrival windows have both closed with no commencement established
no instance of this journey is already open for the the single reservation occurrence that did not take place
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A no-show is never inferred before the relevant service and arrival windows close.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A no-show is not a cancellation.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Fees and penalties are never invented.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A late-arriving attendance event reconciles against the recorded no-show state.

guardrails: state_written_on_stale_entity

useCases: a no-show established only after every other explanation is ruled out
a late arrival inside the grace the semantics allow

requires: a confirmed occurrence whose service and arrival windows have both closed with no commencement established
insufficientAlone: the scheduled start time having passed, which does not close the arrival window and concludes nothing about someone who is running late

nodes.does: Re-read the reservation's latest events before concluding anything. The missed-appointment job runs on a clock and the booking may have moved under it minutes earlier - this check is the difference between a fact and an accusation

nodes.asks: Was the booking cancelled or rescheduled?

branches.label: It was
branches.when: a cancellation or reschedule exists against this occurrence

branches.label: It stands
branches.when: the booking was confirmed and unchanged through its window

nodes.does: Suppress the no-show classification entirely. Recording one against someone who cancelled correctly, or who is booked for next Tuesday, attaches a penalty and a history to behaviour that was exactly right - and it is the kind of error people remember and repeat to others

nodes.state: no-show suppressed; the booking was cancelled or moved and nothing is attributed
nodes.reEntry: the rescheduled occurrence has its own window and is assessed on its own terms when it arrives

nodes.asks: Could the provider or resource actually have delivered?

branches.label: They could
branches.when: the provider and resource were available and able throughout the window

branches.label: They could not
branches.when: the provider was unavailable, the resource failed or the location could not host it

nodes.on: a missed occurrence the provider side could not have delivered
carries: the occurrence and what failed on our side
the explicit instruction that this is a provider failure and not a customer no-show, which decides who bears the consequence

nodes.asks: Do the booking's own semantics define what counts as failing to attend?

branches.label: Defined
branches.when: a grace period, a late-arrival rule and any partial-attendance rule are stated

branches.label: Not defined
branches.when: nothing authoritative states what counts as a no-show for this service

nodes.on: a missed occurrence with no defined attendance semantics
carries: the booking, the windows that closed and what is known about the customer's side
the explicit fact that no grace period or attendance rule was invented, particularly where a fee would follow from it

nodes.asks: Did the customer fail to attend under those semantics?

branches.label: They did not attend
branches.when: no arrival occurred inside the grace the semantics allow

branches.label: They attended late, within the grace
branches.when: arrival happened inside the allowance the semantics define

nodes.on: an arrival inside the grace period the semantics allow
carries: the arrival and how late it was, which may change the deliverable scope
the explicit fact that this is attendance rather than a no-show

nodes.does: Record NO_SHOW with the semantics it was judged under and the window that closed. This is the non-occurrence of one confirmed booking and nothing more - it is not a statement about the customer's engagement, their loyalty or their relationship, and journeys reading it should not treat it as one

nodes.asks: What does policy define as the next action?

branches.label: Rebooking is offered
branches.when: the service is one where missing it means booking again

branches.label: A financial consequence applies
branches.when: the terms attach a fee or a forfeit to a missed appointment

branches.label: Closure
branches.when: policy defines no further action

nodes.on: a missed appointment policy allows to be rebooked
carries: the service and resource the original booking needed
the explicit fact that a new booking is a new commitment and does not undo the missed one

nodes.on: a no-show the terms attach a charge to
carries: the term that creates the charge and the semantics the no-show was judged under
the explicit fact that no fee was invented here, and that a late attendance event arriving afterwards has to reconcile against this

nodes.state: NO_SHOW recorded; no consequence beyond the record
nodes.reEntry: an attendance event arriving after this reconciles against the recorded no-show rather than being ignored - a late system update is a reason to correct the record, not evidence that the record was right

guardrails: A no-show is never inferred before the relevant service and arrival windows close.
A no-show is not a cancellation.
Fees and penalties are never invented.
A late-arriving attendance event reconciles against the recorded no-show state.
journeys.reusableRule: A no-show should be recorded only after excluding cancellation, rescheduling and provider-side failure as explanations for the missed scheduled service.

journeys.name: Provider or resource cancellation → reallocate → reschedule, remedy or cancel
journeys.purpose: Recover a commitment we cannot keep, without any of the cost landing on the person who was ready.

entity.scope: the affected reservations and the provider or resource failure behind them
entity.note: The scope is every booking the failure touches. A closed location is not one cancellation, and treating it as one leaves the rest to be discovered by the people who turn up.

distinctFrom.because: FUL-145 handles a generic fulfillment exception. This carries the scheduling-specific recovery: the same time with a different provider, a different time with the same commitment, and the rule that the customer is never recorded as the cause.

journeys.objective: Recover a commitment we cannot keep, without any of the cost landing on the person who was ready.
eligibility: a confirmed reservation that can no longer be fulfilled by its assigned provider or resource - unavailability, resource failure, location closure, withdrawn capacity or an operational incident
no instance of this journey is already open for the the affected reservations and the provider or resource failure behind them
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A provider cancellation is not a customer cancellation.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: An affected customer is never classified as a no-show.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A replacement must satisfy the service's actual requirements rather than merely being available.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Financial and remedy consequences remain separate lifecycle decisions.

value.rule: Every touch runs against a budget fixed when the instance opened; the budget is the plan's own length, and no touch is repeated because nothing could tell whether it arrived.

default.applicableWhen: GLB-24; the graph's own touch count

cooldown.rule: This journey is per the affected reservations and the provider or resource failure behind them; a later instance concerns a different the affected reservations and the provider or resource failure behind them and no cooldown applies between them.

default.applicableWhen: the entity note: one instance per entity

roles.when: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it
an asserted time bound lies inside the urgent horizon and permission for messages on this channel is recorded

touches.purpose: Tell them what changed, distinguished from a reschedule because the time did not move.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: Tell the customer the confirmed commitment can no longer be kept, that the failure is ours and not theirs, and that they are not recorded as having cancelled or missed it.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

guardrails: complaint
message_after_success
unsubscribe

useCases: a commitment we cannot keep recovered without the cost landing on the person who was ready
an equivalent replacement at the same time, told only where it changes something for them

requires: a confirmed reservation that can no longer be fulfilled by its assigned provider or resource - unavailability, resource failure, location closure, withdrawn capacity or an operational incident
insufficientAlone: a customer asking to move the booking, which is their reschedule and not our failure
a provider's tentative doubt that has not become an inability

nodes.does: Identify every reservation the failure affects, and its scope. A closed location is not one cancellation - treating it as one produces a correct outcome for the booking that raised the alarm and silence for the forty behind it, each of whom finds out at the door

Record that the failure is provider-side. Whatever follows, the customer is not marked as having cancelled and is never classified as a no-show - they were available and the service was not, and the record has to say so before anything else touches this booking

nodes.asks: Is an equivalent replacement available for the same time?

branches.label: Available and permitted
branches.when: another provider or resource can deliver the booked service at the booked time, and the rules allow substituting

branches.label: Not at this time
branches.when: nothing equivalent is free, or substitution is not permitted for this service

nodes.does: Reallocate to the replacement, preserving the commitment and the time. The replacement has to actually satisfy the service's requirements - a different provider who cannot perform the booked service is not a replacement, and substituting one moves the failure from before the appointment to during it
Release the obsolete allocation, idempotently. The original resource returns to availability once, whatever number of times the release is attempted

nodes.asks: Does the reallocation change anything the customer needs to know?

branches.label: It does
branches.when: the provider, the location or the preparation is different

branches.label: It does not
branches.when: nothing visible to the customer changed

nodes.does: Tell them what changed, distinguished from a reschedule because the time did not move. Someone who reads 'your appointment has changed' and assumes the time moved will miss an appointment we successfully saved

nodes.state: reallocated; the time and the commitment both stand
nodes.reEntry: the booking continues to its scheduled occurrence and revalidates there like any other

nodes.asks: Do the applicable decision rules permit rescheduling this booking?

branches.label: Permitted
branches.when: the service can be delivered at another time and the rules allow moving it

branches.label: Not permitted
branches.when: the service was time-specific, or the rules do not allow it to move

nodes.on: a provider-side failure that can be recovered at another time
carries: the original commitment and the requirements a replacement slot has to satisfy
the explicit fact that this move originates on our side, which changes what the customer may be offered and what they may be charged

nodes.does: Cancel the affected reservation, recorded as provider-side. Provider cancellation and customer cancellation are different terminal states with different consequences, and collapsing them charges a cancellation fee to someone whose appointment we could not keep
Release the allocation and stop the obsolete preparation, reminders and check-in actions. A reminder for an appointment we cancelled brings the customer in for a service that has no provider waiting

Tell the customer the confirmed commitment can no longer be kept, that the failure is ours and not theirs, and that they are not recorded as having cancelled or missed it. Sent before any remedy or refund is worked out - waiting for the consequence means the person finds out their booking is gone from a message about money

nodes.asks: What does the failure leave to answer for?

branches.label: An unresolved service obligation
branches.when: the customer still needs the service and it has not been delivered

branches.label: Money to return
branches.when: the booking was paid for or a fee was taken

branches.label: Neither
branches.when: nothing was owed and nothing was paid

nodes.on: a service obligation left unresolved by a provider-side failure
carries: the obligation as it stands and the fact that the customer did nothing wrong - provider_failure_id stands in for REM-157's obligation_id
the explicit fact that the impact of the failure is a separate question from the obligation, and compensation is decided on its own terms
a fresh issue_id, minted at this handoff and deterministically derived from provider_failure_id - SCH-180 has no issue concept of its own, so REM-157's instance is opened here rather than carried

nodes.on: a provider-cancelled booking that was paid for
carries: what was paid and the fact that the cancellation was ours
the explicit fact that no cancellation fee applies to a booking the provider could not keep
a fresh refund_request_id, minted at this handoff and deterministically derived from provider_failure_id

nodes.state: cancelled on the provider side; recorded as ours, with nothing attributed to the customer
nodes.reEntry: a new booking is a new commitment. This cancellation stays in the record as a provider failure, which is what any later question about the customer's booking history depends on

guardrails: A provider cancellation is not a customer cancellation.
An affected customer is never classified as a no-show.
A replacement must satisfy the service's actual requirements rather than merely being available.
Financial and remedy consequences remain separate lifecycle decisions.
journeys.reusableRule: Provider-side inability should preserve the customer's underlying service obligation and attempt recovery before treating the reservation as simply cancelled.

journeys.name: Appointment approaching → prerequisites and revalidation → ready, reminded or at risk
journeys.purpose: Get the customer's side of a confirmed commitment done before the commitment arrives, and send the reminder from what the booking is at that moment rather than from what it was when it was made.

entity.scope: the confirmed booking occurrence plus the prerequisites its customer owes against it
entity.note: One occurrence, one instance. Each occurrence of a recurring commitment revalidates and reminds on its own.

supersession.label: CANONICAL_RULE
supersession.text: A rescheduled occurrence is the same instance re-timed from the new scheduled time. A cancellation or a material change supersedes it; the replacement booking runs its own readiness from its own confirmation.

distinctFrom.because: SCH-174 prepares the conditions and records a reminder having been sent as somebody else's fact. This journey is that somebody, and it never moves the confirmed time.
SCH-177 revalidates at the pre-start point in order to start the service. This revalidates at the same point in order to decide whether anything should be sent at all.

journeys.objective: Get the customer's side of a confirmed commitment done before it arrives, and remind them from what the booking is at the moment of sending.
eligibility: the booking is confirmed in the system of record and its scheduled time is in the future
the customer is contactable for service messages about this booking
no reminder has been sent for this occurrence
hard gates (GLB-31) permit service communication to this person

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Exit on cancellation or material change. A reminder is never built from a stored copy of the booking: every touch re-reads authoritative state first, which is how somebody who cancelled is not told to turn up.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: One reminder per occurrence. A second reminder sent because nothing could tell whether the first arrived is what teaches people to stop reading them.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Where the confirmation already falls inside the pre-start window, no prerequisite prompt is sent; the journey goes straight to revalidation and the reminder.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Deduplicated by booking and occurrence against the confirmation (SCH-277) and any reschedule notice (SCH-180) about the same booking.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Hard gates (GLB-31) apply. The service pressure class deduplicates against other service messages about this booking; it does not ration a reminder the person is owed.

value.rule: A prerequisite prompt and one reminder per occurrence. The at-risk notice is an obligation to the person and sits outside the cap.

default.applicableWhen: GLB-24 and this journey's own guardrail: one reminder per occurrence

cooldown.rule: Per occurrence. The next occurrence of a recurring commitment is its own instance and no cooldown applies between occurrences.

default.applicableWhen: the entity note: each further occurrence of a recurring commitment is its own instance

roles.when: the scheduled time is within the same day, or a critical prerequisite is outstanding, and permission for service SMS is recorded
the message lists things to read and do over time, or no urgent channel is permitted
the person is in the product

touches.purpose: Every outstanding prerequisite, whose it is and the point by which each must be done - in one message rather than one per requirement.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: The reminder plus the one thing that will stop this going ahead, with the last point at which it can still be done. The confirmed time is not moved.
touches.priorityReason: the service cannot be delivered without this prerequisite - not saying so costs the person the appointment
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: The time, the place or joining route, and anything still outstanding that does not block the service.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

guardrails: complaint
reminder_sent_for_cancelled_booking
duplicate_reminder_per_occurrence

useCases: a confirmed appointment with forms, documents or payments the customer must complete first
a class, delivery slot or reservation with a joining route to restate
a recurring commitment whose every occurrence needs its own reminder

requires: a confirmed booking with a scheduled time
at least one prerequisite recorded as outstanding and owned by the customer
insufficientAlone: a request that has not been confirmed
a prerequisite owned by the provider rather than by the customer

nodes.asks: Is there enough time left for a prompt to be worth sending?

branches.label: Time remains
branches.when: the scheduled time is far enough out that an outstanding prerequisite could still be completed

branches.label: Too close to prompt
branches.when: the booking is already inside its pre-start window

nodes.does: Name every outstanding prerequisite, whose it is and the point by which it has to be done, in one message rather than one message per requirement. Somebody with three things to do has one problem, and splitting it into three makes it look like three systems that do not talk

after.rule: The reminder is built at the pre-start point so it reflects the booking as it is then. The point is set from how long the customer's own preparation takes, not from how long ago the booking was made.

default.applicableWhen: appointments the customer must prepare for
default.avoidWhen: same-day bookings - the pre-start point is whatever time remains between confirmation and start

timeout.reason: the pre-start point is where the booking is read again, and anything sent past it is about a commitment that may no longer exist

nodes.recheck: the booking re-read from authoritative state: still confirmed, same time, same provider, and which prerequisites are outstanding now

nodes.asks: What resolved the wait?

branches.label: All complete
branches.when: every prerequisite the customer owed is recorded satisfied

branches.label: Booking changed
branches.when: the booking was cancelled, moved or materially changed

after.rule: The same pre-start point: the reminder is sent against the booking as it is at that moment.

default.applicableWhen: appointments the customer must prepare for

timeout.reason: the reminder exists to arrive before the commitment; after it there is nothing left to remind anybody about

nodes.recheck: the booking re-read from authoritative state before either the at-risk notice or the reminder is built

nodes.does: Re-read the booking from authoritative current state before anything is sent - still confirmed, same time, same provider, and which prerequisites are outstanding now. A reminder generated from the booking as it was is how somebody who cancelled correctly gets told to turn up

nodes.asks: Does the booking still stand as it was just read?

branches.label: Still valid
branches.when: the booking is confirmed, at the time recorded, and deliverable

branches.label: Cancelled, moved or superseded
branches.when: current state no longer matches the booking this reminder was scheduled against

nodes.asks: Is anything outstanding that would stop the service happening?

branches.label: Critical prerequisite missing
branches.when: a requirement the service cannot be delivered without is still not satisfied

branches.label: Nothing critical outstanding
branches.when: everything blocking is done, whatever remains is not blocking

nodes.does: Send the reminder and name the one thing that will stop this going ahead, with the last point at which it can still be done. The confirmed time is not moved here - a prerequisite failing is a reason to warn somebody, not a reason to rewrite a commitment they have planned around

nodes.on: a booking reaching its pre-start point with a critical prerequisite still outstanding
carries: which prerequisite is missing and when it was last prompted
that the customer has been told, and what they were told

nodes.does: Remind them of the time, the place or joining route, and anything still outstanding that does not block it. One reminder per occurrence - a second one sent because nothing could tell that the first arrived is how people stop reading them

nodes.on: reminded against a revalidated booking; the start window and attendance belong to pre-service revalidation
carries: the booking and occurrence
what the reminder said and when it was sent
the prerequisites still outstanding that do not block the service
suppresses: any further reminder for this occurrence

nodes.state: superseded; the booking changed before the reminder was due
nodes.reEntry: the booking that replaced it runs its own readiness from its own confirmation

guardrails: Nothing is sent without re-reading the booking at send time. The scheduled job carries the version it was built against, and that version is a claim rather than a fact.
A reminder having been sent is never recorded as preparation being complete.
Interaction with a reminder is not attendance and is not a prerequisite satisfied.
Preparation never moves the confirmed time. A failing condition escalates; it does not reschedule.
One reminder per occurrence, and outstanding requirements are named together rather than one message each.
journeys.reusableRule: A reminder is only as true as the moment it is built, so it is built at the moment it is sent.

journeys.name: Reservation requested → validate capacity → confirm, re-offer or lapse
journeys.purpose: Tell the requester whether the specific time they asked for is now a commitment, and where it is not, offer the nearest time that actually exists - because the availability they were shown earlier was a picture and never a hold.

entity.scope: the reservation request, the requester, and the resource and slot it names
entity.note: One instance per request. A retried submission is the same request rather than a second claim on the same capacity.

distinctFrom.because: SCH-173 revalidates capacity and decides whether a commitment exists. This journey carries that outcome to the requester and never states a confirmation the booking record does not hold.

journeys.objective: Tell the requester whether the specific time they asked for is now a commitment, and where it is not, offer the nearest time that actually exists - because the availability they were shown earlier was a picture and never a hold.
eligibility: a reservation request recorded against a named requester, resource and slot
a permitted contact point for a booking notice
no instance of this journey is already open for the the reservation request
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.text: A request acknowledged is never worded as a request confirmed.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: What is offered after a failure is current availability, never the set the requester was originally shown.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Nothing is described as held unless the booking semantics actually hold it.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A lapse is stated. Silence after a request is read as a commitment.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: The confirmation restates the concrete slot every time. A reference is not a time and a place.

touches.purpose: State the committed slot, the resource and the terms concretely - the date, the time, the place, what is needed on arrival.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: Say the requested time is gone, name the slots available now, and give a deadline for choosing.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

mustNotClaim: that the requested time is available

touches.purpose: Say plainly that the time could not be committed, that nothing is being held, and when capacity of this kind is next expected.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: Close the request as lapsed and say that nothing is held and nothing was booked.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

useCases: whether the requested time is now a commitment, stated one way or the other
the nearest real slots offered when the requested one is gone

requires: a reservation request recorded against a named requester, resource and slot
a permitted contact point for a booking notice
insufficientAlone: availability being searched or displayed
a slot held inside a session that was never submitted

nodes.does: Acknowledge the request and say explicitly that it is not yet a commitment, naming when the outcome will come. The gap between asking for a time and holding it is where every double-booking dispute begins

after.rule: The period the booking semantics allow a request to stay unresolved.

timeout.reason: an unresolved request sits against capacity other requesters can see, and it cannot sit there indefinitely

nodes.recheck: the the reservation request re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

nodes.asks: What did revalidation decide?

branches.label: Committed
branches.when: the capacity was committed and a confirmed reservation now exists

branches.label: Gone, but something near
branches.when: the slot was no longer available when it was re-read, and current availability holds something close enough to be worth offering

branches.label: Gone, nothing near
branches.when: the slot was no longer available and nothing in current availability is a genuine alternative

nodes.does: State the committed slot, the resource and the terms concretely - the date, the time, the place, what is needed on arrival. A confirmation that does not restate the specifics is not something the requester can act on a month later

nodes.state: committed and stated to the requester
nodes.reEntry: a change or cancellation to this commitment is its own instance; a further request is a new one

nodes.does: Say the requested time is gone, name the slots available now, and give a deadline for choosing. What is offered is current availability and never the set they were originally shown, which by definition contains one slot that no longer exists

after.rule: The stated deadline for choosing.

timeout.reason: the offered slots stay visible to everyone else and are not held while one requester decides

nodes.recheck: the the reservation request re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

nodes.asks: Did they take one of them?

branches.label: Took a slot
branches.when: the requester asked for one of the slots that were offered

branches.label: Declined all
branches.when: the requester declined every alternative offered

nodes.on: a requester choosing one of the alternative slots offered to them
carries: the original request and why it could not be met
the slot chosen and when it was offered

nodes.state: no commitment made, requester informed
nodes.reEntry: a fresh request for a different time enters as a new instance

nodes.does: Say plainly that the time could not be committed, that nothing is being held, and when capacity of this kind is next expected. A rejection with no next horizon sends the requester somewhere else rather than back to the calendar
Close the request as lapsed and say that nothing is held and nothing was booked. Requesters read silence as confirmation, which is the most expensive assumption in scheduling

nodes.state: request lapsed unresolved, nothing held
nodes.reEntry: a fresh request starts the sequence again

guardrails: A request acknowledged is never worded as a request confirmed.
What is offered after a failure is current availability, never the set the requester was originally shown.
Nothing is described as held unless the booking semantics actually hold it.
A lapse is stated. Silence after a request is read as a commitment.
The confirmation restates the concrete slot every time. A reference is not a time and a place.
journeys.reusableRule: Availability shown is a picture and a confirmation is a promise, and the requester must never have to guess which one they were sent.

journeys.name: No-show confirmed → validate the miss → rebook or close
journeys.purpose: Offer a way back to somebody whose booking did not happen, having first established that the miss was theirs and not ours - because a rebooking prompt sent over our own failure is an accusation.

entity.scope: the single booking occurrence that did not take place
entity.note: One occurrence. This says nothing about the person's history or standing - it is a fact about one booking, and a second miss is its own instance.

distinctFrom.because: SCH-179 establishes and records the no-show and decides what consequence policy attaches. This journey is what the customer is told, it never creates the record, and it runs only where policy attached rebooking rather than a consequence.
SCH-177 runs as the time approaches and is about getting somebody there. This starts only once the window has closed with nobody there.

journeys.objective: After a genuinely missed booking, state the fact without penalty language and give the single route to a new booking where one exists - after re-reading the booking, and never where our side could not have delivered.
eligibility: a no-show is recorded against one booking occurrence by the attendance source
the booking, re-read after the recording lag, genuinely did not happen - not moved, cancelled or attended after all
the provider or resource could have delivered; a failure on our side goes to reschedule, not follow-up
hard gates (GLB-31) permit service communication

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Attendance and cancellation events lag; the booking's latest events are re-read before anything leaves, and a booking moved, cancelled or attended after all sends nothing.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A missed booking the provider or resource could not have delivered is ours, not the customer's; it goes to reschedule and no follow-up is sent.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: The miss is stated as a fact; no penalty language, and no penalty applied here - the commitment's own terms own consequences.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Where nothing can be rebooked, the notice acknowledges the miss and what it means, with no rebooking prompt attached.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
