nodes.on: a message whose recipient or destination stopped being valid before send
carries: obligation_id
the obligation, still unmet, and what changed about the routing
the explicit fact that nothing was sent, so no duplicate arises from re-resolving

nodes.asks: Does the content depend on data that has changed since preparation?

branches.label: It changed
branches.when: an amount, a date, a status or a name in the message is no longer current

branches.label: Unchanged
branches.when: everything the message states is still current

nodes.does: Regenerate the content from current data before sending. Sending a stale amount, date or status is worse than sending nothing, because the recipient acts on it and then has to be told it was wrong

Record the message as validated at send time, with what was checked and against what version, and mint attempt_id for the submission this hands off to. This mechanism runs at most once per message_id - CMS-208's own recovery loop retries independently downstream rather than looping back through this mechanism - so a.send is idempotent on message_id: a redelivered t.ready reuses the attempt_id already minted rather than minting a second one and risking a duplicate provider submission. Historical sent messages are never mutated afterwards - what was sent is what was sent, and rewriting it removes the evidence that a wrong thing went out

nodes.on: a message validated immediately before delivery
carries: the message, its content version and the state it was validated against
message_id (carried from CMS-204) and the fresh attempt_id minted at a.send, so CMS-206 persists an attempt against an identity established before submission rather than one it invents itself
the route selected and the fallback held in reserve

guardrails: A queued message is not a permanently valid message.
A reminder for a cancelled appointment does not send.
A resolved payment failure does not send as unresolved.
Historical sent messages are never mutated.
journeys.reusableRule: Messages should be revalidated immediately before delivery whenever delayed execution could make their content or purpose stale.

journeys.name: Send attempt → accepted, failed or unknown
journeys.purpose: Record what happened when the message was handed to a provider, which is not what happened to the recipient.

entity.scope: the individual delivery attempt, with its provider reference
entity.note: One attempt per submission. Outcomes arriving later correlate to a specific attempt, which is why the attempt is written before its outcome is known. attempt_id is caller-supplied - minted by CMS-205's a.send before this mechanism ever runs, per attempt, never by this mechanism itself - specifically so a redelivered t.submitted for the same attempt_id can be told apart from a genuinely new attempt for the same message_id (a retry, minting its own fresh attempt_id upstream).

distinctFrom.because: This is the handover to a provider - accepted, refused or unanswered. CMS-207 is what the channel later reports about whether it reached anyone. A message can be accepted and never delivered, and the two states must be separately visible.

requires: a validated message submitted to a delivery mechanism or provider, carrying a message_id and an attempt_id already minted by the caller

nodes.does: Persist the message id, the attempt id, the destination_id it was submitted to, the channel, the provider and its reference, the submission time and the content version reference. The attempt is written before its outcome is known, so an outcome arriving hours later has something to attach to. Both message_id and attempt_id arrive already minted - a redelivered call for the same (message_id, attempt_id) persists once, not twice - and destination_id is read off the submission itself, one attempt always targeting exactly one destination even on a coordinated multi-channel obligation

until: the provider reports an immediate authoritative failure

timeout.after: the submission timeout for this channel
timeout.reason: a provider that neither accepts nor refuses leaves the message in an unknown state, and the question of whether to resend depends on knowing that rather than assuming either answer

nodes.asks: What did the provider do with it?

branches.label: Accepted
branches.when: the provider took the message for delivery

branches.label: Refused immediately
branches.when: the provider authoritatively rejected the submission

nodes.does: Record SENT and DELIVERY_PENDING. The provider taking the message is a fact about the provider's queue - it can be accepted, held, bounced and discarded without anything reaching anybody

nodes.state: SENT and DELIVERY_PENDING; submitted and accepted, delivery not established
nodes.reEntry: the channel's delivery outcome arrives on its own schedule and correlates to this attempt. Nothing here concludes the obligation

nodes.does: Record DELIVERY_FAILED with exactly what the provider reported, unclassified. The classification belongs to the recovery journey, which needs the raw reason rather than a summary of it

nodes.on: a submission the provider refused, or an unknown outcome where duplicates are harmless
carries: message_id and destination_id, both established at a.persist, which is what CMS-208's own recovery instance is keyed on
the attempt, the channel and what the provider actually said
the fallback held in reserve and the obligation's remaining relevance window

nodes.does: Record DELIVERY_UNKNOWN and hold any resend. A timeout is not a failure - the message may well have gone, and resending blindly delivers the same notice twice, which for some notices reads as a different message than once

nodes.asks: Would a duplicate matter for this communication?

branches.label: It would
branches.when: the message carries a code, a link, a payment instruction or anything a second copy makes ambiguous

branches.label: It would not
branches.when: a repeat is harmless and the message is worth resending on that basis

nodes.on: an unknown submission outcome where a duplicate would matter
carries: the attempt, its provider reference and everything last known about it
the explicit instruction that no resend happens until the outcome is established
suppresses: any resend of this message while its outcome is unknown

guardrails: Provider accepted is not delivered.
A timeout is not a send failure.
A blind resend may create duplicate communication.
journeys.reusableRule: Submitting a message establishes a delivery attempt, not proof that the recipient received it.

journeys.name: Delivery outcome → delivered, failed or unknown → update communication
journeys.purpose: Derive the real delivery state from what the channel reports, attached to the exact attempt it concerns.

entity.scope: the delivery attempt and the outcomes reported against it
entity.note: Outcomes arrive out of order, twice, and late. Each is processed against the attempt it names and against what is already recorded. attempt_id is a correlation key, not a durable-entity key the way instanceKey means elsewhere - concurrency: one-active-per-key here means events for one attempt are processed sequentially against each other, not that only one outcome may ever arrive.

requires: a delivery event or status reported by the channel

nodes.does: Correlate the outcome to the exact delivery attempt it concerns. A status with no attempt to attach to is a status about nothing, and attaching it to the wrong attempt marks a different message delivered

nodes.asks: Did it correlate to a known attempt?

branches.label: Correlated
branches.when: the outcome names an attempt we hold

branches.label: Uncorrelated
branches.when: the outcome names nothing we recognise

nodes.on: a delivery outcome that could not be correlated or that remains ambiguous
carries: the raw outcome as reported and the attempts it might concern
the explicit instruction that no delivery state is written on a guess about which message it belongs to

nodes.asks: Is this outcome new, repeated, or older than what is already recorded?

branches.label: New and current
branches.when: this outcome advances what is known about the attempt

branches.label: Already processed
branches.when: the same outcome has already been applied to this attempt

branches.label: Late and weaker
branches.when: it arrives after, and reports less than, what is already established

nodes.state: duplicate delivery event ignored; recorded state unchanged
nodes.reEntry: a genuinely new outcome for this attempt is processed on its own terms. Channels repeat webhooks, and repeating the state change with them double-counts every delivery

nodes.does: Record the late event without overwriting stronger evidence. A bounce arriving after a confirmed delivery does not undo the delivery - unless the channel's semantics explicitly say it does, in which case they say so and the rule is applied rather than assumed

nodes.state: late outcome recorded; stronger delivery evidence preserved
nodes.reEntry: channel semantics that genuinely make a late failure authoritative are applied as a rule rather than by arrival order

nodes.asks: What does the channel report?

branches.label: Delivered
branches.when: the channel authoritatively reports it reached the destination

branches.label: Definitive failure
branches.when: the channel authoritatively reports it did not and will not arrive

branches.label: Ambiguous
branches.when: the report establishes neither

nodes.does: Record DELIVERED against this attempt. Delivered is not read, and read is not understood - a delivery receipt says the message reached a destination and nothing about anybody having seen it, let alone acted on it

nodes.on: a confirmed delivery
carries: obligation_id, read off the attempt record this delivery correlated to
which attempt delivered, on which channel and when
the explicit fact that delivered is not read, so an obligation requiring comprehension is not met by this

nodes.does: Record DELIVERY_FAILED with the reason exactly as the channel reported it. The reason is what the recovery journey classifies on, and summarising it here loses the distinction between a full mailbox and a dead address

nodes.on: an authoritative delivery failure
carries: message_id and destination_id, read off the attempt record this outcome correlated to
the failure as the channel reported it, unclassified
the attempt, the channel and the obligation's remaining relevance

nodes.does: Record DELIVERY_UNKNOWN. Neither delivered nor failed is a real state, and resolving it to whichever is more convenient produces either a closed obligation nobody met or a duplicate nobody needed

guardrails: Sent is not delivered.
Delivered is not read.
A late failure does not overwrite stronger authoritative delivery evidence without valid channel semantics.
Repeated delivery events are processed idempotently.
An open or a read can be produced by a privacy proxy or a scanner rather than by a person. It is evidence about the message and never authoritative evidence of intent or outcome.
journeys.reusableRule: Communication delivery state should be derived from authoritative channel evidence and correlated to the exact delivery attempt.

journeys.name: Delivery failure → classify → retry, fallback or stop
journeys.purpose: Respond to the failure that actually happened, without spreading it wider than the destination it belongs to.

entity.scope: the failed delivery, its channel and the destination it was aimed at
entity.note: The failure belongs to a destination on a channel. It says nothing about the recipient's other destinations, and recording it against the person loses them. message_id + destination_id is the recovery instance's own identity - one durable retry budget per (message, destination), fixed at the first failure and spent across however many physical attempts a.retry makes against it. Each physical attempt still mints its own fresh attempt_id (the same convention CMS-205/CMS-206 use), so the budget and the per-attempt identity are two different things scoped at two different granularities, not one field doing both jobs.

distinctFrom.because: This mechanism owns its own complete channel-aware retry loop end to end - classification, relevance, budget, fallback - and does not invoke OPS-124's generic engine for it, because the classification a communication failure needs (TEMPORARY / PROVIDER_FAILURE / RATE_LIMITED / PERMANENT / INVALID_DESTINATION / CHANNEL_RESTRICTED) is channel-specific domain knowledge OPS-124 deliberately has no reason to carry. Where a communication-triggering action is separately wrapped in OPS-121's own generic asynchronous-work tracking (the enqueue/dispatch step itself, not the channel delivery), that tracking's own possible OPS-124 delegation is a distinct, outer concern from this mechanism's inner channel-recovery loop - the two do not share a budget and are not the same retry.

requires: a delivery failure reported authoritatively by the channel or provider
insufficientAlone: an unknown outcome, which is not a failure and needs reconciling rather than recovering

nodes.does: Classify the failure by what the channel actually reported, into an explicit class - TEMPORARY, PROVIDER_FAILURE, RATE_LIMITED, PERMANENT, INVALID_DESTINATION, CHANNEL_RESTRICTED or UNKNOWN. The class decides everything downstream, which is why it is established before anything is retried, and treating them all as transient produces a retry loop against an address that will never exist

nodes.asks: Is the communication still relevant?

branches.label: Still relevant
branches.when: the reason for the message still stands and its window is open

branches.label: No longer relevant
branches.when: the event it concerns has resolved, or its relevance window has closed

nodes.does: Suppress the recovery. Recovering delivery of a message whose reason for existing has passed spends effort arriving at a stale notice, which is the worst of both outcomes

nodes.state: recovery abandoned; the message was overtaken by events
nodes.reEntry: the obligation closes as superseded rather than as failed. Its subject producing a new event creates a new obligation

nodes.asks: What does the failure class call for?

branches.label: Temporary, rate-limited or provider-side
branches.when: the destination is fine and the failure is expected to clear

branches.label: Permanent for this destination
branches.when: a hard bounce, an invalid address or a dead token

branches.label: Restricted on this channel
branches.when: this channel will not carry this content, for a reason a retry does not address

branches.label: Unclassifiable
branches.when: the provider gave no class that can be relied on

nodes.does: Treat an unclassifiable failure as temporary but on a smaller budget, and record that the class was unknown. Guessing permanent discards a destination that may work; guessing temporary on the full budget is how an unknown failure becomes an unbounded retry

Retry on the same channel, with backoff, minting a fresh attempt_id for this physical attempt and spending one unit of the budget fixed at the first failure against (message_id, destination_id). The budget is set once and does not renew - that is the difference between a retry policy and a loop, and a schedule with no end looks like a working system from inside and like harassment from the recipient's inbox

attemptBudget.rule: Fixed once at the first failure for this (message_id, destination_id); does not renew on worker restart, on backoff completion, or on delegation between mechanisms.

nodes.asks: Does retry budget remain?

branches.label: Budget remains
branches.when: the attempt count and window still permit another try

branches.label: The destination's contactability changed underneath the retry
branches.when: the contact point's own state moved while the budget was being spent

branches.label: Exhausted
branches.when: the budget fixed at the first failure has been spent

nodes.state: retrying within budget on the same channel
nodes.reEntry: each retry is a new send attempt with its own outcome, and a failure on it returns here with the budget one lower

nodes.does: Stop futile retries against this destination and raise the contactability evidence. One invalid address invalidates that address and nothing else - the recipient's phone, device and in-app account are untouched by an email that bounced

nodes.on: a failure that is a property of the contact point rather than of the attempt
carries: destination_id, which is contact_point_id under this mechanism's own attempt-scoped name - the same durable contact point CON-36 tracks by its permanent record identity
the failure class, the destination, the channel and the provider's response
the explicit scope: this destination only, with the recipient's other routes unaffected
the explicit fact that this is a deliverability problem and not an opt-out - it says nothing about permission on this channel or any other

nodes.asks: Is an alternate channel available?

branches.label: One is available
branches.when: the recipient has another destination on another channel

branches.label: None
branches.when: no other channel remains for this recipient

nodes.on: a failed channel with an alternate destination available
carries: obligation_id, read off the message_id this recovery instance is keyed on
the obligation, its purpose and the channel that has now failed

the explicit requirement that the fallback passes the purpose and permission check on its own terms - a fallback that skips it delivers a message down a route the recipient declined, and the failure becomes the excuse for it
the fact that a permitted alternative allows the move and does not require it - the sending journey still decides whether the message warrants changing channel

nodes.on: a failure with no remaining channel to try
carries: obligation_id, read off the message_id this recovery instance is keyed on
every route attempted and how each failed
the explicit fact that this is exhaustion of routes rather than proof the recipient is unreachable in general

guardrails: A delivery failure does not mean the user is unreachable everywhere.
Retry is bounded rather than infinite.
A fallback must independently pass the purpose and permission checks.
One invalid address does not invalidate unrelated destinations.
The retry budget is fixed at the first failure and does not renew.
A permanent bounce is a deliverability fact rather than an engagement problem, and is never fed into an engagement or churn model as one.
A failure on one channel says nothing about the permission or the contactability of any other.
A permitted alternative channel allows a move; it does not require one.
journeys.reusableRule: Communication recovery should respond to the actual delivery failure while preserving channel-specific contactability and message relevance.

journeys.name: Communication outcome → close obligation or escalate unreachable
journeys.purpose: Close the obligation against what it actually required, and escalate the ones that could not be met.

entity.scope: the communication obligation and every delivery made against it
entity.note: The obligation defines its own required outcome. Some are met by a documented attempt and some only by confirmed delivery, and which applies is not this journey's to decide.

requires: an obligation whose deliveries have reached a state that could close it

nodes.asks: Did the communication become obsolete before it was delivered?

branches.label: It did
branches.when: the event it concerns resolved or was undone while delivery was still in progress

branches.label: It stands
branches.when: the reason for the message is still real

nodes.does: Close as SUPERSEDED or SUPPRESSED, recording that the obligation ended because its reason did rather than because it was met. The two look identical in a completion count and mean opposite things

nodes.state: closed as superseded; the obligation ended unmet and unneeded
nodes.reEntry: a new event about the same subject creates its own obligation rather than reviving this one

nodes.asks: What does this obligation require to be satisfied?

branches.label: Confirmed delivery
branches.when: the requirement is that the message actually reached the recipient

branches.label: A documented send attempt
branches.when: the requirement is that a message was properly sent, with the record to show it

branches.label: Not defined
branches.when: nothing states whether an attempt or a delivery satisfies this notice

nodes.on: an obligation with no defined completion semantics
carries: the obligation, its purpose and every delivery made against it
the explicit fact that no completion standard was invented - guessing closes something unmet or escalates something that was fine, and for a legal notice the difference is the whole point

nodes.asks: Is delivery confirmed?

branches.label: Confirmed
branches.when: authoritative channel evidence establishes it arrived

branches.label: Not confirmed
branches.when: no delivery has been established on any route

nodes.asks: Is a documented send attempt on record?

branches.label: On record
branches.when: a properly validated message was submitted and the attempt is recorded

branches.label: None succeeded in being made
branches.when: no attempt was ever submitted on any permitted route

nodes.does: Record COMMUNICATION_COMPLETED against the requirement it actually satisfied, naming which one. Unread is not undelivered, and an obligation met by delivery is met whether or not anybody opened it

nodes.state: COMMUNICATION_COMPLETED against its stated requirement
nodes.reEntry: a further event about the same subject creates its own obligation. Whether the recipient understood is not something this state claims

nodes.asks: Are all permissible delivery routes exhausted?

branches.label: Routes remain
branches.when: a permitted channel or destination has not yet been tried

branches.label: Exhausted
branches.when: every route permitted for this purpose has been tried and none worked

nodes.state: obligation open; permitted routes remain untried
nodes.reEntry: the remaining routes are attempted and report their own outcomes back here

nodes.does: Record UNREACHABLE_FOR_PURPOSE. This is scoped to the purpose - every route permitted for this kind of message failed, and the same recipient may be perfectly reachable for something else

nodes.asks: Is this communication mandatory or critical?

branches.label: It is
branches.when: a rule, a contract or a regulation requires this recipient to be told

branches.label: It is not
branches.when: the message was useful rather than required

nodes.on: a mandatory communication that could not be delivered by any permitted route
carries: every route attempted, why each failed, and the requirement that makes this mandatory
the explicit fact that more retries will not resolve it - what is needed is a person and an alternate process

nodes.state: UNREACHABLE_FOR_PURPOSE; the obligation closes unmet and recorded as such
nodes.reEntry: a new valid destination for this purpose makes the recipient reachable again, and a later obligation routes normally

guardrails: Whether a send or a delivery is sufficient is never invented.
Unread is not undelivered.
A critical communication failure escalates rather than retrying endlessly.
An obligation does not close merely because a message object exists.
journeys.reusableRule: A communication obligation closes according to its required outcome - attempt, delivery or explicit escalation - not merely because a message object exists.

journeys.name: Document requirement → determine artifact → create, reuse or waive
journeys.purpose: Decide whether a new artifact is genuinely needed, or whether one already exists that answers the requirement.

entity.scope: the business process and the artifact requirement it has reached
entity.note: The requirement names a type, a purpose, parties and validity conditions. Reuse is only possible against all four, not against the type alone.

distinctFrom.because: RSK-195 owns the compliance requirement itself - whether an obligation is met. This owns the artifact lifecycle a requirement may need: which document, generated how, issued when, signed by whom. A compliance requirement can be satisfied without any document, and most documents exist for reasons that are not compliance.

requires: a business process reaching a point where an artifact is required
insufficientAlone: a process step occurring, which does not by itself mean a new document is needed

nodes.does: Determine the required artifact type, its purpose, the required parties, the required data, its validity requirements, and whether an existing artifact could satisfy all of them

nodes.asks: Does an existing valid artifact satisfy this requirement?

branches.label: One does
branches.when: an existing document matches the type, the scope, the parties and is still within its validity

branches.label: None
branches.when: nothing held matches, or what is held has lapsed or was scoped to something else

nodes.does: Reference the existing artifact and its exact version rather than generating another. Regenerating an identical document produces two records claiming the same thing, and a later reader has to work out which one anybody actually acted on

nodes.state: requirement satisfied by an existing valid artifact
nodes.reEntry: that artifact expiring or being revoked reopens the requirement, which is then assessed fresh rather than assumed still met

nodes.asks: Does an authorized rule waive this requirement?

branches.label: It is waived
branches.when: a rule or an authority explicitly excuses the artifact for this case

branches.label: It stands
branches.when: no waiver applies

nodes.does: Record the waiver with the rule and the authority behind it. A requirement quietly skipped is indistinguishable from one nobody noticed, and the difference matters entirely when somebody asks why the document is missing

nodes.state: requirement waived, with the authority recorded
nodes.reEntry: the waiver's own scope bounds it. A different instance of the same requirement is assessed on its own terms

nodes.does: Create the document obligation with its type, purpose, parties, required data and validity requirements

nodes.on: an unmet artifact requirement
carries: the artifact type, its purpose, the parties and the data it needs
the validity requirements, which decide what makes it complete rather than merely rendered

guardrails: A process event does not always require a new document.
An identical artifact is not regenerated unnecessarily.
Reuse respects the existing document's version, scope and validity.
journeys.reusableRule: A document should be created only when the process has an unmet artifact requirement that cannot be satisfied by an existing valid record.

journeys.name: Document draft → populate → validate → ready or blocked
journeys.purpose: Build the contents from authoritative sources and prove they are complete before anything is issued.

entity.scope: the draft and the source entities its contents came from
entity.note: Each field carries which source and which version it came from. A document that cannot say where its contents originated cannot be defended when they are questioned.

requires: a document obligation with a defined type and required contents

nodes.does: Resolve the required data from its authoritative sources, recording which source and which version each field came from. A document that cannot say where its contents came from cannot be defended when they are questioned, and they will be
Populate the draft from what was resolved, and from nothing else
Validate the required fields, the source versions, the party identities, the document type, the draft's internal consistency, and any required attachments or components

nodes.asks: Is the draft complete and valid?

branches.label: Complete and valid
branches.when: every required element is present, sourced and consistent

branches.label: Something is missing or inconsistent
branches.when: a required field, source, party or component is absent or contradicts another

nodes.does: Record BLOCKED or MISSING_REQUIREMENT naming exactly what is absent. Missing data is never filled with a plausible value - a generated file carrying an invented field looks authoritative, reads as authoritative, and is not

timeout.after: the window the requiring process allows for the artifact
timeout.reason: a draft waiting indefinitely on data nobody is supplying blocks the process that needed it, without anyone having decided to block it

nodes.asks: How did the wait resolve?

branches.label: The data arrived
branches.when: what was missing is now available from an authoritative source

branches.label: Withdrawn
branches.when: the requirement no longer stands

nodes.does: Abandon the draft, preserving the record that it was started and why it stopped. Nothing was issued, so nothing about it is authoritative

nodes.state: draft abandoned; nothing was issued
nodes.reEntry: the requirement arising again starts its own draft. Repopulating this one would use the sources as they were rather than as they are

nodes.on: a draft blocked past the window the process allows
carries: the document, the missing element and the source that should have supplied it
the explicit fact that nothing was invented to complete it and nothing was issued

nodes.does: Record READY_TO_ISSUE. A generated file is not a valid document - readiness is the validation having passed rather than the rendering having succeeded, and the two are routinely confused because both produce a file

nodes.on: a validated draft ready for issuance
carries: the validated contents and the source version each field came from
the explicit fact that the draft is still editable and nothing is yet authoritative

guardrails: A generated file is not a valid document.
Missing data is never silently invented.
Source references and their versions remain traceable.
journeys.reusableRule: A document becomes issuable only after its required contents have been populated from authoritative sources and validated for completeness.

journeys.name: Ready document → issue → immutable issued version
journeys.purpose: Freeze the artifact at a version that can be identified, referenced and never quietly changed.

entity.scope: the document and the specific version being issued
entity.note: This is the boundary between an editable draft and an authoritative record. After it, change means a successor.

requires: a validated draft with the authority to issue it established
insufficientAlone: a draft being ready, which says the contents validate and nothing about whether anyone authorized issuing it

nodes.does: Create the issued version, capturing the document id, the version id, the issue time, the issuer, the parties, the content with its hash or reference, the source context it was built from, and the effective semantics where the document defines any

Freeze it. An issued version never changes - a document that can be edited after issue cannot answer what anybody was looking at when they agreed to it, and that is the only question it will ever be asked. Later changes create a successor rather than an edit

nodes.asks: Do the document's own semantics make it effective on issue?

branches.label: Not by itself
branches.when: effect depends on signature, a date, a condition or another dependency

branches.label: Effective on issue, by its own terms
branches.when: the document type takes effect at issuance without further conditions

nodes.does: Record ISSUED and nothing more. Issuance is the artifact existing in fixed, identifiable form - whether it has any effect is a separate question with its own conditions, and a contract can exist in final form and bind nobody

nodes.state: ISSUED and immutable; effect not established
nodes.reEntry: any later change creates a new version through the amendment lifecycle. This version is never reopened, edited or reissued under the same identifier

nodes.does: Record the effective semantics exactly as the document states them, without inventing any. A document type that takes effect at issue says so; assuming it on behalf of one that does not brings terms into force early

nodes.on: an issued document whose own terms make it effective without signature
carries: the issued version, its identifier and the semantics that make it effective
the explicit fact that effectiveness is still validated rather than assumed from issuance

guardrails: A draft is not an issued document.
An issued document never silently changes.
Issuance does not automatically make a document effective.
journeys.reusableRule: Issuance freezes an auditable version of a document so later changes create new versions rather than rewriting what was previously issued.

journeys.name: Document distribution → send or provide access → confirm or fail
journeys.purpose: Get a specific issued version to the party who should have it, without either fact touching the other.

entity.scope: the issued version, the intended recipient, and the distribution of one to the other
entity.note: The distribution is bound to a version. Delivery state describes the distribution and never the document.

journeys.objective: Get a specific issued version to the party who should have it, without either fact touching the other.
eligibility: an issued document version with a party who is to receive it
no instance of this journey is already open for the the issued version
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A document being issued is not the recipient having received it.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Sending a wrong or outdated version is prevented by binding distribution to a version.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Distribution reuses the canonical communication mechanics rather than duplicating them.

value.rule: Every touch runs against a budget fixed when the instance opened; the budget is the plan's own length, and no touch is repeated because nothing could tell whether it arrived.

default.applicableWhen: GLB-24; the graph's own touch count

cooldown.rule: This journey is per the issued version; a later instance concerns a different the issued version and no cooldown applies between them.

default.applicableWhen: the entity note: one instance per entity

roles.when: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it

touches.purpose: Raise the actual delivery through the canonical communication mechanism, which owns channels, permissions, retries and delivery evidence.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

guardrails: complaint
message_after_success
unsubscribe

useCases: a specific issued version delivered to the party who should have it
a failed distribution handed to delivery recovery

requires: an issued document version with a party who is to receive it
insufficientAlone: a document drafted but not issued
a document already viewed or downloaded by its recipient, which is delivery having happened

nodes.does: Resolve the intended recipient and the route permitted for a document of this type. A document reaching the wrong party is worse than one not sent - the second can be retried and the first cannot be recalled

Bind the distribution to the exact issued version. Sending an outdated version is the failure this step exists to prevent: the recipient then holds, relies on, and may sign terms that nobody currently offers

Raise the actual delivery through the canonical communication mechanism, which owns channels, permissions, retries and delivery evidence. Document distribution does not build its own delivery path - a parallel one will disagree with the canonical delivery record about whether the contract was ever sent

after.rule: The distribution outcome is waited for as long as the communication mechanism's own delivery window runs; past it the outcome is reconciled, never assumed.

timeout.reason: a distribution neither confirmed nor failed leaves nobody able to say whether the recipient has the document, which is the one thing distribution exists to establish

nodes.recheck: the the issued version re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

nodes.asks: How did the distribution resolve?

branches.label: Confirmed
branches.when: delivery or availability is established to the level the requirement demands

branches.label: Failed
branches.when: the channel authoritatively reports it did not arrive

nodes.does: Record DELIVERED or AVAILABLE against the exact version distributed. Delivery state describes the distribution and never the document - an undelivered contract is a valid contract nobody has, and treating delivery as validity turns a mail failure into a legal one

nodes.state: the identified version reached the intended recipient; the document's validity is unchanged by this
nodes.reEntry: a superseding version requires its own distribution. Nothing about this one is retracted by that - the recipient was correctly given what was current then

nodes.does: Record the distribution outcome as unknown and do not treat it as delivered. The document's validity is untouched either way - what is unknown is whether anybody has it

nodes.on: a distribution whose outcome could not be established
carries: the version, the recipient and everything last known about the delivery
the explicit fact that the document remains valid and issued regardless of how this resolves

nodes.on: a failed document distribution
carries: message_id (this distribution's own message identity) and destination_id (the recipient destination this attempt targeted), which CMS-208's own recovery instance is keyed on
the failure as the channel reported it, and the exact version that was being sent
the explicit requirement that any fallback route carries the same version - a recovery that sends a different one is worse than the original failure

guardrails: A document being issued is not the recipient having received it.
Sending a wrong or outdated version is prevented by binding distribution to a version.
Distribution reuses the canonical communication mechanics rather than duplicating them.
journeys.reusableRule: Document distribution delivers a specific issued version to an intended recipient without changing the document's underlying validity or status.

journeys.name: Signature request → await signatures → signed, declined or expired
journeys.purpose: Collect the required signatures against one exact version, and know when they are actually all there.

entity.scope: the document version, the signature process against it, and each required signer
entity.note: The process is bound to a version. Signatures do not carry to a successor - a changed document is a new request.

distinctFrom.because: DEC-183 is somebody exercising judgment against criteria. This is collecting authorized marks against a fixed artifact - nobody is deciding anything on the merits, and its failure modes are version binding, incomplete sets and expiry rather than authority to conclude.

journeys.objective: Collect every required signature on one exact document version: request once from each required signer, remind outstanding signers once while a reminder can still change the outcome, and end honestly as fully signed, declined, superseded or expired.
eligibility: a document version requires signature, with required signers, their signing authority and any signing order defined
a signature validity window is either defined by the request's own terms or explicitly recorded as not set
no signature process is already open for this version
no DOC-220 conflict review is open for this document's lineage - a version under active conflict review is not simultaneously collecting signatures against it as though it were already settled

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Every request and reminder is bound to the exact document version; a superseded version ends the process and suppresses its outstanding reminders.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: A reminder goes only to signers still outstanding, naming the action left and the real validity boundary; a signer who signed is never reminded.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: One reminder per signer; a second is a re-request the process does not make.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Where no expiry was set none is invented; an invented signature deadline voids a request nobody agreed to time-limit.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Hard gates (GLB-31) apply; pressure caps do not, because a signature request is the process itself, not outreach.

value.rule: Only the reminder counts against the cap; the request itself is the process and is never rationed.

default.applicableWhen: the graph sends one reminder per signer

cooldown.rule: Signature is per document version; a new version is a new process and no cooldown applies between versions.

roles.when: the request is bound to a document version and must be kept; the signing destination is reached from it

touches.purpose: Issue the request to each required signer, bound to the exact document version, naming the authority they sign under and the validity boundary where one is defined.

mustNotClaim: a deadline the request's terms do not set

touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: Remind only the signers still outstanding, once, naming the action left and the real validity boundary.

mustNotClaim: a deadline the request's terms do not set

touches.label: RECOMMENDED_DEFAULT

guardrails: complaint
reminder_to_signed_signer
invented_deadline_named
wrong_version_signed

useCases: a contract needing several signatures in a defined order
a consent or agreement version with a validity window and one reminder

requires: an issued or prepared document version requiring signature by identified parties
insufficientAlone: a document that requires acknowledgement rather than an authorised mark
a signature request already sent, which is the state this journey creates and not the one that starts it

nodes.does: Define the required signers, the signing authority each of them needs, the signing order where one applies, the scope of what is being signed, and the validity window where one is defined

nodes.asks: Is a signature validity window defined?

branches.label: Defined
branches.when: the process or the document states how long the request stands

branches.label: Not defined
branches.when: nothing states an expiry for the request

nodes.does: Record the window as defined, so the request's own terms decide when it lapses
Record that no expiry was set rather than assigning one. An invented signature deadline voids a request nobody withdrew, and the signer discovers it at the moment their signature is refused

Record AWAITING_SIGNATURE and issue the request to each required signer, bound to the exact document version. A signature request that does not name a version collects marks against nothing anybody can identify afterwards

after.rule: The reminder is placed at the last point at which it could still change the outcome, taken from the request's own validity where one is defined and from the process's review point where none is.

default.applicableWhen: a validity window of weeks
default.avoidWhen: no validity window - the review point is the bound

timeout.reason: the useful reminder point comes before expiry, not at it - a request that lapses without a second touch was never given the chance the window was for

nodes.recheck: the version and each signer re-read: who has signed the correct version, who declined, whether the version still stands

nodes.asks: Would a reminder still change anything?

branches.label: It would
branches.when: signatures are still outstanding, the exact version is still current, the request is still valid, and no reminder has been sent on it yet

branches.label: It would not
branches.when: a reminder has already been sent, or the version or request no longer stands

nodes.does: Remind only the signers still outstanding, naming the action left and the real validity boundary. One reminder, and any signature, decline or supersession cancels it immediately - a second chase turns a request into pressure

after.rule: The process ends at the validity window where one is defined, and at the process's own review point where none is; nothing is invented.

default.value: validity_ends_at where defined, otherwise the process's recorded review point

timeout.reason: a signature request open indefinitely leaves a process waiting on an agreement that will not arrive, with nobody having decided to abandon it

nodes.recheck: the version and each signer re-read at the boundary

nodes.asks: What happened?

branches.label: A required signer signed the correct version
branches.when: the signature is against the version this process governs, by a signer with the required authority

branches.label: A signer declined
branches.when: a required signer refused

branches.label: The version was superseded
branches.when: the document this process is bound to is no longer the current one

nodes.does: Record the signature evidence - who signed, when, which version, and under what authority. The version is part of the evidence rather than context around it

attemptBudget.rule: The signature loop runs once per required signer; the budget is the signer list fixed when the process opened.

nodes.asks: Are all required signatures now complete?

branches.label: All complete
branches.when: every required signer has signed the governed version

branches.label: Some remain
branches.when: at least one required signature is outstanding

nodes.does: Record FULLY_SIGNED against this version. One signature is not a signed document when several are required, and a process that proceeds on the first one proceeds on an agreement that does not exist yet

nodes.on: a document with all required signatures complete
carries: every signature, with its signer, authority, time and the version it binds to
the explicit fact that signed is not effective - what makes it take effect is a separate question with its own conditions

nodes.does: Record DECLINED with the signer and the reason where one was given. A decline is a business outcome rather than a failure, and the process that required the document decides what follows from it

nodes.on: a required signer declining
carries: who declined, when and on what grounds where stated
the explicit fact that the document remains validly issued - what is absent is agreement rather than the artifact

nodes.does: End the signature process because the version it was against no longer stands, and suppress the outstanding requests. Signatures already collected are not carried to the successor - the successor is a different document, and signing it is a new request

nodes.state: signature process ended; its version was superseded before completion
nodes.reEntry: the successor version raises its own signature process. The signatures collected here remain evidence about the version they were made against

nodes.does: Record SIGNATURE_EXPIRED. The request lapsed - nobody declined and nothing was decided, and reporting it as a refusal misstates what the signer did

nodes.state: SIGNATURE_EXPIRED; signatures collected so far remain evidence, the set is incomplete
nodes.reEntry: a fresh request against the same version is a new process. Whether the partial signatures still count is governed by the document's own rules rather than assumed

guardrails: A signature requested is not a signature made.
One signature is not a fully signed document when several are required.
A signature binds to the exact document version.
A signature expiry is never invented.
journeys.reusableRule: A signature process completes only when the required authorized parties have signed the exact document version governed by that process.

journeys.name: Signed document → validate completion → effective or pending condition
journeys.purpose: Establish when a document actually starts doing something, which is not when it was signed.

entity.scope: the completed document version and the effect it is to have
entity.note: Effectiveness is the document's own state. What it then causes elsewhere is a different lifecycle with its own entity.

distinctFrom.because: SUB-161 makes a continuing relationship active. This makes a document effective, which may be what triggers that - but a document can be effective without creating a relationship, and a relationship can activate without any document.

requires: all required signatures complete against one version, or an issued document whose own terms make it effective without signature

nodes.does: Validate that every required signature is present, that each is against the correct version, that each signer held the authority they signed under, which conditions apply, and what the effective date is

nodes.asks: Does the completion hold up?

branches.label: It holds
branches.when: signatures, versions and authorities all check out

branches.label: It does not
branches.when: a signature is against the wrong version, or a signer lacked the authority

nodes.does: Record the completion as not established, naming exactly what fails. A document that looks signed and is not is the most dangerous state in this category, because everything downstream will treat it as agreement

nodes.on: signatures that do not bind to the version they are held against
carries: the signatures, the versions each was made against, and the version claimed as current
the explicit fact that nothing has been made effective and nothing was corrected by overwriting

nodes.asks: What governs when this takes effect?

branches.label: Effective on valid signature
branches.when: the document's terms make completion sufficient

branches.label: A future effective date
branches.when: the document names a date after completion

branches.label: A further dependency
branches.when: effect waits on a condition, an approval or an external event

branches.label: The rules do not define effectiveness
branches.when: nothing states when or whether this document takes effect

nodes.on: a completed document with no defined effectiveness rules
carries: the document, its signatures and what its terms do and do not say
the explicit fact that no legal or business effectiveness was invented - assuming it starts obligations nobody agreed to start

nodes.does: Record PENDING_EFFECTIVE_DATE. The document is complete and does nothing yet, which is a real state and not an incomplete one

until: the document is superseded or revoked before its date

timeout.reason: reaching the effective date is what this wait exists for. It is the normal outcome, and the point at which the document's current standing is checked again

nodes.does: Record PENDING_CONDITION, naming the dependency. A document waiting on an unstated condition is indistinguishable from one that is simply stuck

timeout.after: the window the document or its process allows for the condition
timeout.reason: a signed document waiting forever on a condition that will not arrive is an agreement in limbo, and both parties are entitled to know which it is

nodes.asks: How did the dependency resolve?

branches.label: Satisfied
branches.when: the condition governing effect is met

branches.label: Unsatisfiable
branches.when: the condition cannot now be met

nodes.does: Re-read the document's current standing at the effective moment - is this still the authoritative version, has it been superseded or revoked, do the parties still stand. A stale signed version activating a newer business state is exactly the failure the version binding exists to prevent

nodes.asks: Does the document still stand at its effective moment?

branches.label: Still authoritative
branches.when: this version is current, unsuperseded and unrevoked

branches.label: Superseded or revoked
branches.when: something replaced or withdrew it before it took effect

nodes.does: Record that the document did not take effect, because it was superseded or revoked first. It remains a validly issued and validly signed record of what was agreed - it simply never became operative
Record the condition as unsatisfiable and the document as never effective, naming which dependency failed

nodes.state: complete and never effective; the signed record stands as history
nodes.reEntry: a successor document runs its own effectiveness. Nothing here is deleted - a signed agreement that never came into force is still evidence of what the parties agreed to

nodes.does: Record EFFECTIVE with the version, the moment, and what made it so. This is the document's own state - what it then causes elsewhere is a different lifecycle and is not implied by this

nodes.asks: Does this document taking effect create or change a business state elsewhere?

branches.label: It does
branches.when: a relationship, an entitlement, an obligation or an authorization begins from it

branches.label: It does not
branches.when: the document's effect is entirely a matter of the record itself

nodes.on: an effective document that starts something elsewhere
carries: the effective version, its moment and its scope
the explicit fact that the receiving lifecycle activates on its own conditions - the contract is not the relationship, and a document being effective is evidence rather than activation

nodes.state: EFFECTIVE; the document is in force from the recorded moment
nodes.reEntry: expiry, revocation or supersession each end future reliance on it through their own lifecycles, and none of them changes that it was effective while it was

guardrails: Signed is not automatically effective.
Legal or business effectiveness rules are never invented.
A stale or superseded signed version never activates newer business state.
Effectiveness is revalidated at the effective moment rather than assumed from completion.
journeys.reusableRule: Signing establishes documented agreement or authorization; effectiveness begins only when the conditions governing that document's effect are satisfied.

journeys.name: Document change → new version or amendment → supersede prospectively
journeys.purpose: Change an issued artifact by creating a successor, leaving what it replaces exactly as it was.

entity.scope: the document lineage and the successor version or amendment being created
entity.note: Lineage is the entity. A version without a recorded base and authority is an unrelated file that happens to share a name.

requires: an authorized need to change an issued document, with the authority established
insufficientAlone: an error being noticed, which identifies a need rather than authorizing a change

nodes.does: Identify the base version, the changed scope, the authority for the change, its effective semantics and the parties it affects

nodes.asks: What form does the successor take?

branches.label: A new version
branches.when: the document is reissued in full with the change incorporated

branches.label: An amendment
branches.when: a separate instrument modifies the base while leaving it standing

nodes.does: Create the successor as a new draft version, carrying the base forward with the change incorporated. The base version is not touched
Create an amendment that references the base version rather than restating it. What changed stays legible as a change, which a full reissue makes somebody diff two documents to discover

Record the lineage - this successor, its base, the authority and what changed. Lineage is what makes a document history readable; without it a chain of versions is a set of unrelated files with similar names and nobody can say which one anybody signed

until: the successor completes its own validation, approval and signature requirements

timeout.after: the window the change process allows
timeout.reason: a successor stuck in progress leaves two versions in play and no clear answer about which governs, which is the exact ambiguity the lineage exists to prevent

nodes.asks: Did the successor become authoritative?

branches.label: It did
branches.when: the successor completed validation, approval and any required signatures

branches.label: Abandoned
branches.when: the change was withdrawn or could not complete

nodes.does: Record the change as abandoned. The base version stands unchanged and unmarked - a superseded flag set in anticipation of a successor that never arrived leaves the current document looking obsolete

nodes.state: change abandoned; the base version remains current and unmarked
nodes.reEntry: the change can be attempted again as a new successor against whatever version is current then

nodes.does: Mark the prior version SUPERSEDED for applicable future use. Superseded is not deleted and not historically invalid - the prior version governed everything that happened while it was current, and that stays true regardless of what replaced it

nodes.asks: When do the successor's terms apply?

branches.label: From its own effective conditions
branches.when: the successor states when it takes effect

branches.label: The effective semantics are not defined
branches.when: nothing states when the new terms begin

nodes.does: Apply the new terms only from the successor's own effective conditions. Applying them before it is effective enforces terms nobody has agreed to yet, and applying them backwards makes a compliant history retroactively non-compliant

nodes.state: successor authoritative going forward; the prior version preserved and superseded
nodes.reEntry: a further change creates its own successor against this one, extending the lineage rather than replacing it

nodes.on: a successor with undefined effective semantics
carries: the base, the successor and what the change does and does not state
the explicit fact that no effective date was assumed, so neither version has been made to govern anything it may not

guardrails: A new version does not delete the old version.
Superseded is not historically invalid.
New terms are never applied before the successor's required effective conditions.
Lineage between base and successor is recorded rather than implied.
journeys.reusableRule: Document changes create a traceable successor version whose authority begins according to its own approval and effective conditions.

journeys.name: Document expiry → revalidate requirement → renew, replace or close
journeys.purpose: End future reliance on a time-limited artifact, and stop only what genuinely needs it to be current.

entity.scope: the time-limited document and the processes depending on its current validity
entity.note: What expires is future reliance. Everything done while it was valid was done while it was valid.

distinctFrom.because: Expiry is time running out on terms the document itself set. Revocation is an authority withdrawing it. Nobody decided the first, somebody decided the second, and they carry different consequences for what was relied on meanwhile.

requires: a time-limited document approaching or reaching its defined expiry

nodes.asks: Is the expiry defined by the document or its governing rules?

branches.label: Defined
branches.when: the document or a rule states when its validity ends

branches.label: Not defined
branches.when: no expiry was ever set for this artifact

nodes.does: Record that this document carries no expiry, rather than assigning one. Inventing an expiry invalidates something nobody invalidated, and dependent processes then start failing for a reason that does not exist anywhere in the rules

nodes.state: no expiry defined; the document remains valid until something else ends it
nodes.reEntry: an authority withdrawing it runs through revocation, and a successor replacing it runs through amendment. Neither is expiry

nodes.does: Determine the active and future processes that depend on this document's current validity. What expires is future reliance - nothing that happened while it was valid changes, and the list is of what needs it now rather than of what ever used it
Record EXPIRED. Expired is not revoked: nobody withdrew it, its time ran out, and everything it authorized while valid remains authorized

nodes.asks: Do the governing rules require a replacement or renewal?

branches.label: They require one
branches.when: a current artifact must exist for the process to continue

branches.label: They do not
branches.when: no replacement is mandated by the rules

nodes.does: Raise a new document requirement, linked to the expired artifact so the successor's purpose is traceable to what it replaces

nodes.on: an expired document the rules require to be replaced
carries: the expired artifact, its type, scope and parties
the explicit fact that the expired document remains a valid historical record of the period it covered

nodes.asks: May the dependent processes continue after expiry?

branches.label: They may
branches.when: the governing rules permit them to run on without a current artifact

branches.label: Future actions require current validity
branches.when: specific future actions need a valid document and the rest do not

branches.label: The rules do not say
branches.when: nothing states what the dependent processes do after expiry

nodes.does: Leave the dependent processes running under the rules that permit it, recording that the artifact expired and that they continue by rule rather than by oversight

nodes.state: EXPIRED; dependent processes continue under rules that permit it
nodes.reEntry: a future action that does require current validity is blocked at its own point rather than by pre-emptively stopping everything

nodes.does: Block only the future actions that require a currently valid document. Everything not requiring current validity continues - one expired certificate stopping an entire relationship is a suspension nobody decided and nobody can find the authority for

nodes.state: EXPIRED; only the actions requiring current validity are blocked
nodes.reEntry: a replacement artifact releases the blocked actions. Actions performed while the document was valid remain historical facts

nodes.on: an expired document whose effect on dependent processes the rules do not define
carries: the expired artifact and every process depending on it
the explicit fact that no blocking or continuation was assumed - guessing either stops work nobody stopped or continues work nobody authorized

guardrails: Expired is not revoked.
Expiration dates are never invented.
Actions performed while the document was valid remain historical facts.
Only processes requiring current validity are affected.
journeys.reusableRule: Document expiry ends future reliance on a time-limited artifact according to its governing rules without rewriting actions completed while it was valid.

journeys.name: Document revocation or withdrawal → stop future reliance → reconcile
journeys.purpose: Withdraw an artifact by an authority's decision, exactly as far as that decision reaches.

entity.scope: the revoked document version and the revocation acting on it
entity.note: The revocation has its own effective scope. Applying it more widely withdraws things the authority did not withdraw.

distinctFrom.because: An amendment replaces a document with a successor that carries the same purpose forward. Revocation withdraws it with nothing behind it - there may be no successor, and the reason is a decision rather than a change of terms.

requires: a revocation or withdrawal by an authority entitled to make it
insufficientAlone: a document expiring, which is time rather than a decision
a successor being issued, which supersedes rather than revokes

nodes.does: Record the revoked version, the authority, the reason and its category, the revocation time, and the revocation's own effective semantics

Record REVOKED, preserving the document and everything about it. A revoked document's history stays available - it is the evidence for everything done while it stood, and deleting it destroys the explanation for actions that were entirely correct at the time
Identify the pending and future processes relying on this document

nodes.asks: What does the revocation's effective scope permit going forward?

branches.label: No future reliance at all
branches.when: the revocation withdraws the document entirely from here on

branches.label: Limited scope, some reliance continues
branches.when: the revocation names a scope narrower than the whole document

nodes.does: Block or revalidate the affected processes, which now have no valid artifact behind them

Apply exactly the scope the revocation names, and nothing wider. A revocation applied more broadly than its own terms withdraws things the authority did not withdraw, and there is no record of who decided that because nobody did

nodes.asks: What does the revocation say about actions already completed?

branches.label: It explicitly reaches them
branches.when: the revocation states a retroactive consequence and the authority for it

branches.label: It says nothing about them
branches.when: the revocation addresses future reliance only

nodes.does: Apply the retroactive consequence the revocation actually states, recording the authority for it. What is applied is what was stated - a revocation that reaches backwards has to say so, and how far

Leave completed actions as they stand. Retroactive invalidity is not inferred - assuming it turns every past action taken under a now-revoked certificate into a problem nobody has decided is a problem, and unwinding them is far harder than not unwinding them

nodes.asks: Is a replacement artifact required?

branches.label: One is required
branches.when: the processes that relied on this still need a valid artifact

branches.label: None
branches.when: nothing further requires an artifact of this kind

nodes.on: a revoked document that still needs replacing
carries: the revoked artifact, its scope and the reason it was withdrawn
the explicit fact that the replacement is a new artifact rather than a reissue of the revoked one

nodes.state: REVOKED; future reliance stopped within the revocation's scope, history preserved
nodes.reEntry: the revocation being itself withdrawn or narrowed is a further authoritative act, recorded on top rather than by clearing this one

guardrails: Revoked is not expired.
A revoked document's history remains available and auditable.
Retroactive consequences are never inferred without explicit authority.
The revocation applies exactly its own stated scope.
journeys.reusableRule: Revocation stops reliance on a document according to the revocation's effective scope while preserving the historical record of the artifact and prior actions.

journeys.name: Document or record conflict → determine authoritative version → reconcile
journeys.purpose: Work out which version actually governs, and explain the conflict rather than deleting it.

entity.scope: the document lineage and every conflicting record claiming to be part of it
entity.note: Every conflicting record is evidence. Deleting one to tidy the state removes the proof of what anybody relied on.

distinctFrom.because: A generic sync conflict asks which record is newer. This asks which version is authoritative, which turns on issuance authority, lineage and effective semantics - and it must additionally establish which version each signature actually binds to, a question recency cannot answer.

journeys.objective: Work out which version actually governs, and explain the conflict rather than deleting it.
eligibility: a material inconsistency - different content under one identifier, an incorrect version distributed, a signature attached to the wrong version, a local copy differing from the authoritative record, several versions claiming current status, or a missing amendment link
no instance of this journey is already open for the the document lineage and every conflicting record claiming to be part of it
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: The newest file is not automatically the authoritative version.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Conflicting evidence is never deleted to fix the state.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Signature validity is checked against the exact version.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Reconciliation preserves lineage and prior use.

value.rule: Every touch runs against a budget fixed when the instance opened; the budget is the plan's own length, and no touch is repeated because nothing could tell whether it arrived.

default.applicableWhen: GLB-24; the graph's own touch count

cooldown.rule: This journey is per the document lineage and every conflicting record claiming to be part of it; a later instance concerns a different the document lineage and every conflicting record claiming to be part of it and no cooldown applies between them.

default.applicableWhen: the entity note: one instance per entity

roles.when: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it

touches.purpose: Redistribute the authoritative version, saying explicitly what changed and which version it replaces.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

guardrails: complaint
message_after_success
unsubscribe

useCases: which version actually governs, with the conflict explained rather than deleted
a non-authoritative version that was distributed, corrected explicitly

requires: a material inconsistency - different content under one identifier, an incorrect version distributed, a signature attached to the wrong version, a local copy differing from the authoritative record, several versions claiming current status, or a missing amendment link
insufficientAlone: two versions that differ by design, such as a draft alongside its issued form
a formatting difference between two renderings of the same version

nodes.does: Collect the document ids, the version ids, the content with its hashes or references, the issuance times, the signature evidence, the effective dates, the lineage, and the authority or source behind each record

nodes.asks: Is the authoritative version deterministically identifiable?

branches.label: It is
branches.when: lineage, issuance authority and effective semantics together single out one version

branches.label: It is not
branches.when: two or more versions have equal claim, or the lineage is broken

nodes.does: Record DOCUMENT_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED and change nothing. The newest file is not automatically the authoritative version - recency is a property of a filesystem and authority is a property of an issuance, and picking the newer one is how a superseded draft becomes the contract

nodes.on: a conflict where the authoritative version cannot be safely determined
carries: every conflicting record with its hash, issuance, signatures, effective dates and lineage
the explicit fact that nothing was deleted, corrected or promoted - the conflict is preserved intact for the decision

nodes.does: Record which version is authoritative and why, preserving every conflicting record alongside it. This is a deterministic resolver applying c.identifiable's own criteria - lineage, issuance authority and effective semantics - never a human judgment call at this step; the resolver having already singled out one version is what makes this action reachable at all, which is why an inability to do so routes to h.review's human decision instead of arriving here. Conflicting evidence is not deleted to tidy the state - it is the only proof the conflict happened, and the only way to work out afterwards what anybody actually relied on

nodes.asks: Is any signature bound to a version other than the authoritative one?

branches.label: One or more are
branches.when: a signature was made against a version that is not authoritative

branches.label: All bind correctly
branches.when: every signature is against the authoritative version

nodes.does: Record that the signature does not bind to the authoritative version, without discarding the signature. It is valid evidence for the version it was made against and for no other, however similar the content of the two looks

nodes.on: signatures that bind to a version other than the authoritative one
carries: the authoritative version and which signatures are missing against it
the explicit fact that the existing signatures stand as evidence about their own versions and are not transferred

nodes.asks: Was a non-authoritative version distributed or acted upon?

branches.label: Distributed, not acted upon
branches.when: a recipient holds the wrong version and has done nothing on it

branches.label: Already used for a business action
branches.when: something was decided, paid, granted or performed on the wrong version

branches.label: Neither
branches.when: the conflict was internal and nothing left the system

nodes.does: Redistribute the authoritative version, saying explicitly what changed and which version it replaces. A silent correction leaves the recipient holding two documents and no idea which one counts, which is worse than the original error

Preserve what was done and under which version it was done. The action happened - what to do about it is a separate question with its own authority, and rewriting the record to show the right version leaves an effect with no cause

nodes.on: a business action taken on a non-authoritative document version
carries: what was done, under which version, and what the authoritative version says instead - conflict_id stands in for REM-157's obligation_id
the explicit fact that the history is preserved intact - the remedy addresses the consequence rather than the record
a fresh issue_id, minted at this handoff and deterministically derived from conflict_id - DOC-220 has no issue concept of its own, so REM-157's instance is opened here rather than carried

nodes.state: authoritative version established; conflicting records preserved and explained
nodes.reEntry: a further inconsistency in this lineage is assessed with this reconciliation as part of its evidence, which is why none of it was deleted

guardrails: The newest file is not automatically the authoritative version.
Conflicting evidence is never deleted to fix the state.
Signature validity is checked against the exact version.
Reconciliation preserves lineage and prior use.
journeys.reusableRule: Document reconciliation restores a single authoritative version lineage by explaining conflicts rather than overwriting or deleting inconvenient historical records.

journeys.name: Document effective → entitlement active → first use or dormant
journeys.purpose: Tell the holder that what they signed has actually started, and what it now lets them do, at the moment it becomes true rather than the moment they signed.

entity.scope: the effective document version and the entitlement it confers on its holder
entity.note: One effective version, one instance. A renewal or a superseding version taking effect is its own instance and inherits nothing from this one.

distinctFrom.because: DOC-216 establishes whether and when the document takes effect and revalidates it at that moment. This journey starts only once that record exists, and it decides nothing about effectiveness itself.

ACC-263 runs a claim window on a granted capability that lapses if unused. Here nothing lapses for want of use - the document is in force either way, and dormancy is an observation rather than a loss.

journeys.objective: Tell the holder that what they signed has actually started, and what it now lets them do, at the moment it becomes true rather than the moment they signed.
eligibility: an authoritative record that this version is in force, revalidated at its effective moment
the entitlement it confers, expressed as something the holder can act on
a named holder with a permitted route to them
no instance of this journey is already open for the the effective document version and the entitlement it confers on its holder

no DOC-220 conflict review is open for this document's lineage - a version review can retroactively make what looked authoritative not authoritative, and this journey does not tell a holder an entitlement is active while that question is still open
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Signed is not effective, and only the effective record starts this.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: The entitlement is named as what the holder can do, never as what the document says.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: An entitlement with nothing to exercise is never chased for use.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: One reminder, never two. The entitlement stands whether or not anybody takes it up.

suppressions.label: CANONICAL_RULE
suppressions.text: Dormant and no-longer-in-force are recorded as different outcomes - one is about the holder, the other is about the document.

value.rule: Every touch runs against a budget fixed when the instance opened; the budget is the plan's own length, and no touch is repeated because nothing could tell whether it arrived.

default.applicableWhen: GLB-24; the graph's own touch count

cooldown.rule: This journey is per the effective document version and the entitlement it confers on its holder; a later instance concerns a different the effective document version and the entitlement it confers on its holder and no cooldown applies between them.

default.applicableWhen: the entity note: one instance per entity

roles.when: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it
the person is active in the product and the action is taken there

touches.purpose: Say the document is in force, from when, and name the single first thing the entitlement now lets them do.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: Say the document is in force and what it covers, and name the moment at which it would matter rather than an action to take now.
touches.label: CANONICAL_RULE

touches.purpose: Send one reminder naming what is in force and the same single first action, not a second explanation of the document.
touches.label: RECOMMENDED_DEFAULT

guardrails: complaint
message_after_success
unsubscribe

useCases: the holder told what they signed has started and what it lets them do, when it becomes true
one reminder of the first action, then dormancy recorded

requires: an authoritative record that this version is in force, revalidated at its effective moment
the entitlement it confers, expressed as something the holder can act on
a named holder with a permitted route to them
insufficientAlone: a complete set of signatures
a scheduled effective date that has not been revalidated
a condition that has not yet resolved

nodes.asks: Is this entitlement exercised, or held?

branches.label: Exercised
branches.when: the entitlement is taken up by an action the holder performs - a claim, a booking, an access, a draw-down

branches.label: Held
branches.when: the entitlement is a standing protection or permission with nothing to do unless something happens

nodes.does: Say the document is in force, from when, and name the single first thing the entitlement now lets them do. The gap between signing and taking effect is where holders quietly conclude that nothing happened

Say the document is in force and what it covers, and name the moment at which it would matter rather than an action to take now. An entitlement that only applies when something goes wrong is otherwise read as inactive until it is needed

nodes.state: in force, nothing for the holder to exercise
